name: Empires and Civilisations Entire
description: Fifty subjects — empires, dynasties, civilisations and whole lives from every era and every inhabited continent — each with twenty materially distinct episode slots, for a channel that tells the entire story of one civilisation or one person from beginning to end in a single sitting.

his name on a statue base, the step pyramid complex itself, and the much later cult and medical texts
his surviving treatises including one recovered from a scraped manuscript, and the siege accounts of his enemies
her students' letters, the commentaries attributed to her circle, and the church historians' conflicting accounts
his surviving treatises and their Latin translations, the library's records, and the astronomical tables
his own autobiography continued by a student, the surviving medical and philosophical works, and their translation record
his enormous case compendium, the hospital records, and the citations of him by later physicians
the buildings themselves and their inscriptions, the endowment deeds, the construction account books, and his dictated memoir
the cathedral works records and payments, the surviving machinery drawings, and the contemporary biographies
the notebooks in mirror writing, the commission contracts and lawsuits, and the surviving and lost works record
his own published works and letters, the trial documents, the surviving telescopes, and the observation notebooks
the standard history's account, the surviving treatises and poems, and the reconstruction of his instruments
his own illustrated treatise, the court records of the dispute, and the modern reconstructions from that book
the text itself, the commentaries that unpack it, and the later astronomical tables that depend on it
his optical treatise and its Latin translation, the biographical accounts, and the citations by later opticians
the treatise itself, the buildings that match its prescriptions, and the manuscript rediscovery record
her own works and letters, the convent records, the canonisation inquiry, and the surviving musical manuscripts
his own printed and unprinted works, the town council records that dismissed him, and the mining medicine tradition
his own illustrated anatomy, the university records, the printing house documents, and the court correspondence
the star catalogue itself, the observatory excavation, the college records, and the court chronicles
his own manuscript and the printed book, the chapter records of his day job, and the correspondence with his one advocate
exclusions: No invented quotations, invented private thoughts, invented letters, or invented scenes; describe only what the record supports and say plainly where it stops.
No living people and nobody within living memory: every subject is a civilisation long gone or a person long dead, and no descendant, claimant, or present-day political figure is named.
No hooks, cliffhangers, countdowns, teasers, or alarm of any kind, at the opening of an era section or anywhere inside it.
No dwelling on massacre, torture, execution, famine death, or sexual violence; state briefly that it happened and give the aftermath the time instead.
Never split the arc or point forward to a later episode: the whole story is told once, in order, in this one recording.
No verdict passed on a civilisation or a person as glorious or wicked, no moralising, and no direct address urging the listener to do anything.
No modern political analogy, no claim about a present-day state, people, religion, or party, and no partisan framing of a contested national history.
No claim that a civilisation was destined to rise or doomed to fall, and no explanation of a collapse by the character of a people.
prompt_context: Each episode is the entire story of one civilisation, one empire, one dynasty, or one life, told once, in order, from its beginning to its end, for a listener already drifting toward sleep. Open inside the beginning — the first settlement, the first ruler, the birth — and move forward at one steady pace to the end, without a hook, a question, or a promise. Divide the arc into eras of roughly even length and let each one resolve where it stops, so that a listener who wakes in the middle hears a continuous story and a listener who drifts off loses nothing. Explain how the thing actually worked — how the fields were watered, how the taxes were counted, who was allowed into which room, what a campaign cost to feed, what an oath required, how a succession was decided — and let the explanation itself be the interest. Favour material and administrative detail over incident: the weight of a crown, the tonnage of a grain fleet, the price of a horse, the depth of a canal, the wording of a charter. Where a battle, a conquest, an execution, a plague, or a collapse belongs to the arc, describe it plainly and briefly and give the aftermath more time than the act. Name historical figures as the record names them, invent nobody, and quote nothing that was not written down. Say plainly when a century is thinly attested, when the only surviving account was written by the winner, and when scholars still disagree. Keep sentences unhurried and mostly declarative, and let paragraphs settle rather than accelerate. End each era on a still image — a silted harbour, an emptied hall, a worn coin, a boundary stone in a field — and end the episode on what the place or the person left behind.

idea_axes.label: Whole-arc lens
values: origins, founding and the first century
expansion, conquest and the widest extent
government, taxation and the machinery of rule
cities, building and the shape of daily life
trade, money and what the whole thing ran on
religion, ritual and the sacred order
writing, learning and how the record was kept
war, frontier and the cost of holding ground
crisis, division and the long decline
ending, aftermath and what was inherited

tuples.episode_object: Rome itself, from a herding village on the Tiber to an empire that outlived its own capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the Tiber crossing, Italy and the whole Mediterranean across twelve centuries
tuples.mechanism: the extension of citizenship as an instrument of conquest, which turned absorbed enemies into taxpayers and soldiers instead of subjects to be garrisoned
tuples.evidence_lens: annalistic histories written centuries after the events, read against excavated street levels, dated inscriptions and coin hoards

tuples.episode_object: the Roman Republic, from the expulsion of the kings to the last civil war
tuples.time_place_scope: the city, Italy and the provinces across roughly five hundred years
tuples.mechanism: the annual magistracy, which made supreme power survivable by making it temporary, and stopped working the moment armies outlasted the offices that raised them
tuples.evidence_lens: senatorial histories and speeches read against surviving laws, the consular lists and the archaeology of army camps

tuples.episode_object: the Roman Empire under the emperors, from the first princeps to the last western claimant
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole Mediterranean rim and the northern frontiers across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: the professional standing army as the state's largest employer, which secured the frontier and then priced the treasury out of everything else
tuples.evidence_lens: imperial biographies of uncertain reliability set beside papyrus tax registers, milestones and frontier fort excavation

tuples.episode_object: the Etruscans, from tomb-building city leagues to a language nobody spoke
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the Arno and the Tiber across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: cultural absorption by a neighbour, in which a people is not destroyed but slowly recorded in somebody else's language until the original stops being written
tuples.evidence_lens: painted chamber tombs, bronze work and inscriptions read against the hostile accounts of their conquerors

tuples.episode_object: the Samnites, from mountain confederation to the last Italian rising
tuples.time_place_scope: the central Apennines and the Campanian plain across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a federal league of mountain communities, powerful in defence and unable to convert repeated tactical victory into a durable peace
tuples.evidence_lens: hilltop sanctuary excavation and Oscan inscriptions weighed against a conquest narrative written by the winner

tuples.episode_object: Magna Graecia, from the first colonists in the west to Greek Italy under Rome
tuples.time_place_scope: the coasts of southern Italy and the toe of the peninsula across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: colonial foundation as a release valve for crowded home cities, which reproduced the parent quarrels along with the parent institutions
tuples.evidence_lens: colony foundation dates in later chronicles checked against pottery sequences and the earliest temple platforms

tuples.episode_object: Roman Britain, from the first landing to the last coin that reached the island
tuples.time_place_scope: the island south of the northern walls across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: an occupied province whose towns were paid for by the army's supply chain and emptied when it left
tuples.evidence_lens: villa and fort excavation, writing tablets from a frontier garrison, and the abrupt end of the coin sequence

tuples.episode_object: Roman Gaul, from a conquered patchwork of peoples to a Latin-speaking country
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the Rhine, the Alps and the ocean across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: elite co-option, in which the sons of defeated chieftains were educated into the conquering system and became its magistrates
tuples.evidence_lens: a general's own campaign account read against native oppidum excavation, altars, and the careers recorded on tombstones

tuples.episode_object: Roman Spain, from a landing against Carthage to the peninsula that supplied emperors
tuples.time_place_scope: the Iberian peninsula and its mining districts across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: extractive provincial economics, where silver and lead paid for the conquest that made the mines accessible in the first place
tuples.evidence_lens: mining district archaeology, bronze municipal charters, and shipwreck cargoes of stamped ingots

tuples.episode_object: Roman North Africa, from a burnt rival to the granary of an empire
tuples.time_place_scope: the coast and the high plains from the Gulf of Sidra to the ocean across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: monoculture for export, which made a province indispensable and left it defenceless once the fleet that carried the grain was lost
tuples.evidence_lens: olive and grain estate remains, mosaic floors, city charters and the accounts of a later invasion

tuples.episode_object: Roman Egypt, from a queen's death to an unreachable frontier province
tuples.time_place_scope: the Nile valley, the delta and the eastern desert roads across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: direct imperial ownership of a province, run as an estate rather than governed as a country, with the harvest counted before it was cut
tuples.evidence_lens: papyrus tax rolls, census returns and private letters read against temple building and desert quarry records

tuples.episode_object: Roman Dacia, from a conquered mountain kingdom to the province that was given up
tuples.time_place_scope: the Carpathian arc and the Transylvanian gold country across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a salient held beyond a defensible river line, worth its gold until the cost of the garrison exceeded the yield
tuples.evidence_lens: a triumphal column read as propaganda, wax tablets from the mining settlements, and the dated withdrawal of the legions

tuples.episode_object: Roman Judaea, from a client kingdom to a province renamed after a revolt
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Levant, its hill country and its coastal ports across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: indirect rule through a client dynasty, and what follows when the client fails and the imperial power governs a religious centre directly
tuples.evidence_lens: a participant historian writing for the conquerors, weighed against siege archaeology, coin issues and rabbinic tradition

tuples.episode_object: Palmyra, from a caravan oasis to a ruin remembered for one queen
tuples.time_place_scope: the Syrian steppe between the Euphrates and the Mediterranean across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: the profit and the fragility of a monopoly on one desert route, which enriches a middle city until either end of the road changes hands
tuples.evidence_lens: bilingual tariff inscriptions, tower tomb sculpture and the campaign accounts of the empire that ended it

tuples.episode_object: Pompeii and Herculaneum, from Oscan towns to the day they stopped and what came after
tuples.time_place_scope: the bay beneath the mountain, from the earliest settlement to the modern excavation
tuples.mechanism: catastrophic preservation, in which a disaster destroys a place and simultaneously makes it the best-documented ordinary town of its age
tuples.evidence_lens: the stratified ash deposit itself, painted shop signs and graffiti, and two and a half centuries of excavation records

tuples.episode_object: Ostia, from a salt works at the river mouth to a silted-up ghost of a port
tuples.time_place_scope: the Tiber mouth and its harbour basins across nine centuries
tuples.mechanism: a capital city's dependence on one port, and the slow strangulation of that port by the river's own silt
tuples.evidence_lens: warehouse and apartment block excavation, guild mosaics, and the shifting coastline read from cores

tuples.episode_object: the Rhine and upper Danube frontier, from conquest to the last garrison
tuples.time_place_scope: the river line and the land between the two rivers across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a frontier defined by a river and a road rather than a wall, which functioned as a customs and diplomacy line more than a barrier
tuples.evidence_lens: fort and watchtower sequences, discharge diplomas, and the dated abandonment of the land between the rivers

tuples.episode_object: Roman Pannonia, from a conquered river country to the corridor everyone marched through
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Danube plain and its crossings across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a militarised transit province, whose garrisons made emperors precisely because everything moving between east and west had to pass them
tuples.evidence_lens: legionary fortress excavation, tombstones of transferred soldiers, and the coin evidence of usurpation

tuples.episode_object: Roman Sicily, from a contested island to the first province
tuples.time_place_scope: the island, its grain plains and its ports across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: the invention of provincial administration itself, worked out on one island and then applied everywhere
tuples.evidence_lens: a prosecution speech against a governor, grain tithe records, and the great late villa mosaics

tuples.episode_object: Roman Asia, from inherited kingdom to a province of five hundred cities
tuples.time_place_scope: the western peninsula of Anatolia and its river valleys across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a province acquired by bequest rather than war, and taxed by contractors until the contracting itself became the crisis
tuples.evidence_lens: civic building inscriptions, tax farming records, and the letters of governors to the emperor

tuples.episode_object: the eastern Roman empire, from a new capital on the Bosporus to the last day of the walls
tuples.time_place_scope: the city on the straits and its shrinking hinterland across eleven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a state built around one fortified capital and a fleet, which could lose every province and continue, until the capital itself could be taken
tuples.evidence_lens: court histories written by insiders, seals and lead bulls, and the archaeology of the land walls

tuples.episode_object: Constantinople itself, from a Greek colony on a headland to a city renamed twice
tuples.time_place_scope: the promontory between two seas across twenty-two centuries
tuples.mechanism: the geography of a chokepoint, which made one headland worth any expense to hold and any expense to take
tuples.evidence_lens: the successive wall circuits, harbour excavations and the ceremonial books of the imperial palace

tuples.episode_object: the Sasanian empire's Roman wars, told as the whole life of a rivalry
tuples.time_place_scope: the Mesopotamian plain and the Armenian highlands across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a long frontier war between two states of comparable strength, which exhausted both and left the ground to a third
tuples.evidence_lens: campaign narratives from both sides, frontier fortress remains, and the coin sequences of both treasuries

tuples.episode_object: Byzantine Anatolia, from the granary of the empire to a lost heartland
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau and its passes across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: the theme system, which paid soldiers in land instead of coin and thereby traded central control for a permanent standing defence
tuples.evidence_lens: military manuals, seals of provincial officials, and the abandonment sequence of plateau settlements

tuples.episode_object: Byzantine Italy, from reconquest to the last exarch
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula, its ports and the exarchate around the Adriatic marshes across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: an overstretched reconquest, held long enough to ruin the country and not long enough to keep it
tuples.evidence_lens: mosaics and church foundations, papyrus deeds, and the letters of bishops negotiating with two powers at once

tuples.episode_object: Ravenna, from a marsh port to a capital nobody could reach
tuples.time_place_scope: the lagoon and its harbour across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: defensibility bought at the price of relevance, as a court hidden behind marshes lost touch with the country it governed
tuples.evidence_lens: surviving mosaic programmes, the silted harbour, and legal documents preserved on papyrus

tuples.episode_object: Byzantine Greece, from late antique cities to a country of fortified hills
tuples.time_place_scope: the mainland, the Peloponnese and the islands across nine centuries
tuples.mechanism: the abandonment of open cities for defensible heights, a physical record of what centuries of raiding does to settlement
tuples.evidence_lens: the shift in settlement archaeology, monastic charters, and pilgrim descriptions

tuples.episode_object: Cappadocia and its rock towns, from Roman province to carved refuge
tuples.time_place_scope: the volcanic tableland of central Anatolia across twelve centuries
tuples.mechanism: the use of soft stone as building material and defence together, so that a whole society could go underground during a raiding season
tuples.evidence_lens: carved churches and their painting phases, underground complex surveys, and monastic rules

tuples.episode_object: Byzantine Armenia and the highland principalities, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the mountains between the Black Sea and Lake Van across nine centuries
tuples.mechanism: buffer politics, in which small mountain lordships survive by selling loyalty alternately to two empires and are destroyed when only one remains
tuples.evidence_lens: church architecture and its inscriptions, princely genealogies, and diplomatic correspondence from both empires

tuples.episode_object: the Bulgarian empires, from a steppe arrival to a province of an older empire
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Danube, the Balkan range and the Black Sea coast across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: the conversion of a mobile conquering elite into a settled Christian monarchy, and how quickly that made it legible to its enemies
tuples.evidence_lens: rock inscriptions, capital city excavation, and the annals of the empire it fought

tuples.episode_object: the Serbian medieval kingdom, from mountain principalities to an empire and its end
tuples.time_place_scope: the Morava and Vardar valleys and the Adriatic hinterland across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: silver mining wealth arriving suddenly in a small kingdom, funding an empire that outgrew its own tax base within one reign
tuples.evidence_lens: royal charters, monastery frescoes with donor portraits, and mining town records

tuples.episode_object: the Byzantine church and its schism, told as one long institutional life
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Mediterranean and its patriarchal sees across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: the slow divergence of two churches through language, liturgy and jurisdiction rather than through any single quarrel
tuples.evidence_lens: conciliar acts, liturgical manuscripts, and correspondence between the sees

tuples.episode_object: Thessalonica, from a Macedonian foundation to a great second city
tuples.time_place_scope: the head of the gulf and the road across the Balkans, across twenty-three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a second city on a trunk road, always rich, always the first prize after the capital, and never able to govern itself
tuples.evidence_lens: the road milestones, city wall phases, church foundations, and accounts of successive sieges

tuples.episode_object: Trebizond, from a Black Sea colony to the last Greek state
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Black Sea shore and its mountain passes across nineteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: the survival of a splinter state behind a mountain wall, living on transit trade for two centuries after the parent empire fell
tuples.evidence_lens: port records, dynastic chronicles, and the fortifications of the coastal strip

tuples.episode_object: the Latin empire and the Frankish states in Greece, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Aegean, the Peloponnese and the islands across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: conquest by a crusading army that arrived for somewhere else, and the fragile feudal patchwork such an accident leaves behind
tuples.evidence_lens: feudal registers, castle building phases, and the chronicles written by both the settlers and the dispossessed

tuples.episode_object: the Venetian Aegean, from crusade spoils to the last island fortress
tuples.time_place_scope: the islands and harbours between the Adriatic and Crete across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a maritime empire of harbours rather than territories, which needed only the coast and could be dismantled one port at a time
tuples.evidence_lens: the republic's own senate minutes, harbour fortress remains, and the notarial records of island colonies

tuples.episode_object: Byzantine Sicily and southern Italy, from Greek province to Norman kingdom
tuples.time_place_scope: the island and the southern peninsula across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: the persistence of a language and a rite under three successive conquests, and the point at which administration finally changed it
tuples.evidence_lens: Greek monastic charters, church dedications, and the administrative records of the Norman successors

tuples.episode_object: the Byzantine economy, told as the whole life of one coinage
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Mediterranean and its mints across eleven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a gold coin held stable for seven centuries as an instrument of state credibility, and what its debasement announced about everything else
tuples.evidence_lens: hoard analysis, mint marks, weight studies, and the commercial handbooks of foreign merchants

tuples.episode_object: the Fourth Crusade and its aftermath, told from beginning to end
tuples.time_place_scope: the Adriatic, the Aegean and the capital across two generations
tuples.mechanism: the capture of a state by a debt, in which a transport contract that could not be paid redirected an army onto its own creditor's rival
tuples.evidence_lens: participant accounts from both sides, the treaty of partition, and the dispersal record of looted objects

tuples.episode_object: the last two centuries of the empire, from restoration to the final siege
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital, the Aegean coast and the Peloponnese across two hundred years
tuples.mechanism: a state reduced to a capital and a diplomacy, negotiating between larger neighbours until neither needed it any more
tuples.evidence_lens: the memoirs of courtiers, union negotiations, and the siege accounts of both defenders and besiegers

tuples.episode_object: the Greeks, from the collapse of the palaces to the death of the last Hellenistic queen
tuples.time_place_scope: the Aegean, the wider Mediterranean and the lands to the east across thirteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a civilisation organised as hundreds of separate small states, which produced its brilliance and guaranteed it could never defend itself as one
tuples.evidence_lens: epic poetry read as memory rather than record, alongside inscriptions, excavated sanctuaries and later histories

tuples.episode_object: Athens, from a hill fort to a university town under foreign rule
tuples.time_place_scope: Attica, its silver hills and its port across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a citizen assembly funded by a silver strike and a naval empire, which lasted precisely as long as the fleet did
tuples.evidence_lens: assembly decrees cut in stone, tribute lists, comic drama, and the excavation of the civic centre

tuples.episode_object: Sparta, from a valley of villages to a tourist attraction
tuples.time_place_scope: the Eurotas valley and the country it held down across twelve centuries
tuples.mechanism: a military caste sustained by a subjugated farming population, which fixed its manpower ceiling and made every casualty irreplaceable
tuples.evidence_lens: hostile and admiring outsiders in equal measure, checked against sanctuary dedications and the archaeology of the valley

tuples.episode_object: Corinth, from an isthmus town to a Roman colony and back to a city
tuples.time_place_scope: the isthmus and its two harbours across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: the tax on a shortcut, in which a city grows rich by charging for the two hundred metres of land between two seas
tuples.evidence_lens: harbour and canal-attempt archaeology, pottery distribution, and the accounts of its destruction and refoundation

tuples.episode_object: Thebes and Boeotia, from a legendary citadel to a razed city
tuples.time_place_scope: the Boeotian plain and its lakes across ten centuries
tuples.mechanism: a federal league of neighbouring cities, briefly the strongest power in Greece, and unable to survive the death of the two men who built it
tuples.evidence_lens: federal coinage, the Theban dead of one battlefield, and the accounts of allies and enemies

tuples.episode_object: Macedon, from a highland kingdom to the empire it left behind
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plains, the Balkan interior and everything conquered eastward across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom that combined a highland army with lowland money and then spent both on a march it could not administer
tuples.evidence_lens: court histories written long afterwards, royal tomb finds, and the coin evidence of the successor kingdoms

tuples.episode_object: the Ionian cities of Asia Minor, told from foundation to ruin
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Aegean coast and its river valleys across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: coastal cities caught between a sea empire and a land empire, prosperous while both wanted them and destroyed when one won
tuples.evidence_lens: temple building sequences, tyrant coinages, and the histories written by their own citizens

tuples.episode_object: Miletus, from a harbour city to a plain with a theatre in it
tuples.time_place_scope: the mouth of a silting river across sixteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: the burial of a port by its own hinterland's soil, the slowest possible way for a great city to end
tuples.evidence_lens: harbour sediment cores, the grid plan itself, and the record of colonies the city founded

tuples.episode_object: Delphi, from a spring on a hillside to an abandoned sanctuary
tuples.time_place_scope: the mountainside above the gulf across thirteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: the political usefulness of a neutral oracle, funded by rival states precisely because it belonged to none of them
tuples.evidence_lens: treasury buildings and their dedications, consultation records, and the accounts of successive plunderings

tuples.episode_object: Olympia and the games, told as one long institutional life
tuples.time_place_scope: the river plain in the western Peloponnese across twelve centuries
tuples.mechanism: a festival truce that outlasted every state that observed it, and the sponsorship that eventually replaced the religion
tuples.evidence_lens: victor lists, statue bases, workshop excavation, and the decrees that finally closed the sanctuary

tuples.episode_object: Crete after the palaces, from Dorian cities to the last Venetian fortress
tuples.time_place_scope: the island, its harbours and its mountains across three thousand years
tuples.mechanism: an island large enough to feed itself and too small to defend itself, passed between every sea power in turn
tuples.evidence_lens: law codes cut in stone, harbour fortifications, and the successive administrative archives of its rulers

tuples.episode_object: Rhodes, from three cities to a fortified island order
tuples.time_place_scope: the island and the Anatolian coast opposite across twenty-five centuries
tuples.mechanism: maritime law and a good harbour as a small state's entire foreign policy, respected while the sea trade lasted
tuples.evidence_lens: sea law fragments quoted by later jurists, harbour works, and the siege records of two great sieges

tuples.episode_object: Syracuse, from a colony to the city Rome had to besiege
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Sicilian coast and its plain across ten centuries
tuples.mechanism: the tyrant-financed great city, magnificent and structurally unstable, whose brilliance depended on one man's revenue at a time
tuples.evidence_lens: fortification circuits, tyrant coin issues, and the accounts of the sieges written by their besiegers

tuples.episode_object: Massalia and the Greek west, from a trading post to a Roman city
tuples.time_place_scope: the Gulf of Lion and the river routes inland across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a trading colony that survived by choosing the winner in every regional war, until the one time it chose wrong
tuples.evidence_lens: amphora distribution inland, the colony foundation traditions, and the treaty records with Rome

tuples.episode_object: the Black Sea Greek cities, told from foundation to abandonment
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern and southern shores of the Black Sea across twelve centuries
tuples.mechanism: colonies dependent on a grain trade with the steppe, which prospered or emptied exactly as the steppe politics allowed
tuples.evidence_lens: grain export inscriptions, burial goods mixing Greek and steppe forms, and the accounts of exiled writers

tuples.episode_object: the Seleucid empire, from a general's share to a rump in Syria
tuples.time_place_scope: everything between the Aegean and the Indus across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: an empire of founded cities strung along roads, held together by garrisons and unable to survive a single generation of civil war
tuples.evidence_lens: royal foundation inscriptions, cuneiform astronomical diaries, and the coin sequences of rival claimants

tuples.episode_object: Ptolemaic Egypt, from a stolen body to a queen's death
tuples.time_place_scope: the Nile valley, Alexandria and the eastern Mediterranean across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a foreign dynasty ruling through an existing bureaucracy in a language most subjects did not read, and the cost of that translation
tuples.evidence_lens: papyrus administration, bilingual decrees, and the Alexandrian court histories

tuples.episode_object: Alexandria, from a survey line on a beach to a diminished port
tuples.time_place_scope: the western delta shore and its harbours across twenty-three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the deliberate foundation of a capital as an instrument of policy, and what happens to a designed city when the policy ends
tuples.evidence_lens: harbour archaeology now underwater, library and museum references, and the papyrus record of its quarters

tuples.episode_object: the Greek kingdoms of Bactria and India, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Oxus country and the northwest of the subcontinent across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a settler kingdom cut off from its origin, which survived by becoming local and then vanished from the written record entirely
tuples.evidence_lens: bilingual coinage as almost the only source, city excavation on the Oxus, and Indian textual references

tuples.episode_object: the Hellenistic world's end, told as one long absorption
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Mediterranean and the Near East across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: the piecemeal purchase and annexation of exhausted kingdoms, in which very little was conquered and almost everything was inherited
tuples.evidence_lens: treaty texts, royal wills, and the provincial reorganisation records of the absorbing power

tuples.episode_object: the Achaemenid empire, from a vassal kingdom to a burnt palace
tuples.time_place_scope: the Iranian plateau and everything from the Aegean to the Indus across two and a quarter centuries
tuples.mechanism: government by satrapy and road, in which a small ruling people held an enormous empire by leaving local systems intact and taxing them
tuples.evidence_lens: royal inscriptions in three languages, fortification tablets from the treasury, and the hostile histories of one province

tuples.episode_object: the Medes, from a highland confederation to a swallowed kingdom
tuples.time_place_scope: the Zagros mountains and the northern plateau across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a tribal confederation that inherits an empire's wreckage and cannot institutionalise fast enough to keep it
tuples.evidence_lens: Assyrian records of their neighbours, later Greek narrative, and the excavation of highland fortress sites

tuples.episode_object: Elam, from the earliest cities of the plain to a name in a royal titulary
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain east of the Tigris and the mountains behind it across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a lowland and highland state permanently paired with Mesopotamia, borrowing its writing and outliving several of its empires
tuples.evidence_lens: its own untranslated language in administrative texts, temple excavation, and the annals of its neighbours

tuples.episode_object: the Parthian empire, from a nomad takeover to a dynastic collapse
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau, Mesopotamia and the trade roads across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a feudal empire of great houses under a nominal king, resilient against invasion and permanently vulnerable to its own nobility
tuples.evidence_lens: coin portrait sequences, parchment deeds from caravan cities, and the campaign accounts of its western enemy

tuples.episode_object: the Sasanian empire, from a rebellion in the south to the last king in flight
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau, Mesopotamia and the eastern frontier across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: state religion and centralised bureaucracy imposed on a feudal inheritance, powerful and brittle in exactly the ways that combination predicts
tuples.evidence_lens: rock reliefs and their inscriptions, seal archives, the law book, and the accounts of two invasions

tuples.episode_object: Persepolis, from a terrace on a plain to a name for a ruin
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain in the southern highlands across twenty-five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a ceremonial capital used a few weeks a year, which reveals what a state wanted to show rather than how it worked
tuples.evidence_lens: the audience hall reliefs, the archived clay tablets from its treasury, and the burn layer itself

tuples.episode_object: Zoroastrianism, told as the whole life of a religion
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau, the Indian coast and the diaspora across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a state religion that survived the loss of the state by becoming a minority in two countries, one of them not its own
tuples.evidence_lens: liturgical texts of very uncertain date, fire temple archaeology, and the legal position of the community under later rulers

tuples.episode_object: the Persian Gulf trade world, from Dilmun to the pearling fleets
tuples.time_place_scope: the gulf shores, its islands and the sea routes to India across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: an entrepot economy resting on two commodities and a monsoon calendar, prosperous exactly as long as the route mattered
tuples.evidence_lens: cuneiform trade records, island burial mounds, and the port customs registers of later empires

tuples.episode_object: the Achaemenid road system, told as the whole life of one infrastructure
tuples.time_place_scope: the roads from the Aegean coast to the plateau capitals across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the relay post as a technology of empire, which made a message faster than an army and therefore made rebellion harder
tuples.evidence_lens: way station excavation, travel ration tablets, and the descriptions of foreign travellers

tuples.episode_object: Bactria and the Oxus country before the Greeks, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the upper Oxus, its irrigated oases and the mountains across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: irrigated oasis agriculture supporting dense settlement in a dry country, and the total dependence of that settlement on canal maintenance
tuples.evidence_lens: walled oasis site surveys, canal traces from the air, and the administrative records of successive empires

tuples.episode_object: Sogdiana and the Sogdian merchants, told from first cities to last colony
tuples.time_place_scope: the Zarafshan valley and the roads to China across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a merchant diaspora that carried goods, script and religion along one route and disappeared when the route was cut
tuples.evidence_lens: letters abandoned in a watchtower, colony records in Chinese archives, and wall paintings in the home cities

tuples.episode_object: Armenia between the empires, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland plateau around Lake Van and Ararat across twenty-five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a highland country that adopted a distinct alphabet and church early, and used both to remain itself under every neighbour
tuples.evidence_lens: an invented alphabet and its earliest manuscripts, church building phases, and the treaties that partitioned the country

tuples.episode_object: Urartu, from a highland kingdom to a name recovered from inscriptions
tuples.time_place_scope: the mountains around three lakes across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: fortress and canal building as state policy, which made a mountain kingdom agriculturally viable and archaeologically visible
tuples.evidence_lens: citadel excavation, cuneiform building inscriptions, and the campaign annals of its southern enemy

tuples.episode_object: the Kushan empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country from the Oxus to the Ganges plain across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a nomad dynasty that became the hinge of continental trade, minting in several traditions at once to be legible to all its customers
tuples.evidence_lens: multilingual coinage, monastery and stupa foundations, and the dating disputes that still surround its kings

tuples.episode_object: the Hephthalites and the Hunnic states of Iran, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern plateau, the Oxus and the northwest of India across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a steppe power that ruled settled provinces without settling, leaving little record beyond the damage it did to others
tuples.evidence_lens: coin overstrikes on earlier issues, the accounts of two settled empires, and the destruction layers of monasteries

tuples.episode_object: the Safavid empire, from a Sufi order to a fallen capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau, the Caucasus and Mesopotamia across two and a quarter centuries
tuples.mechanism: the conversion of a religious brotherhood into a dynasty, and the state's later struggle to control the clergy it had created
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicles of the court, European embassy reports, endowment deeds, and the surviving building programme of the capital

tuples.episode_object: Isfahan, told from provincial town to imperial capital and after
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau oasis on the river across twenty centuries
tuples.mechanism: a capital built to a single plan in one reign, and the fate of such a city when the dynasty that designed it ends
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving square and its buildings, endowment documents, and travellers' descriptions before and after the siege

tuples.episode_object: the Afsharid and Zand interlude, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau, the eastern frontier and the gulf across seventy years
tuples.mechanism: a conqueror's state with no institution behind it, which cannot survive the conqueror, and the brief decent government that follows exhaustion
tuples.evidence_lens: court chronicles, mint output, and the correspondence of foreign trading companies

tuples.episode_object: the Qajar century and a half, told from a tribal claim to a constitution
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau, the Caucasus, the gulf and the Russian and British frontiers across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a weak central state financed by selling concessions, and the political movement that grew out of resenting them
tuples.evidence_lens: treaties and concession documents, the earliest photography, and the newspapers of the constitutional period

tuples.episode_object: Iranian Zoroastrian and Jewish communities, told as two long lives
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau cities and their quarters across two and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: the legal category of the protected minority, which guaranteed survival and permanent subordination in the same clause
tuples.evidence_lens: community endowment records, poll tax registers, and the internal legal writings of both communities

tuples.episode_object: Sumer, from the first cities to a language nobody spoke and everybody copied
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern alluvium between the two rivers across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: irrigation agriculture requiring collective labour, which produced the surplus, the accounting and therefore the writing that defines a city
tuples.evidence_lens: administrative tablets in enormous quantity, temple and city mound excavation, and later scribal copies

tuples.episode_object: Uruk, from a village cluster to the largest city on earth and then a ruin
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern floodplain across five millennia
tuples.mechanism: urban primacy, in which one city out-grows every neighbour, invents the tools to run itself, and exports them
tuples.evidence_lens: the earliest writing tablets, the city wall circuit, and the stratigraphy of successive rebuildings

tuples.episode_object: Akkad, from a usurper's city to an empire nobody can find
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle and southern floodplain across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: the first territorial empire, held by garrisons and a standing army and undone by drought and by the provinces it never integrated
tuples.evidence_lens: royal inscriptions copied by later scribes, victory monuments, and the climate record from cores

tuples.episode_object: Ur and its third dynasty, told from foundation to abandonment
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern floodplain near the old coastline across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a bureaucratic state that recorded everything, whose completeness of accounting is exactly why its collapse is so visible
tuples.evidence_lens: tens of thousands of dated administrative tablets, royal tombs, and the lament literature written afterwards

tuples.episode_object: Babylon, from a small town on a canal to a ruin in an empty plain
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle floodplain across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a city that mattered as an idea long after it mattered as a power, kept alive by whichever empire wanted its prestige
tuples.evidence_lens: the law stele, the excavated processional way, astronomical diaries, and the descriptions of foreign visitors

tuples.episode_object: the Old Babylonian kingdom and its law, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Euphrates and the floodplain across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: codified law as royal advertisement rather than working statute, and what the actual court records show instead
tuples.evidence_lens: the famous stele read against thousands of ordinary contracts and verdicts from the same courts

tuples.episode_object: Assyria, from a trading town to the empire that fell in a generation
tuples.time_place_scope: the upper Tigris, the Levant and Egypt at its widest across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: deportation as an administrative technique, which broke local resistance and permanently mixed the population it governed
tuples.evidence_lens: palace reliefs, royal annals, the state archive letters, and the destruction layers of the capitals

tuples.episode_object: Nineveh, from a shrine town to a burnt library
tuples.time_place_scope: the upper Tigris across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: the accumulation of a royal library as a state project, and the accident that a fire baked the tablets it was meant to destroy
tuples.evidence_lens: the library tablets themselves, palace relief programmes, and the account of the final siege

tuples.episode_object: the Neo-Babylonian empire, from rebellion to a bloodless surrender
tuples.time_place_scope: the floodplain, the Levant and the Arabian oases across ninety years
tuples.mechanism: an empire built in one lifetime on a temple economy, which never resolved the quarrel between its king and its priesthood
tuples.evidence_lens: building inscriptions, temple archives, astronomical diaries, and the propaganda of the conqueror

tuples.episode_object: the Kassite centuries, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the floodplain and the eastern mountains across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a foreign dynasty that governed by continuity, adopting the local language and gods so completely that its own origins are unrecoverable
tuples.evidence_lens: boundary stones recording land grants, diplomatic letters from an Egyptian archive, and temple rebuilding records

tuples.episode_object: Mari and the middle Euphrates kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Euphrates and the steppe behind it across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a river kingdom living on transit tolls and diplomacy, whose correspondence survives because the palace was burnt intact
tuples.evidence_lens: the palace letter archive, wall paintings, and the campaign records of the king who destroyed it

tuples.episode_object: Ebla and the northern Syrian cities, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain of northern Syria across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: an inland trade capital dependent on textiles and metals moving between coast and river, destroyed twice and rebuilt once
tuples.evidence_lens: a palace tablet archive in an unexpected language, city gate excavation, and the destruction layers

tuples.episode_object: the Hurrians and Mitanni, from a mountain people to a client kingdom
tuples.time_place_scope: the upper Khabur plain and northern Mesopotamia across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a chariot aristocracy ruling a farming population, formidable in the field and thin on the ground when the field was lost
tuples.evidence_lens: diplomatic correspondence held in foreign archives, treaty texts, and the still-unlocated capital

tuples.episode_object: Aramean Syria and the Aramaic language, told as one very long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the Syrian steppe, the Levant and eventually the whole Near East across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: the spread of a language by trade and deportation until it outlived every state that spoke it as a mother tongue
tuples.evidence_lens: royal stelae, alphabetic ostraca, the administrative record of empires that adopted the script, and living dialects

tuples.episode_object: the Chaldeans and the southern marsh tribes, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the marshes and canal country of the far south across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the political usefulness of impenetrable marshland, which let a tribal confederation resist an empire for two hundred years
tuples.evidence_lens: Assyrian campaign accounts, tribal genealogies in king lists, and the geography of the marshes themselves

tuples.episode_object: Babylonian astronomy, told as the whole life of one science
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern cities and their temple observatories across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: continuous dated observation by an institution rather than by individuals, which is what makes prediction possible at all
tuples.evidence_lens: the astronomical diaries, mathematical tablets, and the later Greek writers who inherited the numbers

tuples.episode_object: the temple economies of the south, told from first accounts to last offering
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern cities and their estates across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: the temple as landlord, bank and employer, and the slow transfer of that role to the palace and then to private families
tuples.evidence_lens: temple archives, tithe records, prebend sale contracts, and the excavation of storerooms

tuples.episode_object: Seleucid and Parthian Babylonia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the floodplain and its two capitals across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: the relocation of a capital a short distance away, which killed the old city slowly and completely without a siege
tuples.evidence_lens: cuneiform records written to the very end, Greek civic inscriptions, and the excavation of the new foundations

tuples.episode_object: the last cuneiform scribes, told as the end of a three-thousand-year practice
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern temple cities across the final four centuries of the script
tuples.mechanism: the death of a writing system as the death of the institution that trained its users, not of the language it wrote
tuples.evidence_lens: the latest dated tablets, scribal family archives, and the parallel rise of alphabetic documents

tuples.episode_object: Mesopotamian flood and creation stories, told as the life of a tradition
tuples.time_place_scope: the floodplain and everywhere its literature travelled, across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: the transmission of a story across languages and centuries by copying schools, and how each copy carries its own moment
tuples.evidence_lens: successive tablet recensions, school exercise copies, and the reappearance of the material in neighbouring literatures

tuples.episode_object: Egypt itself, from the first villages on the river to the closing of the last temple
tuples.time_place_scope: the Nile valley, the delta and the deserts on both sides across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: an annual flood that made the harvest predictable, which made taxation predictable, which made a continuous state possible for longer than anywhere else
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals and king lists checked against dated inscriptions, tomb biographies, and the flood level records

tuples.episode_object: the predynastic and early dynastic centuries, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley from the first cataract to the delta across a thousand years
tuples.mechanism: the unification of two very different countries into one office, and the ceremony invented to keep saying so for three thousand years
tuples.evidence_lens: decorated palettes and mace heads, the earliest royal cemeteries, and sealings recording officials

tuples.episode_object: the Old Kingdom, from the first stone building to the collapse of the central state
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern valley, the desert plateau and the Nubian trade roads across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: state capacity measured in stone, and the slow transfer of that capacity from the crown to the provincial governors who spent it
tuples.evidence_lens: pyramid complexes and their construction records, officials' tomb biographies, and provincial cemetery wealth

tuples.episode_object: the Middle Kingdom, from reunification to a delta ruled by outsiders
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole valley, the Faiyum and the Nubian forts across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: internal colonisation, in which a state reclaims a lake basin and fortifies a river frontier instead of building monuments
tuples.evidence_lens: the fortress chain in Nubia and its dispatches, land reclamation works, and the literature of the period

tuples.episode_object: the New Kingdom, from a war of expulsion to a divided country
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley, the Levantine corridor and Nubia across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: empire financed by tribute rather than by tax, which paid for the temples and left nothing when the tribute stopped
tuples.evidence_lens: temple annals of campaigns, diplomatic letters between great kings, and the workmen's village records

tuples.episode_object: Thebes and its west bank, told from provincial town to necropolis
tuples.time_place_scope: the great southern bend of the river across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: a religious capital whose priesthood accumulated land until it could govern the south independently of the king
tuples.evidence_lens: temple endowment lists, royal tomb archaeology, and the strike records of the tomb workers

tuples.episode_object: Amarna, told whole from a survey stone to an erased city
tuples.time_place_scope: a virgin bay in middle Egypt across one generation and its aftermath
tuples.mechanism: a state religion changed by decree, and the speed with which such a change is undone once its author dies
tuples.evidence_lens: boundary stelae, a planned city excavated as a single phase, and the diplomatic archive left behind

tuples.episode_object: Nubia and Kush under and against Egypt, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley above the first cataract and the desert gold roads across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a southern neighbour alternately colony and conqueror, which eventually ruled Egypt using Egypt's own royal language
tuples.evidence_lens: fortress inscriptions, the pyramid fields of the southern kingdoms, and the campaign records of both sides

tuples.episode_object: the Third Intermediate Period, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the delta, the valley and the Libyan margin across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a country governed by several dynasties at once, which functions economically and cannot act militarily
tuples.evidence_lens: genealogies of priestly families, parallel dynastic records, and the burial caches of relocated royal mummies

tuples.episode_object: the Late Period, from Saite revival to Persian province
tuples.time_place_scope: the delta, the valley and the Aegean trading ports across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: revival financed by foreign mercenaries and Greek trade, which restored the country and mortgaged its independence
tuples.evidence_lens: temple building programmes, mercenary graffiti, demotic contracts, and the accounts of Greek visitors

tuples.episode_object: the Egyptian language, told as one continuous life to Coptic
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley and the delta across four and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: a single language recorded in four successive scripts, whose final form survived only inside a church
tuples.evidence_lens: the script transitions themselves, bilingual decrees, and liturgical manuscripts in the final stage

tuples.episode_object: Egyptian religion, told as the whole life of a system
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley, the delta and the Mediterranean where its cults travelled, across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: the absorption of new gods without discarding old ones, which gave the system enormous resilience and no defence against exclusivity
tuples.evidence_lens: temple reliefs and their revisions, funerary papyri, oracle records, and the decrees that closed the temples

tuples.episode_object: the pyramids as a project, told from first mastaba to last royal pyramid
tuples.time_place_scope: the desert plateaus flanking the northern valley across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a construction programme whose real product was an organised state workforce, and which stopped when that workforce was needed elsewhere
tuples.evidence_lens: quarry marks and builders' graffiti, the workmen's settlements and their bakeries, and harbour delivery journals

tuples.episode_object: mummification, told as the whole life of a technique
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley, the delta and the oases across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: a funerary technology that became an industry with price tiers, and vanished when the belief that funded it changed
tuples.evidence_lens: the bodies themselves, embalming workshop finds, price lists on papyrus, and the accounts of foreign observers

tuples.episode_object: the Faiyum, told from a lake to a farmed basin and back
tuples.time_place_scope: the depression west of the valley across five millennia
tuples.mechanism: hydraulic engineering that creates farmland out of a lake and requires permanent maintenance to keep it
tuples.evidence_lens: canal and dyke archaeology, land survey papyri, and the portrait panels of its later inhabitants

tuples.episode_object: the oases of the western desert, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the depressions of the western desert and the caravan routes between them across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: settlement made possible by artesian water, and the political usefulness of places that are hard to reach and impossible to leave
tuples.evidence_lens: well and qanat archaeology, exile records, temple foundations, and caravan route surveys

tuples.episode_object: Alexandria under Rome and after, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western delta shore and its lake harbour across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a city of quarters that governed itself by riot as much as by council, and the earthquakes and silt that eventually finished it
tuples.evidence_lens: prefects' edicts, the record of civic disturbances, and the submerged harbour archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Christian Egypt, from the first communities to the desert monasteries
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley, the delta and the desert fringes across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: the invention of communal monasticism in a place with cheap desert land next to rich farmland
tuples.evidence_lens: monastic rules, ostraca from the monasteries, and the excavation of desert communities

tuples.episode_object: the Ptolemaic and Roman Egyptian countryside, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley villages and the Faiyum across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: the survival of a village world through three changes of ruling language, documented because its rubbish heaps stayed dry
tuples.evidence_lens: village archives on papyrus, tax registers, private letters, and land survey documents

tuples.episode_object: the rediscovery of Egypt, told as the whole life of an obsession
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley, the delta and the museums of Europe across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: the decipherment of a script, which turned a country of ruins into a country with a readable history and set off a century of removal
tuples.evidence_lens: expedition publications, excavation records of varying honesty, and the acquisition registers of museums

tuples.episode_object: the eastern Mediterranean Bronze Age, from the first palaces to the general collapse
tuples.time_place_scope: the Aegean, Anatolia, the Levant, Cyprus and Egypt across a thousand years
tuples.mechanism: an interlocking system of palace economies trading tin and copper, in which the failure of any large part brings down the rest
tuples.evidence_lens: palace archives in several scripts, shipwreck cargoes, and the destruction horizons across the whole region

tuples.episode_object: Minoan Crete, from the first palaces to a Mycenaean administration
tuples.time_place_scope: the island, its harbours and the southern Aegean across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: redistribution through palace storerooms, an economy of counting and issuing rather than of markets
tuples.evidence_lens: storeroom archaeology, an undeciphered administrative script, fresco programmes, and the later Greek-language tablets

tuples.episode_object: Mycenaean Greece, from shaft graves to burnt citadels
tuples.time_place_scope: the mainland, the islands and the trade routes east across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: warrior aristocracies running palace bureaucracies, which recorded everything they controlled and controlled less than they seemed to
tuples.evidence_lens: the deciphered palace tablets, citadel fortification phases, and the destruction layers

tuples.episode_object: Troy and the northeast Aegean, told through nine cities on one mound
tuples.time_place_scope: the mound at the mouth of the straits across three and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: a settlement rebuilt nine times on one spot because the spot controlled a strait, whatever happened to the people on it
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavation stratigraphy itself, Hittite diplomatic references, and the epic tradition read as memory

tuples.episode_object: the Hittite empire, from a highland town to a burnt capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the Anatolian plateau, north Syria and the Levantine corridor across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: an empire held together by sworn treaties with vassal kings rather than by garrisons, which failed when the oaths outlived the reasons for them
tuples.evidence_lens: the capital's clay tablet archive, treaty texts, rock reliefs, and the destruction of the capital

tuples.episode_object: Cyprus in the Bronze Age and after, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island, its copper hills and the sea routes around it across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: an island economy built on one metal, which made it indispensable to every neighbour and never strong enough to be independent
tuples.evidence_lens: copper smelting site archaeology, oxhide ingots from shipwrecks, and the correspondence of foreign kings requesting metal

tuples.episode_object: Ugarit, told from a coastal town to a destroyed archive
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Levantine coast and its harbour across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a port city as clearing house between empires, whose neutrality was its business model until the sea routes failed
tuples.evidence_lens: the palace archives in several languages, the alphabetic cuneiform texts, and the final letters written during the attack

tuples.episode_object: the Canaanite city-states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Levantine coast and its valleys across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a landscape of small city kingdoms, each too weak to unify the region and each valuable enough to be worth an empire's attention
tuples.evidence_lens: diplomatic letters from an Egyptian archive, city gate and temple excavation, and the alphabet they invented

tuples.episode_object: the Sea Peoples and the collapse, told from first raids to resettlement
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole eastern Mediterranean coast across two generations
tuples.mechanism: systemic collapse in which migration is as much a symptom as a cause, and the survivors settle where the palaces used to be
tuples.evidence_lens: Egyptian relief accounts, destruction layers across many sites, and the material culture of the new coastal settlements

tuples.episode_object: the Philistine cities, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Levantine coast across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: an immigrant population that becomes local within three generations, visible in pottery long after it is invisible in politics
tuples.evidence_lens: distinctive early pottery and its disappearance, city excavation, and hostile textual sources

tuples.episode_object: Bronze Age Anatolia beyond the Hittites, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau, the western valleys and the southern coast across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: the metals trade run by resident foreign merchant colonies, documented by their own correspondence rather than by any state
tuples.evidence_lens: merchant colony tablet archives, mine and smelting sites, and the seal impressions on contracts

tuples.episode_object: Bronze Age Cyprus and Levant maritime trade, told through one wrecked ship
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Anatolian coast and the routes around the eastern basin
tuples.mechanism: a single voyage as a cross-section of an entire economy, carrying ten cultures' goods in one hull
tuples.evidence_lens: the wreck excavation and its cargo, compared with palace inventories and customs texts on land

tuples.episode_object: the Aegean islands before Greece, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Cyclades and their marble islands across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: small island societies specialising in one exportable material, prosperous in a trading age and empty in a raiding one
tuples.evidence_lens: marble figurine contexts, obsidian distribution, and settlement abandonment sequences

tuples.episode_object: Bronze Age Egypt abroad, told as the whole life of a foreign policy
tuples.time_place_scope: the Levantine corridor, Nubia and the Aegean across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: empire by garrison and hostage-taking, in which the sons of vassals are educated at the imperial court and sent home loyal
tuples.evidence_lens: diplomatic letter archives, garrison town excavation, and the tribute scenes in tombs

tuples.episode_object: Bronze Age Mesopotamian trade with the east, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the gulf, the Iranian plateau and the Indus coast across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: long-distance exchange in stone, metal and beads between literate and less literate partners, visible mainly from one side
tuples.evidence_lens: seals found far from home, cuneiform cargo records, and the material distribution maps

tuples.episode_object: Bronze Age Italy and the western Mediterranean, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Italian peninsula, Sardinia, Sicily and the western basin across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: the arrival of eastern trade at the western edge, and the local societies that grew around supplying it
tuples.evidence_lens: tower and nuraghe archaeology, imported pottery in local contexts, and metal hoards

tuples.episode_object: Bronze Age Iberia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula, its silver country and its Atlantic coast across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: an Atlantic metal economy connected to the Mediterranean only intermittently, which shaped everything about its timing
tuples.evidence_lens: fortified settlement excavation, metal hoards, and the isotope analysis of exported metal

tuples.episode_object: Bronze Age Britain and the Atlantic coast, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the islands, the Channel and the Atlantic seaways across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a periphery joined to a continental system by one commodity, tin, and reorganised entirely when the demand for it moved
tuples.evidence_lens: tin stream working, hoards of continental metalwork, and the isotope evidence in graves

tuples.episode_object: the Bronze Age steppe and its wagons, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the grasslands from the Danube to the Altai across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: the domestication of the horse and the wheeled wagon together, which turned grassland from an obstacle into a road
tuples.evidence_lens: kurgan burial excavation, wagon and chariot finds, and the genetic evidence of population movement

tuples.episode_object: the end of the Bronze Age, told as one long systems failure
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole eastern Mediterranean and its hinterlands across a century
tuples.mechanism: the compounding of drought, earthquake, migration and trade failure, none of which alone explains what happened
tuples.evidence_lens: climate proxies from cores and pollen, destruction dates, and the last letters written from several archives

tuples.episode_object: the Phoenicians, from Levantine harbour towns to a memory carried in an alphabet
tuples.time_place_scope: the Levantine coast and every shore of the Mediterranean across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a trading people organised as separate harbour cities that never unified, which made them ubiquitous and permanently vulnerable
tuples.evidence_lens: their own inscriptions, which are short and few, read against the accounts of everyone who dealt with them

tuples.episode_object: Tyre, from an island town to a peninsula
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Levantine coast across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: an offshore island fortress, effectively impregnable until somebody was willing to build a causeway to it
tuples.evidence_lens: siege accounts from three different empires, harbour archaeology, and the tribute lists of Assyrian kings

tuples.episode_object: Sidon and Byblos, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central Levantine coast across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: cedar and papyrus as the two exports that made a coast indispensable to two great neighbours at once
tuples.evidence_lens: temple excavation, royal sarcophagus inscriptions, and Egyptian records of timber expeditions

tuples.episode_object: Carthage, from a colonial foundation to a ploughed field and a Roman city
tuples.time_place_scope: the gulf of Tunis, north Africa, Sicily, Sardinia and Iberia across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a merchant republic that hired its armies and could never replace them at the speed a farming rival replaced its own
tuples.evidence_lens: the accounts of its enemies almost exclusively, checked against the harbour excavation and the child cemetery debate

tuples.episode_object: the Punic wars, told as one hundred and twenty years from start to finish
tuples.time_place_scope: the western Mediterranean, Italy, Iberia and north Africa
tuples.mechanism: a war of attrition between a naval power and a manpower power, decided by which side could absorb repeated total defeats
tuples.evidence_lens: two rival historical traditions, battlefield and siege archaeology, and the treaty texts

tuples.episode_object: Punic Sardinia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island, its plains and its mining hills across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a colony held for grain and metal, whose interior was never really taken by anyone who held the coast
tuples.evidence_lens: tower settlement continuity, Punic sanctuary sites, and the successive administrative records

tuples.episode_object: Punic and Phoenician Iberia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Spanish coast, the silver rivers and the Atlantic gate across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: colonial mining enclaves paying for a home city's wars, which turned a peninsula into the treasury of two empires in succession
tuples.evidence_lens: mining district remains, colony excavations, and the campaign narratives of the wars fought for them

tuples.episode_object: Gadir and the Atlantic voyages, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Atlantic mouth of the Mediterranean and the coasts beyond, across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the deliberate secrecy of a trade route, which preserved a monopoly and destroyed the record we would need to describe it
tuples.evidence_lens: fragmentary voyage accounts preserved by others, Atlantic coast finds, and the fish salting installations

tuples.episode_object: the alphabet, told as the whole life of one invention
tuples.time_place_scope: the Levantine coast and everywhere ships went, across three and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: a writing system with few enough signs to be learned by traders rather than by scribes, which is why it travelled
tuples.evidence_lens: the earliest inscriptions in mines and on grave goods, letter form comparisons, and the borrowings by other languages

tuples.episode_object: Punic religion and the tophet debate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Carthage and the western colonies across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: the difficulty of reading a religion whose only surviving description was written by the people who destroyed it
tuples.evidence_lens: the urn deposits and their osteology, dedication stelae, and the polemical accounts of enemies

tuples.episode_object: Roman Carthage, told from refoundation to Vandal capital and after
tuples.time_place_scope: the gulf of Tunis and the African provinces across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: the refoundation of a destroyed city on the same harbour, because the harbour was always the reason for the city
tuples.evidence_lens: the Roman street grid over the Punic layers, church councils, and the accounts of two later conquests

tuples.episode_object: Numidia and the Berber kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the high plains and mountains of north Africa across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: kingdoms that grew by playing two Mediterranean powers against each other and ended when only one remained
tuples.evidence_lens: royal monuments, coin issues, and the campaign narratives of both Mediterranean powers

tuples.episode_object: Punic and Roman Malta, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the islands in the middle of the sea across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: a harbour in the exact centre of a sea, valuable to every power in turn and never able to be anything but a base
tuples.evidence_lens: temple complexes far older than the Phoenicians, harbour finds, and the successive garrison records

tuples.episode_object: Motya and Punic Sicily, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western tip of Sicily and its lagoons across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: an island trading post that became a frontier fortress when a war it did not start arrived on its beach
tuples.evidence_lens: the causeway and fortifications, the destruction layer, and the accounts of the siege

tuples.episode_object: the Phoenician cities under Persia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Levantine coast and the eastern Mediterranean across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: supplying the fleet of an empire that had no sailors of its own, which bought autonomy at the price of every war
tuples.evidence_lens: Persian naval records in Greek histories, city coin issues, and royal inscriptions of local kings

tuples.episode_object: purple dye, told as the whole life of an industry
tuples.time_place_scope: the Levantine and north African coasts across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a luxury monopoly resting on a shellfish and a smell, which set a colour aside for rulers for two thousand years
tuples.evidence_lens: murex shell middens, dyeing installation remains, price edicts, and sumptuary law

tuples.episode_object: Phoenician shipbuilding and navigation, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole Mediterranean and the Atlantic approaches across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the hull and the star knowledge that made night sailing possible, and therefore made a two-day crossing a one-night crossing
tuples.evidence_lens: wreck timbers, ship depictions on reliefs and coins, and the sailing directions preserved by later writers

tuples.episode_object: Cadiz to Cornwall, the tin road told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Atlantic coast from Iberia to the British isles across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a supply chain for one indispensable alloying metal, run through intermediaries so that neither end knew the other
tuples.evidence_lens: isotope sourcing of bronze, coastal trading site finds, and the guarded references in ancient geographies

tuples.episode_object: the Carthaginian constitution and its fall, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the city and its African hinterland across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a republic admired by its enemies for its stability and unable to survive losing control of its own mercenary army
tuples.evidence_lens: the constitutional descriptions of foreign philosophers, the mercenary war narrative, and civic inscriptions

tuples.episode_object: the destruction of Carthage and its long afterlife, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the gulf of Tunis and the Mediterranean imagination across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: the deliberate erasure of a city, and the way such an erasure guarantees the city is remembered for nothing else
tuples.evidence_lens: the siege narrative, the excavated burn layer, and the literary afterlife in the conquerors' own poetry

tuples.episode_object: the Mongol empire, from a confederation on the Onon to four separate khanates
tuples.time_place_scope: the grasslands, China, Iran, Russia and eastern Europe across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a conquest army organised in decimal units that cut across tribes, which destroyed the loyalties that would otherwise have broken it apart
tuples.evidence_lens: a secret dynastic history, the chronicles of every conquered literate society, and the administrative records of the successor states

tuples.episode_object: the Scythians, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the steppe from the Danube to the Altai across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a mobile society whose wealth was portable and whose graves are therefore the entire archive
tuples.evidence_lens: frozen kurgan burials, Greek ethnographic writing, and the gold work traded from settled neighbours

tuples.episode_object: the Xiongnu confederation, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Mongolian plateau and the Chinese frontier across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a steppe confederation whose unity depended on extracting goods from a settled empire, and which fragmented when the extraction stopped
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals of the settled neighbour, elite burial excavation, and frontier fortification archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the Huns in Europe, told from arrival to dispersal
tuples.time_place_scope: the Danube basin and the Roman frontiers across a century
tuples.mechanism: a tribute empire with no institutions beyond the person of one ruler, which cannot survive his funeral
tuples.evidence_lens: the accounts of embassies to the royal camp, Roman frontier records, and the archaeology of the plain

tuples.episode_object: the Turkic khaganates, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the steppe from Manchuria to the Black Sea across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the first steppe empire to write about itself, and what having its own script changed about its politics
tuples.evidence_lens: inscribed memorial stones in a native script, Chinese annals, and the accounts of Byzantine embassies

tuples.episode_object: the Khazars, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Volga, the Caucasus and the steppe across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a steppe state on a river junction that lived on tolls and chose a third religion to avoid choosing between two neighbours
tuples.evidence_lens: correspondence preserved by a distant community, Arab geographies, and the excavation of river fortresses

tuples.episode_object: the Avars, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Carpathian basin across two and a half centuries
