tuples.mechanism: the ring fortress and the accumulated treasure of a tribute empire, and how completely such a state disappears once the treasure is taken
tuples.evidence_lens: grave goods in enormous numbers, Byzantine tribute records, and the Frankish account of the final campaign

tuples.episode_object: the Cumans and Kipchaks, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the steppe from the Danube to the Volga across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a stateless steppe society absorbed by every neighbour it touched, contributing dynasties to several of them
tuples.evidence_lens: stone grave figures, the chronicles of settled neighbours, and a language recorded in one foreign handbook

tuples.episode_object: the Golden Horde, from a Mongol appanage to a broken frontier
tuples.time_place_scope: the Volga steppe, the Crimea and the Russian forest edge across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: indirect rule over forest principalities by tax farming and dynastic licence, which built the very state that eventually replaced it
tuples.evidence_lens: the yarlyk grants, Russian chronicles, Italian colony records in the Crimea, and the excavation of the capitals

tuples.episode_object: the Ilkhanate in Iran, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Iranian plateau, Mesopotamia and the Caucasus across eight decades
tuples.mechanism: conquerors adopting the religion and the bureaucracy of the conquered within two generations, and the succession quarrels that followed
tuples.evidence_lens: court histories written by the conquered, tax reform documents, and the observatory and its records

tuples.episode_object: the Chagatai khanate and the eastern steppe, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Central Asia between the Oxus and the Tarim across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the split between nomad and settled halves of one inheritance, which turned a khanate into two incompatible societies
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicles from both halves, coin evidence of rival claims, and the caravan city archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Timur and the Timurid century, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Central Asia, Iran, India and Anatolia across a century
tuples.mechanism: a conqueror who ruled through a puppet lineage because he could not claim descent himself, and the cultural flowering his heirs paid for
tuples.evidence_lens: campaign histories written for the court, the architecture of the capital, and the accounts of foreign ambassadors

tuples.episode_object: the Yuan dynasty in China, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: China, the steppe and the maritime approaches across a century
tuples.mechanism: steppe rulers governing a farming empire through a legal hierarchy of peoples, which secured the throne and guaranteed resentment
tuples.evidence_lens: dynastic history compiled by successors, tax and postal records, and the accounts of foreign visitors

tuples.episode_object: the Manchus before the conquest, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the forests and plains northeast of the wall across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: the banner system, which organised a mixed forest population into an army and a society at the same time
tuples.evidence_lens: the early archives in a new script, frontier trade records, and the campaign accounts of the neighbouring dynasty

tuples.episode_object: the Kazakh khanate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the steppe between the Urals, the Altai and the Syr Darya across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a pastoral confederation of three hordes, held together by custom and pasture rights rather than by a capital
tuples.evidence_lens: oral genealogies later written down, Russian and Chinese frontier reports, and the customary law collections

tuples.episode_object: the Crimean khanate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula, the northern shore and the raiding roads across three and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a state economically dependent on the captive trade, which made its foreign policy for it and ensured its neighbours would end it
tuples.evidence_lens: the khanate's own chancery records, Ottoman correspondence, and the ransom registers of its neighbours

tuples.episode_object: the Dzungar khanate, told from rise to annihilation
tuples.time_place_scope: the basins and mountains of the far northwest across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: the last steppe power to threaten a settled empire, and the first to be destroyed by gunpowder logistics rather than by another nomad
tuples.evidence_lens: the campaign records of the conquering dynasty, Jesuit maps and reports, and the demographic collapse evidence

tuples.episode_object: the horse, told as the whole life of one relationship
tuples.time_place_scope: the steppe and everywhere riders reached, across five millennia
tuples.mechanism: the compounding advantages of the horse — traction, then riding, then stirrup and composite bow — each of which redrew a continent
tuples.evidence_lens: harness and bit finds, chariot burials, artistic depictions, and the genetics of horse populations

tuples.episode_object: the silk and tribute economy of the steppe, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the frontier between grassland and farmland across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a system in which settled empires paid for peace in cloth and the steppe resold it, so that both sides depended on the arrangement
tuples.evidence_lens: frontier market records, textile finds in steppe graves, and the fiscal accounts of the paying empires

tuples.episode_object: the end of the steppe as a power, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the grasslands from Hungary to Manchuria across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the reversal produced by firearms, fortified lines and settled agriculture, which turned the world's great highway into a periphery
tuples.evidence_lens: military supply records, fortress line construction, settlement surveys, and the treaties of partition

tuples.episode_object: China itself, from the first walled towns to the last dynasty, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the two great river basins and everything the state reached, across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: a bureaucratic empire reconstituted after every collapse because the idea of one country survived each fall intact
tuples.evidence_lens: dynastic histories written by successors, excavated administrative documents, and the archaeology of capitals

tuples.episode_object: the Shang, from an oracle-bone capital to a conquered dynasty
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Yellow River across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: divination as an instrument of government, which recorded the state's questions and therefore its whole anxiety
tuples.evidence_lens: inscribed oracle bones in tens of thousands, royal tomb excavation, and bronze vessel inscriptions

tuples.episode_object: the Zhou, from a conquest to a king with no country
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yellow River basin and the expanding frontier across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: the delegation of territory to relatives, which secures a conquest in one generation and dissolves the state in ten
tuples.evidence_lens: bronze vessel inscriptions recording grants, the ritual classics, and the annals of individual states

tuples.episode_object: the Spring and Autumn states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yellow River plain and the Yangtze margins across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a system of many small states with an agreed etiquette of war, which worked until one state stopped observing it
tuples.evidence_lens: state annals with commentaries, treaty records, and the tombs of regional lords

tuples.episode_object: the Warring States, from many kingdoms to one empire
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole of the settled north and the middle Yangtze across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: the replacement of aristocratic levies with conscript infantry and iron tools, which made total war affordable and unification inevitable
tuples.evidence_lens: philosophical writings addressed to rulers, excavated legal texts, and the mass military burials

tuples.episode_object: the Qin, told whole from a frontier state to a fifteen-year empire
tuples.time_place_scope: the western valley and the whole unified country across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: standardisation of script, axle width, weights and law as the machinery of unification, imposed faster than the country could absorb
tuples.evidence_lens: excavated legal and administrative bamboo strips, the tomb complex, and the hostile histories of successors

tuples.episode_object: the Han, told whole from a peasant emperor to three kingdoms
tuples.time_place_scope: the two river basins, the western corridor and the northern frontier across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: an examined bureaucracy funded by state monopolies, which professionalised government and created a permanent argument about taxation
tuples.evidence_lens: the standard histories, excavated frontier documents from desert garrisons, and tomb finds

tuples.episode_object: Chang'an, told from a Qin suburb to a ruined capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the western valley and its river across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a planned capital whose water supply and grain canal set an absolute ceiling on its population and therefore on the dynasty's ambitions
tuples.evidence_lens: city wall and grid excavation, canal engineering records, and the poetry written about the city

tuples.episode_object: the Silk Road corridor under the Han, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western corridor, the oases and the routes to the west across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: garrisoned trade, in which an empire pays for forts on a road it does not own in order to buy horses it cannot breed
tuples.evidence_lens: frontier garrison documents on wood, oasis city excavation, and the embassy reports in the histories

tuples.episode_object: the Three Kingdoms and the long division, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole country from the Yellow River to the south across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the militarisation of provincial government, which made warlords out of governors and division out of a civil war
tuples.evidence_lens: the standard history and a later novelisation carefully distinguished, plus tomb and fortification archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the northern dynasties and the sinicisation debate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plains and the steppe frontier across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: steppe rulers adopting the language, dress and bureaucracy of their subjects by decree, and the backlash from their own army
tuples.evidence_lens: court edicts, cave temple inscriptions, tomb epitaphs, and the frontier garrison revolt records

tuples.episode_object: the southern dynasties, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Yangtze and the southern coast across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the transplantation of a northern court into a southern country, and the agricultural revolution that eventually made the south richer
tuples.evidence_lens: court literature, land reclamation records, and the archaeology of southern estates

tuples.episode_object: Buddhism in China, told as the whole life of an arrival
tuples.time_place_scope: the western corridor, the capitals and the mountains across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: the translation of a foreign religion into an existing philosophical vocabulary, and the state's recurring alarm at its wealth
tuples.evidence_lens: translation colophons, cave temple sequences, monastery land registers, and the suppression edicts

tuples.episode_object: the Sui, told whole from reunification to a canal and a collapse
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole country and the new canal line across thirty-seven years
tuples.mechanism: a dynasty that spent its entire political capital on infrastructure that its successor then enjoyed for three centuries
tuples.evidence_lens: canal engineering records, the campaign accounts of the failed wars, and the hostile successor history

tuples.episode_object: the Tang, told whole from a coup to a warlord partition
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole country, the western corridor and the tributary states across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a cosmopolitan capital and a frontier army system, which brought in the world and then let one frontier general use it
tuples.evidence_lens: the standard histories, examination and land allotment records, poetry, and the excavated foreign quarters

tuples.episode_object: the Grand Canal, told as the whole life of one waterway
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the Yangtze and the northern capitals across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: the artificial connection of two river systems, which let a capital be built where no capital could feed itself
tuples.evidence_lens: engineering and dredging records, transport tax accounts, and the towns that grew and died along the line

tuples.episode_object: Chinese writing, told as one continuous life
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole country and its neighbours across three and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: a script tied to meaning rather than sound, which held a country of mutually unintelligible speech together in one civil service
tuples.evidence_lens: oracle bone through modern forms in sequence, script reform edicts, and the borrowings by neighbouring languages

tuples.episode_object: the examination system, told from first proposals to abolition
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole empire and its schools across thirteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: recruitment by examination, which opened government to talent, defined an entire elite culture, and fossilised its curriculum
tuples.evidence_lens: examination records and quotas, printed study guides, and the abolition decree and its aftermath

tuples.episode_object: the Great Wall, told as the whole life of a frontier
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern frontier from the sea to the desert across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a wall as a customs and signalling line rather than a barrier, rebuilt in different places by dynasties with different frontier policies
tuples.evidence_lens: construction records, garrison documents, and the archaeology of the several distinct wall lines

tuples.episode_object: Chinese bronze and iron, told as the whole life of two metals
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern basins and the southern ore country across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: state control of metal production as the basis of both ritual authority and military power, and the point at which it became too big to control
tuples.evidence_lens: foundry excavation, vessel inscriptions, monopoly debate texts, and iron working site archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the Song dynasty, told whole from reunification to a drowning at sea
tuples.time_place_scope: the two river basins, the southern coast and the shrinking north across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a commercial revolution and a professional civil service financing a defensive state that paid its neighbours rather than fighting them
tuples.evidence_lens: the standard histories, tax and monopoly accounts, printed books in quantity, and the excavation of the two capitals

tuples.episode_object: Kaifeng and Hangzhou, told as the whole life of two capitals
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yellow River plain and the southern lake city across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: the shift of a capital from a river plain to a coastal delta, and how completely that changed what the state could tax
tuples.evidence_lens: a famous scroll painting read as evidence, city gazetteers, and flood and canal engineering records

tuples.episode_object: the Liao and the Jin, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern frontier, Manchuria and the northern plains across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: dual administration, one system for the steppe subjects and one for the farming ones, run by a single court
tuples.evidence_lens: bilingual inscriptions in two invented scripts, tomb painting, and the histories written by their conquerors

tuples.episode_object: the Tangut Xia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northwestern corridor and the desert margins across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a small state astride a trade corridor that invented its own script and printing tradition and left almost no readers
tuples.evidence_lens: a recovered library from a walled desert city, the invented script's dictionaries, and neighbouring annals

tuples.episode_object: the Ming, told whole from a peasant rebellion to a suicide on a hill
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole country, the northern frontier, and the sea across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: an inward turn after an early age of ocean voyages, and the fiscal rigidity that left no answer to silver inflation and famine
tuples.evidence_lens: the veritable records of the court, tax and land registers, and the private writings of officials

tuples.episode_object: the Ming treasure voyages, told from first fleet to burnt records
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern ports, the Indian Ocean and the east African coast across three decades
tuples.mechanism: state-funded prestige voyages with no commercial purpose, which are the first thing cut when the treasury is squeezed
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving stele inscriptions, shipyard archaeology, and the foreign records of the fleets' arrivals

tuples.episode_object: Beijing as a capital, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain below the passes across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: a capital placed to watch a frontier rather than to feed itself, permanently dependent on a canal and a grain fleet
tuples.evidence_lens: palace construction records, grain transport accounts, and the successive city wall circuits

tuples.episode_object: the Qing, told whole from beyond the wall to an abdication
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole empire including the steppe, the plateau and the far west across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a conquest dynasty ruling five constituencies in five idioms at once, which doubled the empire and could not survive being one thing
tuples.evidence_lens: the palace memorial archive, multilingual edicts, census and land data, and foreign diplomatic records

tuples.episode_object: the Chinese population, told as one long demographic life
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole country across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: the arrival of new crops that could grow on hillsides, which trebled a population and pushed settlement into ground that could not sustain it
tuples.evidence_lens: census and tax household data, crop introduction records, and the settlement archaeology of upland regions

tuples.episode_object: Chinese porcelain, told as the whole life of an industry
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern kiln country and every port it shipped from, across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a manufacturing town making a single high-value export for the world, and what happens when the world learns the recipe
tuples.evidence_lens: kiln site excavation, shipwreck cargoes, order documents from foreign buyers, and reign marks

tuples.episode_object: tea, told as the whole life of a commodity
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern hills, the caravan roads and the sea routes across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a crop that became a currency on one frontier and an addiction on another, dragging two empires into a war over the balance
tuples.evidence_lens: tax and monopoly records, tea-horse trade documents, and the trade accounts of foreign companies

tuples.episode_object: Chinese printing, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole country and its neighbours across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: the invention of printing in a script with thousands of characters, where woodblock beat movable type for eight hundred years
tuples.evidence_lens: dated printed sheets, block workshop records, and the publishing catalogues of commercial printers

tuples.episode_object: the Chinese canal and grain tribute system, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern plains between the Yangtze and the capital across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the annual movement of millions of tonnes of grain by state fleet, an operation larger than most contemporary states
tuples.evidence_lens: transport bureau records, lock and dredging engineering documents, and the collapse of the system's evidence

tuples.episode_object: Chinese maritime trade and its bans, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southeastern coast, the islands and Southeast Asia across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the recurring state decision to forbid private sea trade, which never stopped it and reliably created smuggling and piracy
tuples.evidence_lens: customs office records, prohibition edicts, wreck cargoes, and the genealogies of overseas communities

tuples.episode_object: the Chinese frontier in the southwest, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the mountains and river gorges of the southwest across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: the slow replacement of local chieftaincies by appointed officials, a policy carried out over six centuries and never quite completed
tuples.evidence_lens: chieftaincy appointment records, garrison colony documents, and the local gazetteers of frontier prefectures

tuples.episode_object: Xinjiang and the Tarim oases under Chinese rule, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the desert basin and its oasis ring across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: an intermittently governed corridor, controlled whenever a dynasty could afford garrisons and abandoned whenever it could not
tuples.evidence_lens: garrison documents, oasis manuscript finds in several languages, and dynastic frontier policy debates

tuples.episode_object: Tibet and the Chinese empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau and the routes down to the lowlands across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: the pairing of a monastic hierarchy with an external patron, an arrangement that gave both sides something and satisfied neither
tuples.evidence_lens: treaty pillars, monastic chronicles, imperial edicts, and the records of the imperial residents

tuples.episode_object: Chinese silver and the world economy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coastal ports, the Pacific and the Atlantic economies across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: an empire that taxed in silver it did not mine, tying its domestic stability to mines on the other side of the world
tuples.evidence_lens: customs and mint records, Spanish colonial shipping registers, and the price series in local gazetteers

tuples.episode_object: the Taiping and the mid-century wars, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yangtze provinces and the southern hills across fourteen years
tuples.mechanism: a millenarian rebellion that raised provincial armies to defeat it, and thereby moved military power out of the capital permanently
tuples.evidence_lens: rebel proclamations, the memorials of the officials who fought it, and the demographic evidence of the losses

tuples.episode_object: the end of the Chinese empire, told from first treaty to abdication
tuples.time_place_scope: the coastal ports, the capital and the provinces across seventy years
tuples.mechanism: a state that could reform its arsenals but not its revenue, borrowing against customs it no longer controlled
tuples.evidence_lens: treaty texts, customs service archives, reform memorials, and the provincial assembly records

tuples.episode_object: Japan itself, from the first pottery to the end of the shoguns, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the four main islands and the seas around them across ten millennia
tuples.mechanism: an island country that borrowed intensively by choice and closed itself by choice, and could do both because the sea allowed it
tuples.evidence_lens: court chronicles, temple archives, excavated administrative documents, and the diaries of officials

tuples.episode_object: the Jomon, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the archipelago and its coasts across ten millennia
tuples.mechanism: a settled society without agriculture, sustained by nuts, fish and shellfish, which upends the usual order of the story
tuples.evidence_lens: shell middens, the pottery sequence itself, pit dwelling excavation, and pollen cores

tuples.episode_object: the Yayoi and the arrival of rice, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western islands and the plains across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the arrival of wet rice farming and metal together, and the warfare that appears in the record at exactly the same moment
tuples.evidence_lens: moated settlement excavation, bronze bell deposits, skeletal evidence of violence, and Chinese notices

tuples.episode_object: the Kofun period and the tomb builders, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central plains and the Inland Sea across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: keyhole tomb building as a political map, since who was allowed which size of mound records the whole hierarchy
tuples.evidence_lens: the mounds themselves and their haniwa figures, imported mirrors and swords, and the later chronicles

tuples.episode_object: the Asuka and Nara centuries, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central basin and the new capitals across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a Chinese-style law code imported wholesale into a country with a very different landholding reality, and the gap that opened
tuples.evidence_lens: the law codes and their commentaries, temple treasure inventories, wooden tally documents, and census fragments

tuples.episode_object: Heian Japan, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital basin and the provinces across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a court that governed by marriage politics and delegated the provinces to men who slowly became a military class
tuples.evidence_lens: court diaries, tale literature read carefully as evidence, land estate documents, and temple records

tuples.episode_object: Kyoto, told as the whole life of a capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern basin between three mountains across twelve centuries
tuples.mechanism: a capital that survived losing political power by becoming the country's cultural and religious authority instead
tuples.evidence_lens: city plan and excavation, fire and war damage records, and the accounts of successive rebuildings

tuples.episode_object: the Kamakura shogunate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern seaboard, the capital and the western defences across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: military government beside an intact imperial court, a dual system that lasted seven hundred years because neither could remove the other
tuples.evidence_lens: warrior house documents, land grant records, the invasion defences, and temple chronicles

tuples.episode_object: the Mongol invasions and their aftermath, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Kyushu coast and the straits across two campaigns and a generation
tuples.mechanism: a defence that bankrupted the winners, because a defensive war produces no land with which to reward the defenders
tuples.evidence_lens: the coastal wall, the wreck archaeology, warrior claim petitions, and the chronicles of both sides

tuples.episode_object: the Muromachi centuries, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital, the provinces and the China trade across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a shogunate too weak to control its own deputies, which produced both a hundred years of civil war and a great cultural age
tuples.evidence_lens: temple estate documents, trade licence records, and the diaries of courtiers and monks

tuples.episode_object: the Warring States century, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole archipelago province by province across a hundred and fifty years
tuples.mechanism: the replacement of inherited lordship by cadastral survey and sworn retainer bands, which is how a fragmented country reunified
tuples.evidence_lens: land survey registers, castle archaeology, house codes, and the letters of the contending lords

tuples.episode_object: the arrival of firearms and Christianity, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern islands, the ports and the capital across a century
tuples.mechanism: two imported technologies, one military and one religious, accepted at speed and then handled in opposite ways
tuples.evidence_lens: missionary letters and reports, gun manufacture records, and the persecution and expulsion edicts

tuples.episode_object: the reunification and the invasion of Korea, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the archipelago and the Korean peninsula across four decades
tuples.mechanism: a unifier who solved his surplus-soldier problem with an overseas war, and the succession vacuum that war left at home
tuples.evidence_lens: campaign correspondence, Korean and Chinese accounts, and the land survey that underwrote the whole system

tuples.episode_object: the Tokugawa peace, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole country, its road system and its two great cities across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: control by hostage residence and alternate attendance, which bankrupted the lords with travel and built a national road economy
tuples.evidence_lens: domain financial records, road station documents, city registers, and the shogunate's own edicts

tuples.episode_object: Edo, told as the whole life of a city
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern bay and its river delta across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a city built for a garrison that became the largest in the world, run on fire, water engineering and rice brokerage
tuples.evidence_lens: fire and rebuilding records, water supply engineering, rice exchange documents, and printed city guides

tuples.episode_object: Japanese seclusion, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the ports, the one open island and the northern and southern frontiers across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a policy of controlled contact rather than closure, in which four gateways were kept open on the state's own terms
tuples.evidence_lens: trading post journals, translated foreign books, castaway interrogation records, and frontier reports

tuples.episode_object: Japanese Buddhism, told as one long institutional life
tuples.time_place_scope: the capital, the mountains and the provinces across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: monastic institutions that became landowners and then armies, and the state's repeated attempts to disarm them
tuples.evidence_lens: temple land registers, sect founding documents, and the campaign accounts of the temple wars

tuples.episode_object: Ainu and the northern frontier, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern island, the Kuriles and Sakhalin across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a trading people caught between two expanding states, whose commerce was converted into subordination one contract at a time
tuples.evidence_lens: trading post records, Ainu oral literature written down later, and the archaeology of northern settlements

tuples.episode_object: the Ryukyu kingdom, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern island chain and the sea routes across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a small kingdom that paid tribute to two larger neighbours simultaneously and prospered precisely by being useful to both
tuples.evidence_lens: the kingdom's own diplomatic records, Chinese investiture accounts, and castle excavation

tuples.episode_object: the end of the shogunate, told from the first foreign ship to the last domain
tuples.time_place_scope: the ports, the capital and the domains across fifteen years
tuples.mechanism: a regime undone by having to make foreign policy in public, which turned every treaty into a domestic legitimacy crisis
tuples.evidence_lens: treaty texts, domain memorials, foreign legation reports, and the earliest photographs

tuples.episode_object: Korea itself, from the first walled towns to the last king, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula and its northern border country across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a peninsula between a continental empire and an island one, which survived by being formally subordinate and practically separate
tuples.evidence_lens: dynastic annals kept in extraordinary detail, stele inscriptions, and the excavation of successive capitals

tuples.episode_object: Gojoseon and the earliest states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northwest of the peninsula and the Liao country across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the difficulty of writing the history of a state known mainly from the records of the empire that destroyed it
tuples.evidence_lens: dolmen and bronze dagger distributions, Chinese commandery records, and later Korean traditions

tuples.episode_object: Goguryeo, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern peninsula and Manchuria across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a fortress kingdom in mountainous country, which survived four centuries of invasion and fell to a coalition rather than to a conquest
tuples.evidence_lens: tomb murals, a great memorial stele, fortress archaeology, and the annals of three neighbours

tuples.episode_object: Baekje, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southwest of the peninsula and the sea routes to Japan across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a maritime kingdom that exported craftsmen and Buddhism across a strait and drew its defence from the same relationship
tuples.evidence_lens: royal tomb finds, temple site excavation, and the chronicles of the archipelago it traded with

tuples.episode_object: Silla, told whole from a small kingdom to a unified peninsula
tuples.time_place_scope: the southeast and eventually the whole peninsula across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: bone rank, a hereditary status ceiling that made the kingdom stable for centuries and then made reform impossible
tuples.evidence_lens: the capital's tombs and their gold, temple foundations, stone inscriptions, and the later dynastic history

tuples.episode_object: Gaya, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern river valleys and the strait across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: an iron-producing confederation of small polities that never unified, and was therefore absorbed piece by piece
tuples.evidence_lens: iron ingot burials, harbour site excavation, and the references in the records of both neighbours

tuples.episode_object: Balhae, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Manchuria, the northern peninsula and the maritime province across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a successor state to a destroyed kingdom, recorded almost entirely by the empires it sent embassies to
tuples.evidence_lens: capital city excavation, embassy records in two foreign archives, and the tomb inscriptions of its princes

tuples.episode_object: Goryeo, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula, the northern frontier and the sea across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a Buddhist aristocratic kingdom that survived a Mongol conquest by moving its court to an island for three decades
tuples.evidence_lens: the printed canon and its blocks, government records, celadon kiln sites, and Mongol treaty documents

tuples.episode_object: the Goryeo printed canon and Korean printing, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island refuge, the temples and the capital across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: the carving of an entire Buddhist canon as an act of state defence, and the metal type that followed it
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving blocks themselves, printing office records, and the earliest metal-type books

tuples.episode_object: the Joseon dynasty, told whole from a coup to a protectorate
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula, the northern rivers and the sea across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a Confucian bureaucratic state that recorded its own daily business obsessively and made faction the engine of its politics
tuples.evidence_lens: the daily court annals, examination records, land surveys, and the private writings of officials

tuples.episode_object: the Korean alphabet, told as the whole life of one invention
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a script designed for the language rather than borrowed, resisted by the elite for four hundred years and then adopted completely
tuples.evidence_lens: the promulgation document itself, early printed texts, and the private letters written in it long before it was official

tuples.episode_object: the Imjin war, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula, the straits and the sea across seven years
tuples.mechanism: a land invasion defeated at sea by a fleet that cut its supply line, and the twenty-year recovery that followed
tuples.evidence_lens: the admiral's own war diary, court records, Japanese and Chinese accounts, and the demographic evidence

tuples.episode_object: Joseon and the Manchu invasions, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern frontier and the capital across a generation
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom forced to change overlord by a two-month campaign, and the ideological crisis of serving a dynasty it considered barbarian
tuples.evidence_lens: the surrender stele, court debate records, and the accounts of hostage princes

tuples.episode_object: Korean Confucianism and its academies, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the provinces and the capital across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: private academies that trained the bureaucracy and became factional strongholds, until the state closed most of them
tuples.evidence_lens: academy registers, factional correspondence, examination results, and the closure decree

tuples.episode_object: Korean Buddhism, told as one long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the mountains, the capitals and the temples across sixteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a religion that was the state's ideology, then its enemy, then its refuge in the mountains, without ever disappearing
tuples.evidence_lens: temple foundation records, monk registers, suppression edicts, and mountain monastery archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Korean celadon and porcelain, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southwestern kiln country and the export routes across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a court taste that supported a regional industry, and the wars and conscriptions that moved its potters abroad
tuples.evidence_lens: kiln excavation, shipwreck cargoes, tribute lists, and the later Japanese kiln genealogies

tuples.episode_object: Korean agriculture and its famines, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula's valleys and terraces across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: double cropping and irrigation raising the population to the exact limit of the land, so that every bad year became a famine
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural manuals, relief grain records, weather diaries, and the population registers

tuples.episode_object: Korea and the sea, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coasts, the islands and the sea lanes across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: an intentionally shallow maritime policy, which suppressed piracy and private trade together and left the coast defenceless
tuples.evidence_lens: coastal fortress records, piracy reports, shipwreck finds, and the fisheries documents

tuples.episode_object: Jeju and the island periphery, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern volcanic island and the smaller islands across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: an island kingdom absorbed as a horse pasture and penal colony, and the distinct society that persisted anyway
tuples.evidence_lens: island chronicles, horse ranch records, exile documents, and the local oral tradition later recorded

tuples.episode_object: the end of Joseon, told from first treaty to annexation
tuples.time_place_scope: the ports, the capital and the frontier across four decades
tuples.mechanism: a court caught between three neighbours and reforming under all their supervision at once, which satisfied none of them
tuples.evidence_lens: treaty texts, legation reports from several countries, reform edicts, and the newspaper record

tuples.episode_object: the Khmer empire, told whole from first kingdoms to an abandoned capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the great lake, the lower Mekong and the whole basin across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: hydraulic urbanism on a floodplain, a city of reservoirs and canals that could not be maintained once the rains changed
tuples.evidence_lens: Sanskrit and Khmer inscriptions, temple building sequences, and the water system mapped from the air

tuples.episode_object: Angkor as a city, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the plain north of the great lake across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a low-density city spread over a thousand square kilometres, which is invisible on the ground and obvious from above
tuples.evidence_lens: aerial and radar survey, temple foundation inscriptions, and the account of one Chinese visitor

tuples.episode_object: Funan and the earliest Mekong states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Mekong delta and the gulf coast across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a portage state living on the trans-peninsular route, which became irrelevant when ships learned to sail around instead
tuples.evidence_lens: canal traces from the air, Roman and Indian objects in delta sites, and Chinese embassy records

tuples.episode_object: Champa, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central Vietnamese coast and its river mouths across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a chain of separate coastal principalities sharing a culture, absorbed one river valley at a time over eight hundred years
tuples.evidence_lens: brick tower sanctuaries and their inscriptions, Chinese and Vietnamese annals, and port site archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Dai Viet and Vietnam, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Red River delta, the central coast and the southern delta across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a delta state that expanded southwards along a coast for six centuries, absorbing two other countries as it went
tuples.evidence_lens: dynastic annals, stele inscriptions, land registers, and the archaeology of the successive capitals

tuples.episode_object: the Vietnamese under Chinese rule and after, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Red River delta and the northern frontier across a millennium and its aftermath
tuples.mechanism: a thousand years of provincial administration followed by nine centuries of independence conducted in the same written language
tuples.evidence_lens: Chinese administrative records, Vietnamese annals written afterwards, and the epigraphy of both periods

tuples.episode_object: Pagan and the first Burmese empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the dry zone of the middle Irrawaddy across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: temple donation as a tax-free transfer of land to religion, which endowed a spectacular capital and starved the crown
tuples.evidence_lens: donation inscriptions in several languages, the temple field itself, and the chronicles written later

tuples.episode_object: the Burmese kingdoms after Pagan, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Irrawaddy valley, the Shan hills and the coasts across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a valley state repeatedly rebuilt from the dry zone, always able to conquer the coast and never able to hold the hills
tuples.evidence_lens: royal chronicles, revenue inquest records, and the accounts of foreign merchants and envoys

tuples.episode_object: the Mon kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Irrawaddy, the Salween mouth and the Chao Phraya across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a coastal people who supplied the writing, religion and law to the valley kingdoms that eventually absorbed them
tuples.evidence_lens: early inscriptions, Buddhist ordination records, and the chronicles of neighbouring kingdoms

tuples.episode_object: Sukhothai and the first Thai kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the upper Chao Phraya basin across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: small valley kingdoms formed as a larger empire receded, whose reputation was later enlarged for national purposes
tuples.evidence_lens: a much-debated stone inscription, temple architecture, and the ceramics industry's kiln sites

tuples.episode_object: Ayutthaya, told whole from foundation to sack
tuples.time_place_scope: the Chao Phraya floodplain and the gulf across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: an island city at a river junction living on transit trade, cosmopolitan in personnel and absolutely centralised in law
tuples.evidence_lens: foreign trading company records, court law codes, the ruins themselves, and the accounts of the final siege

tuples.episode_object: Lan Na and the northern Thai states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern valleys and the upper Mekong across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a mountain-valley kingdom of the middle ground, tributary to whichever of three larger neighbours was strongest that decade
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicles kept in monasteries, palm leaf manuscripts, and the tribute records of neighbours

tuples.episode_object: Lan Xang and the Lao kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Mekong and its tributaries across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a river kingdom split into three by inheritance, which turned one state into three tributaries of two larger powers
tuples.evidence_lens: monastery chronicles, boundary stele, and the diplomatic records of the neighbouring courts

tuples.episode_object: the Shan and Tai upland states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the hills between the Irrawaddy, the Salween and the Mekong across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: upland principalities that survived by paying tribute in several directions at once and being too costly to garrison
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicles of individual states, tribute records of three empires, and colonial survey reports

tuples.episode_object: the Tai migrations, told as one long movement
tuples.time_place_scope: the country from the southern Chinese hills to the Malay isthmus across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the gradual southward spread of a language group along river valleys, absorbing and being absorbed as it went
tuples.evidence_lens: linguistic distribution, chronicle traditions, and the archaeology of valley settlement sequences

tuples.episode_object: the Irrawaddy and Mekong delta reclamations, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the two great deltas across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the conversion of mangrove and swamp into rice land, which fed empires and created entirely new societies on new ground
tuples.evidence_lens: land grant and canal records, rice export statistics, and the settlement mapping of the delta

tuples.episode_object: Theravada Buddhism in the mainland, told as one long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the valleys from the Irrawaddy to the Mekong across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a monastic order reformed repeatedly by kings who needed its legitimacy, so that religious purification was also state building
tuples.evidence_lens: ordination lineage records, monastery land grants, reform edicts, and inscription programmes

tuples.episode_object: the Malay isthmus and the portage routes, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the narrow neck of the peninsula and both its coasts across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: the choice between carrying goods across a neck of land and sailing round it, which made and unmade a dozen ports
tuples.evidence_lens: port site excavation, Chinese and Arab sailing directions, and the customs records of successive controllers

tuples.episode_object: the mainland under colonial rule, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the deltas, the uplands and the frontier lines across a century
tuples.mechanism: the drawing of straight frontiers through upland societies, and the delta rice economies built to pay for the administration
tuples.evidence_lens: survey and boundary commission records, rice export statistics, and the administrative reports of three colonial powers

tuples.episode_object: Siam between the empires, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole kingdom and its shifting frontiers across a century
tuples.mechanism: the one mainland state that stayed nominally independent by ceding peripheries to both neighbours and reforming to their template
tuples.evidence_lens: treaty texts, boundary commission reports, palace reform records, and foreign advisers' correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Srivijaya, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the straits, the eastern Sumatran rivers and the sea lanes across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a thalassocracy of river mouths that controlled a strait without controlling any territory behind it
tuples.evidence_lens: Chinese pilgrim and embassy accounts, a handful of stone inscriptions, and the archaeology of river port sites

tuples.episode_object: Majapahit, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: eastern Java, the archipelago's ports and the trade routes across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: an agrarian Javanese core financed by a maritime periphery, an arrangement that only holds while the ports find it profitable
tuples.evidence_lens: a court poem read as a claim rather than a map, temple remains, and Chinese trade records

tuples.episode_object: Java before Islam, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the volcanic plains and river valleys of the island across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: rice terraces on volcanic soil supporting a population dense enough to build the largest monuments in the region
tuples.evidence_lens: temple complexes and their reliefs, copperplate charters, and the eruption stratigraphy that dates them

tuples.episode_object: Borobudur and the temple-building centuries, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central Javanese plain across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: monumental religious construction as a competition between two dynasties, abandoned when the political centre moved east
tuples.evidence_lens: the monuments themselves and their reliefs, foundation charters, and volcanic burial and rediscovery records

tuples.episode_object: the Malacca sultanate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the straits and the peninsula's west coast across a century
tuples.mechanism: a port state that made itself indispensable by guaranteeing safety and fair measures, and was taken in a single afternoon
tuples.evidence_lens: a court chronicle, Portuguese conquest accounts, and harbour and customs archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the Malay sultanates after Malacca, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula, Sumatra and the straits across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the dispersal of one entrepot into several, each too small to control the strait and too useful to be destroyed
tuples.evidence_lens: court chronicles, treaty documents with trading companies, and the correspondence between sultans

tuples.episode_object: Aceh, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern tip of Sumatra and the Indian Ocean approaches across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a pepper state with a direct route to the Red Sea, which made it rich, devout and permanently at war with the strait powers
tuples.evidence_lens: the sultanate's own letters, Ottoman and Portuguese records, and pepper export accounts

tuples.episode_object: the spice islands, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the small islands of the eastern archipelago across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: three tiny islands producing the only supply of two spices, and the century of violence that a monopoly attempt required
tuples.evidence_lens: trading company records, fort archaeology, tree-planting and eradication orders, and local oral history

tuples.episode_object: the Bugis and Makassar, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southwestern peninsula of Sulawesi and the eastern seas across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a seafaring people who became indispensable crews, settlers and mercenaries across the archipelago after their own port fell
tuples.evidence_lens: the kingdom's own written chronicles and diaries, treaty documents, and the distribution of their settlements

tuples.episode_object: Brunei and the northern Borneo coast, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the north coast of Borneo and the Sulu sea across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a coastal sultanate ruling upriver peoples through trade monopolies rather than administration, and ceding coast by coast
tuples.evidence_lens: the sultanate's grants and treaties, foreign traveller accounts, and river settlement archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the Sulu sultanate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island chain between Borneo and the Philippines across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a maritime state whose economy required raiding and slaving, which made accommodation with settled neighbours impossible
tuples.evidence_lens: captive and ransom records, Spanish and British reports, and the sultanate's own correspondence

tuples.episode_object: the Philippines before and after Spain, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island group, its coasts and its highlands across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a scattering of coastal chiefdoms consolidated by a maritime empire that arrived from the opposite side of the world
tuples.evidence_lens: early Chinese trade notices, Spanish administrative and missionary records, and the archaeology of coastal sites

tuples.episode_object: the Manila galleon, told as the whole life of a route
tuples.time_place_scope: the Pacific between Manila and Acapulco across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: an annual voyage exchanging American silver for Chinese goods, which joined two hemispheres into one price system
tuples.evidence_lens: cargo registers, shipwreck excavation, mint records, and the customs accounts at both ends

tuples.episode_object: Islam in the archipelago, told as one long arrival
tuples.time_place_scope: the coasts and rivers of the islands across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a religion that arrived by trade rather than conquest, adopted first by port rulers and spread inland by their authority
tuples.evidence_lens: gravestone inscriptions, court chronicles, mosque architecture sequences, and merchant network records

tuples.episode_object: the Dutch company in the islands, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the archipelago's ports and the Java interior across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a chartered company with sovereign powers, which behaved like a state and went bankrupt like a business
tuples.evidence_lens: the company's own enormous archive, its balance sheets, treaty texts, and the accounts of its local partners

tuples.episode_object: Bali, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island, its terraces and its temples across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: an irrigation society organised through temple associations, which allocated water by ritual calendar rather than by decree
tuples.evidence_lens: water temple records, palm leaf manuscripts, terrace archaeology, and colonial conquest accounts

tuples.episode_object: Sumatra's interiors, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, lakes and river valleys of the island across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: upland societies that supplied the coast with gold, camphor and pepper and were never governed by it
tuples.evidence_lens: highland inscription finds, trade route surveys, missionary and colonial reports, and oral genealogies

tuples.episode_object: Borneo's rivers, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the great river systems of the island across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a geography where a river is the only road, so that every polity is a chain of settlements and nobody controls the interior
tuples.evidence_lens: upriver trade goods in longhouse contexts, coastal port records, and colonial expedition journals

tuples.episode_object: the archipelago's shipbuilding and navigation, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the seas between the islands and out to the Indian Ocean across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a plank-built hull and a monsoon calendar that made ordinary long voyages possible for ordinary traders, not just for states
tuples.evidence_lens: wreck excavation, ship depictions on temple reliefs, and the sailing directions of foreign pilots

tuples.episode_object: the Austronesian expansion, told as one enormous voyage
tuples.time_place_scope: the ocean from Taiwan to Madagascar and to Easter Island across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: the outrigger and the double canoe, which turned the largest ocean on earth into a settleable frontier
tuples.evidence_lens: linguistic family trees, pottery distribution, plant and animal transfers, and the genetics of island populations

tuples.episode_object: the Indus civilisation, from the first towns to the last street level
tuples.time_place_scope: the Indus and Ghaggar river systems and the coast across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a large urban civilisation with standardised weights and drains and no visible palaces or kings, which changes what a state is assumed to look like
tuples.evidence_lens: excavated city plans and drainage, an undeciphered seal script, standardised weights, and river course studies

tuples.episode_object: the Vedic centuries, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Punjab rivers and the upper Ganges plain across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: an oral corpus preserved with extraordinary precision by memorisation, which is a better record of language than of events
tuples.evidence_lens: the hymns themselves treated as language evidence, painted grey ware sites, and iron working horizons

tuples.episode_object: the Mahajanapadas and the first Indian states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Ganges plain from the Punjab to Bengal across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the appearance of territorial kingdoms and republics side by side, and the fiscal advantage that let the kingdoms win
tuples.evidence_lens: punch-marked coinage, fortified city excavation, and the earliest Buddhist and Jain texts as social evidence

tuples.episode_object: the Mauryan empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: almost the whole subcontinent and the northwest across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: an empire announced on rocks in several languages, which tells us what the centre wanted said and very little about how it governed
tuples.evidence_lens: the rock and pillar edicts, a treatise on statecraft of uncertain date, and Greek ambassadorial fragments

tuples.episode_object: Buddhism in India, told from a teacher to a near disappearance
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Ganges plain and outward across the subcontinent across eighteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a monastic religion dependent on royal and merchant patronage, which followed the trade routes out and left when they moved
tuples.evidence_lens: monastic site excavation, donative inscriptions naming the donors, and pilgrim accounts from abroad

tuples.episode_object: Jainism, told as one continuous life
tuples.time_place_scope: western and southern India across twenty-six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a religion of merchants and ascetics that survived by staying small, literate and useful to rulers who needed bankers
tuples.evidence_lens: manuscript libraries preserved for centuries, temple inscriptions, and merchant community records

tuples.episode_object: the Satavahanas and the Deccan, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Deccan plateau and both coasts across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a plateau kingdom joining two coasts, which prospered from Roman-era sea trade and declined with it
tuples.evidence_lens: cave monastery donation inscriptions, Roman coin hoards, and port site excavation

tuples.episode_object: Tamil south India before empires, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the far south, its rivers and its coasts across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a literate southern society documented by its own poetry, which describes an economy the inscriptions later confirm
tuples.evidence_lens: the early Tamil poetic anthologies, hero stones, Roman trade goods, and cave inscriptions

tuples.episode_object: the Gupta centuries, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Ganges plain and the north across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: an empire of subordinate kings rather than provinces, which produced stability and left no administrative record to speak of
tuples.evidence_lens: gold coin issues, land grant plates, temple sculpture, and the account of a Chinese pilgrim

tuples.episode_object: the Indian Ocean trade of the classical period, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western coast, the Red Sea and the gulf across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: monsoon sailing that made a direct crossing possible, converting a coastal creep into an annual bulk trade
tuples.evidence_lens: a merchant handbook of the routes, port excavation on both shores, amphorae, and customs papyri

tuples.episode_object: Gandhara and the northwest, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Kabul and Indus valleys and the passes across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a crossroads region whose art and religion are legible as a mixture precisely because the sources were so far apart
tuples.evidence_lens: monastic and stupa excavation, sculpture in a hybrid style, and inscriptions in several scripts

tuples.episode_object: Indian mathematics and astronomy, told as one long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the subcontinent's centres of learning across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a positional number system with a zero, developed for astronomy and exported west by translation two centuries later
tuples.evidence_lens: dated mathematical treatises, astronomical tables, inscriptional numerals, and the Arabic translations

tuples.episode_object: Sanskrit, told as the whole life of a language
tuples.time_place_scope: the subcontinent and Southeast Asia across three and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: a language fixed by grammarians and kept as the medium of learning and inscription long after nobody spoke it at home
tuples.evidence_lens: the grammatical treatises, the epigraphic record, manuscripts, and the inscriptions of Southeast Asian courts

tuples.episode_object: the Indian epics, told as the life of two texts
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain and everywhere the stories travelled, across two and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: the growth of two enormous poems by accretion, so that the text records the centuries that copied it as much as the age it describes
tuples.evidence_lens: manuscript recension comparison, temple relief programmes, and regional retellings

tuples.episode_object: the caste order, told as one long institutional life
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole subcontinent across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a hereditary occupational order that varied enormously by region, hardened under census categorisation, and shaped every institution around it
tuples.evidence_lens: legal treatises, inscriptional donor titles, caste association records, and colonial census categories

tuples.episode_object: the Kushan and post-Kushan north, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northwest, the Punjab and the upper Ganges across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a foreign dynasty using several religious idioms at once because its subjects and customers used several
tuples.evidence_lens: multilingual coinage, monastic donations, and the dating controversies of its era systems

tuples.episode_object: the Chola precursors and early Tamil kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Kaveri delta and the southern coasts across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: delta irrigation and temple landholding, the two institutions that made southern kingdoms durable and legible
tuples.evidence_lens: temple wall inscriptions recording grants and assemblies, irrigation works, and hero stones

tuples.episode_object: Indian ports and their Roman trade, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western and eastern coasts across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a bullion-for-goods imbalance that worried one empire's moralists and enriched the other's ports for two centuries
tuples.evidence_lens: coin hoards, amphora finds, port warehouse excavation, and the customs and complaint literature of both ends

tuples.episode_object: Indian iron and steel, told as the whole life of a craft
tuples.time_place_scope: the Deccan and the southern hills across two and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: a crucible steel process producing a superior blade metal, exported for a thousand years and lost when its markets industrialised
tuples.evidence_lens: furnace and crucible archaeology, the surviving iron pillar, trade records, and metallurgical analysis

tuples.episode_object: the end of the classical order, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain, the northwest and the Deccan across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the fragmentation of an imperial system into regional kingdoms that were smaller, richer and better documented than what preceded them
tuples.evidence_lens: land grant plates in great numbers, temple building programmes, and the accounts of foreign travellers

tuples.episode_object: the Delhi sultanate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain, the Deccan and the frontier across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a military slave elite converting conquest into administration, repeatedly overthrown by its own generals and never displaced as an institution
tuples.evidence_lens: court chronicles by insiders, coinage, revenue reform records, and the architecture of successive capitals

tuples.episode_object: the Mughal empire, told whole from a battle in the north to a pensioned emperor
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole subcontinent, the northwest and the Deccan across three and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a revenue system that measured and taxed land directly, which funded an enormous army and collapsed when the measuring stopped
tuples.evidence_lens: the imperial chronicles and memoirs, revenue manuals, land records, and European embassy accounts

tuples.episode_object: the Vijayanagara empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Deccan plateau, the southern rivers and both coasts across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a fortified capital and a horse-import dependency, which made an empire militarily strong and strategically hostage to the coast
tuples.evidence_lens: the ruined capital's excavation, temple inscriptions, and the accounts of Persian and Portuguese visitors

tuples.episode_object: the Bahmani and Deccan sultanates, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Deccan and its plateau forts across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a frontier state split by the quarrel between local-born and immigrant elites, which fractured it into five kingdoms
tuples.evidence_lens: court histories, fort architecture, Persian correspondence, and the coin issues of the successor states

tuples.episode_object: the Chola empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Kaveri delta, the southern coasts and the sea routes across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: temple-centred local self-government paired with an overseas naval reach, both recorded on the same temple walls
tuples.evidence_lens: the extraordinarily detailed temple wall inscriptions, bronze sculpture, and Southeast Asian inscriptions

tuples.episode_object: Bengal, told whole from delta kingdoms to a colonial province
tuples.time_place_scope: the delta, its rivers and its ports across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a shifting river delta that made agriculture rich and administration provisional, since the rivers moved the country underneath it
tuples.evidence_lens: land grant plates, river course studies, textile trade records, and the revenue settlements

tuples.episode_object: Gujarat and the western coast, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula, the gulf and the Indian Ocean routes across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a merchant coast whose bankers financed inland empires and whose ports outlived every dynasty that claimed them
tuples.evidence_lens: port customs records, merchant family papers, temple and mosque endowments, and shipping registers

tuples.episode_object: Rajasthan and the Rajput kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the desert, the hills and the fort country across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: clan kingdoms in defensible hill country, which survived every empire by negotiating subordination on terms they could live with
tuples.evidence_lens: bardic chronicles read cautiously, fort building phases, treaty documents, and land grant records

tuples.episode_object: Kashmir, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley and its passes across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a mountain valley with one entrance, rich enough to be worth taking and difficult enough to be governed at arm's length
tuples.evidence_lens: a rare local dynastic chronicle, temple and mosque architecture, and the revenue records of successive rulers

tuples.episode_object: the Sikh community and the Punjab state, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Punjab rivers and the northwest frontier across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a religious community that became an army and then a kingdom in two generations, and lost the kingdom in two more
tuples.evidence_lens: the community's own scripture and chronicles, court records, and the accounts of foreign officers in its service

tuples.episode_object: the Marathas, told whole from a hill fort to a lost confederacy
tuples.time_place_scope: the western Deccan, the ghats and eventually most of India across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: mobile light cavalry and a revenue claim on other people's provinces, which conquered an empire and never built a state
tuples.evidence_lens: court and revenue records in a regional script, campaign correspondence, and the accounts of rival powers

tuples.episode_object: Indian Ocean shipping and the coming of the Europeans, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western coast, the Red Sea, the gulf and the routes east across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the introduction of the armed merchantman into a sea where trade had not been armed, and what that single change decided
tuples.evidence_lens: port records, company correspondence, shipping registers, and the accounts of Asian merchants

tuples.episode_object: the Portuguese in India, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western coast and its fortified ports across four and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a chain of fortified ports rather than a territory, run as a licensing regime on other people's shipping
tuples.evidence_lens: the licence and customs records, fort archaeology, church registers, and the accounts of the licensed

tuples.episode_object: the East India Company's rise, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coastal factories, Bengal and the interior across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a trading company acquiring the right to collect a province's revenue, after which it never had to trade with its own money again
tuples.evidence_lens: company correspondence and accounts, revenue settlement records, and the parliamentary inquiries at home

tuples.episode_object: Indian textiles, told as the whole life of an industry
tuples.time_place_scope: the coasts, the weaving towns and the world markets across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a global manufacturing lead in cotton cloth, undone in two generations by mechanisation and tariffs elsewhere
tuples.evidence_lens: trade registers, weavers' contracts, tariff schedules, and the surviving cloth itself

tuples.episode_object: Indian temple building, told as one long practice
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole subcontinent across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: temples as landholders, employers and banks, so that building one was an economic act as much as a religious one
tuples.evidence_lens: foundation and endowment inscriptions, building sequences, and the account books of temple treasuries

tuples.episode_object: Persian in India, told as the whole life of a language of state
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern courts and the whole administration across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: an administrative language nobody grew up speaking, which created a class defined entirely by having learned it
tuples.evidence_lens: court chronicles and poetry, revenue documents, dictionaries and manuals, and the language replacement records

tuples.episode_object: Indian coinage and money, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the subcontinent's mints and markets across twenty-five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a silver currency in a country with almost no silver, so that money supply was set by the balance of trade with the world
tuples.evidence_lens: hoard analysis, mint records, exchange rate references in accounts, and the bullion import registers

tuples.episode_object: Indian famines and the monsoon, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole subcontinent across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: an agriculture entirely dependent on one seasonal rain, and the difference that relief policy makes between shortage and catastrophe
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicle famine notices, grain price series, relief works records, and rainfall reconstructions

tuples.episode_object: the end of Mughal India, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain, the Deccan and the coasts across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a centre that kept its prestige and lost its revenue, so that its own governors became independent while still using its name
tuples.evidence_lens: imperial and provincial records side by side, company correspondence, and the coinage that kept the emperor's name

coverage_profiles.subject: Central Asia and the Silk Road

tuples.episode_object: the Silk Road, told as the whole life of a route
tuples.time_place_scope: the roads between China, the oases, Iran and the Mediterranean across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a relay trade in which no merchant travelled the whole way, so the route existed as a chain of local markets rather than a road
tuples.evidence_lens: goods found far from their origin, way station records, manuscript finds, and the customs documents at each end

tuples.episode_object: Samarkand, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Zarafshan oasis across twenty-seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: an oasis city refounded on a new site after each destruction, because the water and the road stayed where they were
tuples.evidence_lens: successive city site excavation, wall paintings, endowment deeds, and the observatory records

tuples.episode_object: Bukhara, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Zarafshan oasis across twenty-five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a caravan city that became a centre of law and learning, exporting scholars for a thousand years as reliably as it exported cloth
tuples.evidence_lens: endowment deeds for colleges, biographical dictionaries of scholars, and the trade records of its markets

tuples.episode_object: Merv, told whole from an oasis to a dead city
tuples.time_place_scope: the Murghab delta oasis across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a city whose entire existence depended on a canal system, ended not by the sack itself but by the loss of the men who maintained it
tuples.evidence_lens: the succession of walled cities on one oasis, canal archaeology, and the accounts of the destruction

tuples.episode_object: Khwarezm, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Amu Darya delta and the inland sea across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: an irrigated delta state at the end of a river, wealthy, isolated, and destroyed twice by choosing the wrong quarrel
tuples.evidence_lens: fortress ruins in the desert, canal traces, coin sequences, and the chronicles of its conquerors

tuples.episode_object: the Tarim basin oasis kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the desert rim between the mountains and the sand across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: small oasis states surviving on transit and irrigation, preserved for us by the same dryness that eventually emptied them
tuples.evidence_lens: manuscripts in a dozen languages, cave temple painting, and the abandoned settlements themselves

tuples.episode_object: the Uyghur khaganates and the Turkic west, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Mongolian plateau and the Tarim basin across eleven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a steppe people who settled into oasis towns and changed religion twice, both times for reasons that were partly commercial
tuples.evidence_lens: manuscripts in several religions, city excavation, and the annals of the Chinese neighbour

tuples.episode_object: the Samanid state, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Oxus country and eastern Iran across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a provincial dynasty that revived a literary language and trained the slave soldiers who would replace it
tuples.evidence_lens: court poetry and its patronage record, coin issues, and the geographical writings of the period

tuples.episode_object: the Seljuk empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Iran, Mesopotamia, Anatolia and the steppe frontier across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a nomad dynasty ruling through Persian bureaucrats, which held together as long as one vizier's system did
tuples.evidence_lens: a famous book of government written by that vizier, chronicles, endowment deeds, and coin sequences

tuples.episode_object: the Karakhanids and the Islamisation of the Turks, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Tian Shan valleys and the oases across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the conversion of a steppe confederation, which reoriented an entire region's law, script and trade partners within a century
tuples.evidence_lens: the first Turkic Islamic literature, mausoleum architecture, and the coin issues of joint rulers

tuples.episode_object: the Khwarezmshahs and the Mongol catastrophe, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Oxus, the plateau and the roads east across a century
tuples.mechanism: a state that made an enemy of a neighbour it did not understand, and the demographic damage a punitive campaign can do
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicles from the survivors, canal and city destruction archaeology, and the tax records afterwards

tuples.episode_object: the Timurid renaissance, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Central Asia, Khorasan and the eastern plateau across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a conquest fortune spent on architecture, astronomy and books by heirs who could not defend what they had inherited
tuples.evidence_lens: the buildings and their inscriptions, the observatory's star catalogue, manuscript colophons, and court memoirs

tuples.episode_object: the Uzbek khanates, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the oases between the Oxus and the Syr Darya across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: three oasis khanates permanently at war with each other, which made the whole region easy to take once a modern army arrived
tuples.evidence_lens: chancery documents, endowment deeds, Russian embassy reports, and the slave market records

tuples.episode_object: the caravan trade's decline, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the roads from China to the Mediterranean across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the substitution of sea freight for land freight, which did not close the roads but made them local again
tuples.evidence_lens: shipping tonnage figures against caravan records, customs receipts, and the shrinking of caravanserai networks

tuples.episode_object: Buddhism in Central Asia, told from arrival to disappearance
tuples.time_place_scope: the oases, the mountains and the routes east across fifteen centuries
