tuples.mechanism: a religion carried by merchants and monks along one road, which vanished from its corridor while flourishing at both ends
tuples.evidence_lens: cave temple sequences, manuscript caches, monastery excavation, and the accounts of pilgrims passing through

tuples.episode_object: Manichaeism and the lost religions of the road, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: from Mesopotamia to the Tarim basin and China across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a religion designed for translation into every culture it met, which made it portable and left it with no home to defend
tuples.evidence_lens: manuscript fragments in several scripts, wall paintings, and the polemics of the religions that displaced it

tuples.episode_object: Central Asian metals, horses and slaves, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the steppe, the oases and the settled empires around them across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: three exports that settled empires could not do without, and the political leverage that dependency produced
tuples.evidence_lens: trade records at both ends, horse procurement documents, market tax registers, and legal texts on status

tuples.episode_object: the Russian conquest of Central Asia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the steppe, the oases and the mountain frontier across half a century
tuples.mechanism: the replacement of caravan politics by railway logistics, after which distance stopped protecting anybody
tuples.evidence_lens: military campaign records, railway construction files, treaty texts, and the local chronicles of the conquered

tuples.episode_object: Central Asian irrigation, told as one very long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the Amu Darya, Syr Darya and Zarafshan basins across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: a hydraulic society in which the canal network is the state, and every conquest is judged by whether it maintained the ditches
tuples.evidence_lens: canal archaeology, water allocation documents, agricultural tax records, and satellite mapping of old channels

tuples.episode_object: the Central Asian manuscript finds, told as the whole life of a discovery
tuples.time_place_scope: the desert oases, the cave libraries and the museums abroad across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: the recovery of a dozen lost languages from one dry region, and the dispersal of that record across four continents
tuples.evidence_lens: expedition journals, museum acquisition registers, and the conservation and decipherment record

tuples.episode_object: the Arab conquests, told whole from the first raids to the last frontier
tuples.time_place_scope: Arabia, the Levant, Iran, Egypt, north Africa and Iberia across a century
tuples.mechanism: two exhausted empires and one mobile army, which explains the speed better than any account of either faith or tactics
tuples.evidence_lens: later chronicles written from oral report, papyri and inscriptions from the conquered provinces, and coin overstrikes

tuples.episode_object: the Rashidun caliphate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Arabia and the newly conquered provinces across thirty years
tuples.mechanism: succession by consultation without a rule for it, which produced a civil war that has organised the religion ever since
tuples.evidence_lens: the earliest surviving documents and coins, and later narrative traditions carefully weighed for partisanship

tuples.episode_object: the Umayyad caliphate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: from Iberia to the Oxus, governed from Syria, across ninety years
tuples.mechanism: an Arab ruling caste taxing non-Arab converts as if they had not converted, which built the coalition that destroyed it
tuples.evidence_lens: administrative papyri, the earliest Islamic coinage and inscriptions, and the histories written by their successors

tuples.episode_object: Damascus as a capital, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Syrian oasis and its road network across five millennia
tuples.mechanism: an inland oasis on the desert road, always the natural capital of Syria and never a naval or trading power in its own right
tuples.evidence_lens: the great mosque's building phases, administrative papyri, and the accounts of the successive conquests

tuples.episode_object: the Abbasid caliphate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq, Iran, the Levant and the shrinking provinces across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a caliphate that became a legitimating office rather than a government, useful to the soldiers who controlled it
tuples.evidence_lens: court chronicles, administrative manuals, the correspondence of viziers, and the coin evidence of real power

tuples.episode_object: Baghdad, told whole from a round city to a sacked capital
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Tigris across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a capital founded on a canal junction with no defensible position, which relied on the empire's strength for its own safety
tuples.evidence_lens: the descriptions of its plan, market and hospital records, and the accounts of the final siege

tuples.episode_object: Islamic law, told as one long institutional life
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole Islamic world across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: law developed by private scholars rather than by the state, which made it independent of rulers and slow to change
tuples.evidence_lens: the founding legal compendia, court records, legal opinions in enormous numbers, and endowment deeds

tuples.episode_object: the translation movement, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Baghdad, the eastern provinces and the older centres of learning across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: state and private patronage of translation on a scale that moved a whole scientific corpus from one language into another
tuples.evidence_lens: translation colophons, library catalogues, patron records, and the surviving translated texts themselves

tuples.episode_object: the Fatimid caliphate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: north Africa, Egypt, the Levant and the Red Sea across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a rival caliphate that built a new capital and a trade empire and was ended by the general it hired to defend it
tuples.evidence_lens: the state chancery documents, a merchant community's discarded papers, and the buildings of the new capital

tuples.episode_object: Cairo, told as the whole life of a city
tuples.time_place_scope: the head of the delta across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a capital founded beside an older city and repeatedly refounded next door, so that its plan records every dynasty in sequence
tuples.evidence_lens: endowment deeds for its buildings, market inspection manuals, plague records, and traveller descriptions

tuples.episode_object: the Abbasid provinces and their independence, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Iran, Egypt, north Africa and Central Asia across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the fiscal logic of a governor who stops remitting revenue, which is how almost every successor dynasty began
tuples.evidence_lens: coin issues bearing local names, tribute records, and the correspondence between capital and province

tuples.episode_object: the Mamluk sultanate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Egypt, the Levant and the Red Sea across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a state governed by imported military slaves who could not inherit, so that power was re-competed every generation
tuples.evidence_lens: chancery documents, endowment deeds, chronicles by insiders, and the architecture of the sultans

tuples.episode_object: the Crusader states, told whole from first arrival to last port
tuples.time_place_scope: the Levantine coast and its hinterland across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: colonial settler states dependent on annual reinforcement from abroad, which failed the moment that reinforcement stopped
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicles from three sides, castle archaeology, treaty texts, and the property records of the settlers

tuples.episode_object: the Red Sea and Indian Ocean trade under the caliphates, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Red Sea, the gulf and the routes to India and China across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a merchant network operating under several states at once through shared law and credit rather than through any flag
tuples.evidence_lens: a synagogue storeroom of merchant letters, port customs records, shipwrecks, and legal opinions on partnership

tuples.episode_object: Islamic science and medicine, told as one long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the cities from Iberia to Central Asia across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: hospitals, observatories and libraries funded by permanent endowments, which outlived the dynasties that founded them
tuples.evidence_lens: endowment deeds, hospital records, dated astronomical tables, and manuscript transmission chains

tuples.episode_object: the Islamic slave trade, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Sahara, the Indian Ocean, the Caucasus and the Mediterranean across twelve centuries
tuples.mechanism: the recruitment of soldiers and administrators from outside the community, which repeatedly put the state in the hands of the recruited
tuples.evidence_lens: market tax records, legal texts on status, military register documents, and the accounts of the trading routes

tuples.episode_object: Mecca and Medina as institutions, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western Arabian hills and the pilgrimage roads across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: an annual pilgrimage as an economic and political system, which made whoever protected the road the leading Muslim ruler
tuples.evidence_lens: pilgrimage road engineering, endowment records, the accounts of pilgrims, and the correspondence over protection

tuples.episode_object: Arabic, told as the whole life of a language
tuples.time_place_scope: Arabia, the conquered provinces and the wider world across sixteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a language spread by administration rather than by settlement, which replaced several older languages within three centuries
tuples.evidence_lens: the papyrus record of the administrative switch, inscriptions, grammatical works, and the surviving minority languages

tuples.episode_object: the Zanj revolt and the Iraqi marshes, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the salt flats and marshes of southern Iraq across fifteen years and their aftermath
tuples.mechanism: a plantation labour system in a hostile landscape, and the fifteen-year rebellion that ended the experiment permanently
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicle accounts, the land reclamation records, and the archaeology of the salt flats

tuples.episode_object: the end of the caliphate as a power, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq, Egypt and the wider Islamic world across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the separation of religious legitimacy from military power, and the long afterlife of an office with no army
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles of the sack, the records of the shadow caliphate in exile, and the claims of later sultans

tuples.episode_object: al-Andalus, told whole from a landing to a surrender
tuples.time_place_scope: the Iberian peninsula and its frontier across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: a frontier society whose borders moved for eight hundred years, so that every institution was built for a provisional situation
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicles from both sides, treaty and capitulation texts, tax registers, and the archaeology of frontier castles

tuples.episode_object: Cordoba, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Guadalquivir valley across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a capital whose greatness rested on one caliphate's revenue and irrigation, and which never recovered when both were lost
tuples.evidence_lens: the great mosque's building phases, the palace city excavation, library catalogues, and market inspection manuals

tuples.episode_object: the Umayyad emirate and caliphate of the west, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula and the north African coast across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a dynasty in exile founding a rival caliphate, which bought legitimacy with architecture and lost it to its own army
tuples.evidence_lens: coin issues, court chronicles, palace excavation, and the accounts of embassies from northern kingdoms

tuples.episode_object: the taifa kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula's cities and their hinterlands across a century
tuples.mechanism: the fragmentation of a caliphate into city states that bought peace with tribute, which financed the neighbours who ended them
tuples.evidence_lens: tribute agreements, court poetry, coin debasement evidence, and the chronicles of the northern kingdoms

tuples.episode_object: the Almoravids, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Sahara, Morocco and southern Iberia across a century
tuples.mechanism: a desert reform movement that took two countries and could not govern a city society it disapproved of
tuples.evidence_lens: the movement's own legal writings, coin issues, capital city excavation, and hostile Andalusi accounts

tuples.episode_object: the Almohads, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Maghreb and southern Iberia across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a doctrinal empire held by a single lineage's religious claim, which had no answer to one lost battle
tuples.evidence_lens: the movement's letters and doctrine, monumental architecture, and the chronicles of both its subjects and enemies

tuples.episode_object: Granada and the Nasrid kingdom, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southeastern mountains and the coast across two and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: a tributary kingdom surviving in mountains by paying its neighbour and being useful to its neighbour's rivals
tuples.evidence_lens: the palace complex and its inscriptions, tribute treaties, silk trade records, and the surrender terms

tuples.episode_object: the Christian reconquest, told as one very long process
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole peninsula across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: a slow frontier movement driven by settlement charters and land hunger rather than by any continuous religious campaign
tuples.evidence_lens: settlement charters, repartition registers, military order records, and frontier castle sequences

tuples.episode_object: the Mozarabs and Mudejars, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula's cities and countryside across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: the legal category of the tolerated minority on both sides of a frontier, and how completely it eventually failed on both
tuples.evidence_lens: capitulation agreements, poll tax records, community court documents, and the expulsion decrees

tuples.episode_object: Sephardi Jewish Iberia, told whole from arrival to expulsion and diaspora
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula and the Mediterranean diaspora across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a community whose usefulness to rulers was also its exposure, and which reconstituted itself across a sea within one generation
tuples.evidence_lens: community responsa, tax registers, the expulsion edict, and the records of the receiving communities

tuples.episode_object: Andalusi agriculture and irrigation, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern river valleys and the huertas across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: the introduction of new crops and irrigation from the east, which changed what the peninsula could grow and feed
tuples.evidence_lens: agricultural manuals, irrigation court records that still function, crop distribution, and land survey documents

tuples.episode_object: Andalusi learning, told as one long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula's cities and their libraries across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a scholarly culture built on huge private libraries, dispersed and partly saved by translation into another language
tuples.evidence_lens: library catalogues, translation records, manuscript survivals, and the biographies of scholars

tuples.episode_object: Morocco and the Moroccan dynasties, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Atlas, the Atlantic plains and the Saharan approaches across thirteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a country repeatedly unified by movements from its margins, and the recurring difficulty of taxing mountains
tuples.evidence_lens: dynastic chronicles, endowment deeds, coin issues, and the accounts of European and Ottoman envoys

tuples.episode_object: Fez and the Moroccan cities, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern valleys and the routes across the mountains across twelve centuries
tuples.mechanism: an inland city living on crafts, learning and the caravan road, which survived every dynasty by not depending on any
tuples.evidence_lens: guild and market records, college endowment deeds, and the chronicles of successive rulers

tuples.episode_object: Ifriqiya and Tunisia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Maghreb coast and its plains across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: the most agriculturally productive part of the Maghreb, and therefore the part every outside power wanted to govern directly
tuples.evidence_lens: tax and land records, port customs registers, and the chronicles of successive dynasties

tuples.episode_object: the Berber peoples, told as one very long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the Maghreb, the Atlas and the Sahara across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a language and society that absorbed every conquest at the coast and persisted in the mountains and the desert
tuples.evidence_lens: inscriptions in an old script, language distribution, tribal genealogies, and the administrative records of conquerors

tuples.episode_object: the trans-Saharan trade, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the desert routes between the Maghreb and the Sahel across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: gold moving north and salt moving south across a desert, an exchange that funded both ends and depended on camels and wells
tuples.evidence_lens: customs records at both ends, caravan itineraries, coin metal analysis, and the archaeology of desert towns

tuples.episode_object: the Barbary corsair states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the north African coast and the western Mediterranean across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: state-licensed raiding as a revenue model, which functioned as long as the ransom trade was cheaper than a naval campaign
tuples.evidence_lens: captive and ransom registers, treaty texts, consular correspondence, and the harbour fortification records

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman Maghreb, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coast from Egypt to Morocco across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: provinces nominally imperial and practically independent, governed by a garrison that elected its own rulers
tuples.evidence_lens: provincial chancery records, imperial correspondence, garrison registers, and European consular reports

tuples.episode_object: the Maghreb under European rule, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coastal plains, the mountains and the Sahara across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: settler colonisation of the best farmland, which reorganised a whole society around land title and never resolved it
tuples.evidence_lens: land registration records, settlement statistics, military reports, and the local press of the period

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman empire, told whole from a frontier band to a partition
tuples.time_place_scope: Anatolia, the Balkans, the Levant, Egypt, north Africa and the Black Sea across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a frontier warband that turned itself into a bureaucratic empire by recruiting and training its own elite from outside itself
tuples.evidence_lens: the imperial council registers, tax survey books, chancery correspondence, and the accounts of foreign residents

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman beginnings, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: northwestern Anatolia and the Marmara shore across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a small frontier principality that grew by absorbing rivals through marriage and hire rather than by destroying them
tuples.evidence_lens: later chronicles written with hindsight, early endowment deeds, coin issues, and frontier fortress archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the conquest of Constantinople and its aftermath, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the straits, the city and the surrounding provinces across a century
tuples.mechanism: the repopulation of a captured capital by compulsory resettlement, which rebuilt a city and reorganised an empire's economy
tuples.evidence_lens: the resettlement registers, the tax surveys of the new quarters, and the accounts of both besiegers and besieged

tuples.episode_object: Istanbul as an Ottoman city, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the two shores of the straits across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: provisioning a capital of half a million people from the Black Sea and Egypt, an operation that dictated foreign policy
tuples.evidence_lens: grain and meat supply records, guild registers, fire and plague accounts, and endowment deeds for its quarters

tuples.episode_object: the devshirme and the janissaries, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Balkans, the capital and the frontiers across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a slave-recruited standing army that became a hereditary urban interest group, and finally a veto on every reform
tuples.evidence_lens: levy registers, pay rolls, guild and barracks records, and the accounts of the corps' abolition

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman land and tax system, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Anatolia, the Balkans and the Arab provinces across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: cavalry paid in the revenue of assigned villages, which worked while war paid for itself and failed when it stopped
tuples.evidence_lens: the detailed provincial survey books, timar registers, and the tax farming contracts that replaced them

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman Balkans, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula from the Danube to the Aegean across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: government through religious communities rather than territories, which preserved local difference and prepared the eventual partition
tuples.evidence_lens: community court records, poll tax registers, monastery archives, and the provincial correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Ottoman Egypt, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Nile valley, the delta and the Red Sea across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a province governed through the very military caste the empire had conquered, which is why it separated so easily
tuples.evidence_lens: provincial treasury records, grain shipment accounts, endowment deeds, and the correspondence with the capital

tuples.episode_object: Ottoman Syria and the Arab provinces, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Levant, the desert and the pilgrimage road across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: an empire whose main obligation in the region was to move and protect the annual pilgrimage caravan
tuples.evidence_lens: pilgrimage road accounts, provincial court registers, tax farming contracts, and consular reports

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman navy and the Mediterranean, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole Mediterranean and the Red Sea across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a galley fleet built and manned by state arsenals, dominant in an enclosed sea and irrelevant beyond it
tuples.evidence_lens: arsenal construction records, campaign accounts, captive registers, and the treaties after each war

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman-Habsburg frontier, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Hungarian plain, Croatia and the Danube across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a permanently militarised border where raiding was normal and full war episodic, and which depopulated the ground between
tuples.evidence_lens: frontier fortress records from both sides, truce agreements, and the settlement archaeology of the border zone

tuples.episode_object: Ottoman Hungary, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Danube plain and its fortresses across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a province held as a military march rather than developed, which left it emptier at the end than at the beginning
tuples.evidence_lens: tax surveys, garrison registers, and the reconquest records of the successor administration

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman guilds and urban economy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the empire's cities across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: price-regulated guilds guaranteeing supply and quality, which stabilised cities and slowed every kind of change
tuples.evidence_lens: market inspection registers, guild charters, price ceiling edicts, and court disputes between guilds

tuples.episode_object: Ottoman Christians and Jews, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the empire's cities and provinces across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a legal order that guaranteed communal autonomy and permanent legal inequality in the same arrangement
tuples.evidence_lens: community court records, poll tax registers, petitions to the imperial council, and communal endowment deeds

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman court and its women, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the palace on the point and the imperial household across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a household in which succession, marriage and faction were the same subject, and the mother of a sultan held real office
tuples.evidence_lens: endowment deeds by royal women, household registers, ambassadorial reports, and building patronage records

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman reform century, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole empire and its new institutions across eighty years
tuples.mechanism: a state reforming itself into a European template while borrowing from Europe to pay for it, and defaulting on both
tuples.evidence_lens: reform edicts, school and army records, budget documents, debt administration files, and the periodical press

tuples.episode_object: Ottoman Iraq and the gulf frontier, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Mesopotamia, the marshes and the gulf coast across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a distant province contested with a rival empire, governed through tribal confederations that neither side could tax
tuples.evidence_lens: provincial registers, boundary commission records, tribal correspondence, and river navigation reports

tuples.episode_object: the Ottoman Black Sea, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole Black Sea rim and its rivers across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a closed imperial lake supplying the capital with grain and captives, opened by treaty and never closed again
tuples.evidence_lens: customs registers, grain shipment records, treaty texts, and the accounts of the northern trading ports

tuples.episode_object: Ottoman coffee, told as the whole life of a commodity
tuples.time_place_scope: Yemen, the Red Sea, the empire's cities and beyond across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a drink that created a new kind of public space, banned repeatedly for exactly that reason and taxed instead
tuples.evidence_lens: market and customs records, prohibition edicts, coffee house regulations, and travellers' descriptions

tuples.episode_object: the end of the Ottoman empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Anatolia, the Arab provinces and the Balkans across a century
tuples.mechanism: an empire dismantled at its edges by nationalism and at its centre by debt, and finally partitioned by a war it entered late
tuples.evidence_lens: debt administration records, the treaties of partition, army records, and the parliamentary debates

coverage_profiles.subject: Arabia and the gulf, told whole

tuples.episode_object: the Arabian peninsula, told whole from the incense kingdoms to the oil century
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole peninsula, its coasts and its deserts across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a desert interior linked by a few trade commodities to the outside world, whose politics were set by whichever commodity mattered
tuples.evidence_lens: south Arabian inscriptions, caravan route archaeology, chronicles of neighbours, and the later concession records

tuples.episode_object: the south Arabian kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands and wadis of the southwest across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: dam and terrace irrigation supporting a dense highland population, and the collapse that follows when a dam is not repaired
tuples.evidence_lens: monumental inscriptions, the great dam's remains, terrace archaeology, and the incense trade records

tuples.episode_object: the incense road, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western Arabian caravan route from the south to the Levant across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a luxury trade in two resins that funded a chain of desert cities and evaporated when religious practice changed
tuples.evidence_lens: caravan station excavation, tariff inscriptions, temple consumption records, and the accounts of classical geographers

tuples.episode_object: the Nabataeans, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northwest Arabian desert, the Negev and the Hejaz across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a caravan people who mastered desert water storage, which is what let them hold a route nobody else could cross
tuples.evidence_lens: rock-cut tombs and their inscriptions, cistern and dam engineering, and the annexation records of Rome

tuples.episode_object: pre-Islamic Arabia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula, its oases and its frontiers across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: tribal confederations acting as buffer clients for two empires, and what happened when both empires stopped paying
tuples.evidence_lens: poetry preserved orally and written later, inscriptions, and the frontier records of two empires

tuples.episode_object: Yemen, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the coast and the island approaches across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a country of highland terraces and coastal ports, always rich enough to be invaded and too mountainous to be held
tuples.evidence_lens: inscriptions, terrace and dam remains, port customs records, and the chronicles of successive occupiers

tuples.episode_object: Oman and the Ibadi imamate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the mountains, the coast and the Indian Ocean across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: an elected religious leadership in the mountains beside a commercial sultanate on the coast, permanently in tension
tuples.evidence_lens: imamate election records, falaj irrigation documents, shipping registers, and treaty correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Omani east Africa, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the gulf, the Indian Ocean and the east African coast across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: an Arabian dynasty moving its capital to Africa to be closer to its revenue, and losing Arabia in the process
tuples.evidence_lens: customs records at both ends, treaty texts, plantation and caravan documents, and consular reports

tuples.episode_object: the gulf pearling economy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the gulf shores and banks across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: a seasonal diving industry financed by advances against a future catch, which bound whole coastal populations in debt
tuples.evidence_lens: diving crew contracts, merchant ledgers, customs records, and the collapse evidence after cultured pearls

tuples.episode_object: Bahrain and Dilmun, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island and the gulf shore across five millennia
tuples.mechanism: an island with fresh springs in a salt sea, which made it a trading centre for four thousand years without interruption
tuples.evidence_lens: cuneiform trade records, the enormous burial mound fields, temple excavation, and later customs registers

tuples.episode_object: the Hejaz and the pilgrimage economy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western hills, the ports and the caravan roads across fourteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a region whose entire economy was one annual arrival, and whose politics were therefore made elsewhere
tuples.evidence_lens: pilgrimage road engineering, endowment records, port accounts, and the correspondence over protection rights

tuples.episode_object: Najd and the interior, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central plateau, its oases and its deserts across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: an interior of oasis towns and tribal confederations, unified only when a religious movement and a family combined
tuples.evidence_lens: oasis chronicles, the movement's own writings, tribal genealogies, and the reports of foreign travellers

tuples.episode_object: the Arabian camel and the caravan, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula's deserts and the routes across them across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a pack animal that made desert crossing routine, which turned an obstacle into the shortest road between two seas
tuples.evidence_lens: saddle technology evidence, caravan route surveys, animal remains, and the freight records of the routes

tuples.episode_object: Arabia and the sea to India, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Arabian coasts, the gulf and the Indian Ocean across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: monsoon sailing between two coasts that made Arabian ports the middlemen for everything moving between east and west
tuples.evidence_lens: sailing directions, port excavation, wreck cargoes, and the merchant letters of the ocean trade

tuples.episode_object: the Red Sea, told as the whole life of a corridor
tuples.time_place_scope: the sea between Africa and Arabia and its two ends across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: a difficult sea with a canal at one end, which alternated between the world's busiest route and an expensive detour
tuples.evidence_lens: port archaeology at both ends, navigation hazards described in pilots, canal records, and customs registers

tuples.episode_object: Arabian Jews and Christians, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the oases, the highlands and the coasts across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: communities that were central to the peninsula's trade and learning before the seventh century and marginal after it
tuples.evidence_lens: inscriptions, community records, chronicles of persecution and protection, and the later emigration registers

tuples.episode_object: the Wahhabi movement and the first Saudi state, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central plateau and the peninsula across a century
tuples.mechanism: an alliance between a religious reform movement and a ruling family, in which each supplied what the other lacked
tuples.evidence_lens: the movement's own treatises, Ottoman campaign records, chronicles from the oases, and European traveller accounts

tuples.episode_object: the gulf under British treaties, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the gulf coast, its ports and its sheikhdoms across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a system of maritime truces that froze the political map of a coast for a hundred and fifty years
tuples.evidence_lens: the treaty texts, political residency files, naval patrol records, and the ruler correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Arabian oil, told from the first concession to the last frontier settlement
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern province, the gulf and the desert interior across a century
tuples.mechanism: the arrival of enormous state revenue in societies with almost no administrative apparatus to spend it
tuples.evidence_lens: concession agreements, geological survey records, production statistics, and the boundary arbitration files

tuples.episode_object: the Arabian deserts as a subject, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the great sand seas and the gravel plains across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: the practical limits of a landscape without water, which decided every route, every frontier and every settlement on the peninsula
tuples.evidence_lens: well and route surveys, rock art and inscriptions, exploration journals, and the satellite mapping of palaeochannels

tuples.episode_object: Ghana, Mali and Songhai, told as one whole succession
tuples.time_place_scope: the Sahel between the desert and the forest across nine centuries
tuples.mechanism: control of the point where the desert trade met the river, a position that made three empires in succession and destroyed each
tuples.evidence_lens: Arabic geographies and chronicles, the local town chronicles, oral tradition, and the archaeology of the river towns

tuples.episode_object: the empire of Ghana, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western Sahel and the desert edge across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a state taxing gold and salt in transit without producing either, which is a strong position until the route shifts
tuples.evidence_lens: the accounts of Arab geographers, the excavation of a desert capital, and the gold field surveys

tuples.episode_object: the Mali empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the upper Niger, the Sahel and the gold country across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: an empire built on a river highway and a gold field, held together by a court that travelled and by oral constitution
tuples.evidence_lens: an oral epic tradition, Arab travellers' eyewitness accounts, coin metal analysis, and river town archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the Songhai empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Niger bend, the desert ports and the Sahel across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a river empire with a fleet and a professional army, ended by a small force with firearms crossing a desert
tuples.evidence_lens: the Timbuktu chronicles, the invasion accounts from both sides, and the manuscript libraries of the river cities

tuples.episode_object: Timbuktu and the river cities, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Niger bend and the desert edge across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: a scholarly city where the caravan met the canoe, whose libraries outlived every state that governed it
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving manuscript collections, endowment records, chronicles, and the accounts of foreign visitors

tuples.episode_object: Jenne-jeno and the earliest West African urbanism, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the inland delta of the Niger across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a city that grew without a palace or a wall, which upset the assumption that urbanism requires a king
tuples.evidence_lens: excavation of the mound complexes, the absence of monumental structures, and the trade goods in ordinary houses

tuples.episode_object: the Hausa city-states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the savannah south of the Sahara across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: walled trading cities each strong enough to survive and none strong enough to unify, until a religious movement did it
tuples.evidence_lens: city chronicles, wall archaeology, trade and craft records, and the writings of the reform movement

tuples.episode_object: the Sokoto caliphate, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the savannah from the Niger to Lake Chad across a century
tuples.mechanism: a scholarly reform movement that became the largest state in the region and governed it through appointed emirs
tuples.evidence_lens: the founders' own extensive writings, emirate records, tax documents, and the accounts of European travellers

tuples.episode_object: Kanem-Bornu, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Lake Chad basin and the desert routes north across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: one dynasty ruling either side of a lake for a thousand years by moving its capital when the lake and the trade moved
tuples.evidence_lens: royal chronicles, correspondence with north African states, and the archaeology of the successive capitals

tuples.episode_object: the Asante empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the forest and the gold country of the interior across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a forest state that centralised gold and tribute through a single office and a road system into the interior
tuples.evidence_lens: state treasury records, the accounts of British missions, oral constitutional tradition, and the road surveys

tuples.episode_object: Benin and the forest kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the forest west of the Niger across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a walled forest capital with a court art tradition that recorded its own political history in metal
tuples.evidence_lens: the cast plaques read as a chronicle, the enormous earthwork system, and the accounts of European visitors

tuples.episode_object: Ife and the Yoruba city-states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the forest and its edge in the southwest across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a religious centre acknowledged by cities that never obeyed it politically, which is a durable arrangement and an invisible one
tuples.evidence_lens: the naturalistic sculpture, excavation of the pavements and shrines, oral dynastic tradition, and city wall surveys

tuples.episode_object: Oyo, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the savannah north of the forest across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a cavalry empire on the grassland edge, which could not follow its trade into the forest where horses could not live
tuples.evidence_lens: oral tradition recorded in the nineteenth century, trade records at the coast, and the accounts of visitors

tuples.episode_object: Dahomey, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coastal plain and the plateau behind it across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a centralised kingdom whose revenue was the coastal trade, and whose institutions were rebuilt around that single fact
tuples.evidence_lens: annual palace census records, European trading post accounts, and the kingdom's own recorded traditions

tuples.episode_object: the Senegambian states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the two river valleys and the coast across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: river kingdoms squeezed between desert raiders and coastal traders, which reorganised repeatedly around whichever pressed harder
tuples.evidence_lens: river trading post records, oral chronicles, Portuguese and French accounts, and archaeological survey

tuples.episode_object: the trans-Atlantic slave trade seen from West Africa, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coast from Senegal to Angola and the interior behind it across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: an export trade in people that reorganised inland politics around raiding, and left the coast dependent on it
tuples.evidence_lens: shipping registers, trading post accounts, African state records, and the demographic reconstructions

tuples.episode_object: West African gold, told as the whole life of a commodity
tuples.time_place_scope: the forest and savannah gold fields and the routes north across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a metal mined in one place and coined in another, so that African production set European money supply for centuries
tuples.evidence_lens: mint records in the north, metal isotope analysis, trade accounts, and mining site archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Islamic learning in West Africa, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Sahel cities, the desert and the savannah across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: a manuscript culture in the Sahel that copied, taught and wrote for eight centuries with almost no printing
tuples.evidence_lens: surviving manuscript libraries, teaching chains recorded in biographies, and endowment documents

tuples.episode_object: the Sahel's environment, told as one long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the belt between the desert and the savannah across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a moving climatic frontier which shifted settlement and empire northward and southward with the rains
tuples.evidence_lens: lake sediment cores, settlement abandonment sequences, famine chronicles, and the pastoral migration records

tuples.episode_object: West Africa under colonial rule, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coast, the savannah and the Sahel across eighty years
tuples.mechanism: administration through existing rulers wherever they existed and invented ones where they did not, on borders drawn abroad
tuples.evidence_lens: boundary commission files, native authority records, cash crop statistics, and the local press

coverage_profiles.subject: the Swahili coast and East Africa

tuples.episode_object: the Swahili coast, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the east African shore and its islands from Somalia to Mozambique across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a chain of stone towns facing the ocean rather than the interior, joined by a language and a monsoon and never by a state
tuples.evidence_lens: coral stone town archaeology, imported ceramics, town chronicles, and the accounts of ocean traders

tuples.episode_object: Kilwa, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Swahili coast and the Mozambique channel across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: a town that controlled the outlet of a gold trade it did not produce, and declined precisely when a rival controlled the source
tuples.evidence_lens: the town's own chronicle, palace and mosque excavation, coin issues, and Portuguese conquest accounts

tuples.episode_object: Zanzibar and Pemba, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the islands off the east African coast across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: islands close enough to trade with the mainland and far enough to be safe, which is the classic entrepot position
tuples.evidence_lens: customs records, plantation registers, consular reports, and the archaeology of the stone town

tuples.episode_object: Mogadishu and the Benadir coast, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Somali coast and its hinterland across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a coast whose trade depended on pastoral hinterland supply, so that its fortunes tracked the rains inland
tuples.evidence_lens: town chronicles, inscriptions in the mosques, Chinese and Arab trade notices, and hinterland survey

tuples.episode_object: Great Zimbabwe and the plateau states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau between the Zambezi and the Limpopo across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: cattle wealth plus gold export, which built a stone capital and moved when the pasture and the trade route moved
tuples.evidence_lens: the stone enclosures themselves, imported goods in the middens, and cattle isotope and pasture studies

tuples.episode_object: Mapungubwe and the Limpopo, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the confluence country of the Limpopo across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the emergence of hereditary rank visible archaeologically as physical separation, a hill for the ruler and a valley for the rest
tuples.evidence_lens: the settlement layout, elite burials with gold objects, and the trade goods from the coast

tuples.episode_object: the Mutapa state, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plateau and the Zambezi valley across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a gold-exporting kingdom that admitted foreign traders inland and lost control of its own succession to them
tuples.evidence_lens: Portuguese mission and trade records, the kingdom's own tradition, and the archaeology of the trading fairs

tuples.episode_object: the Zambezi valley and the prazos, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the river valley and its hinterland across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: land grants to private holders in a place with no state capacity, which produced private armies rather than estates
tuples.evidence_lens: grant documents, mission records, river trading post accounts, and the archaeology of the estates

tuples.episode_object: the Great Lakes kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lakes, the highlands and their pastures across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: cattle clientage as the basic political relationship, in which the loan of a cow is the loan of a status
tuples.evidence_lens: oral dynastic traditions recorded later, earthwork capital archaeology, and the reports of the first outsiders

tuples.episode_object: Buganda, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern lakeshore and its hinterland across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom of appointed chiefs rather than hereditary ones, which made the court unusually strong and unusually factional
tuples.evidence_lens: royal oral chronicles, missionary and explorer accounts, road and capital archaeology, and court correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Ethiopia's neighbours and the Horn's sultanates, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern lowlands, the Red Sea coast and the Ogaden across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: trading sultanates on the caravan roads to the highlands, permanently at war with the highland empire above them
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicles from both sides, town excavation, and the accounts of Red Sea traders

tuples.episode_object: the east African interior trade routes, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the routes from the coast to the lakes across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: caravan routes into the interior organised by coastal financiers, which changed inland politics faster than anything before
tuples.evidence_lens: caravan account books, mission station records, explorer journals, and the archaeology of route stations

tuples.episode_object: the Indian Ocean monsoon system, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole ocean from Africa to India and beyond across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a wind that reverses twice a year, which made a round trip a fixed annual calendar rather than a journey
tuples.evidence_lens: sailing directions, port arrival records, ship construction evidence, and the seasonal customs registers

tuples.episode_object: east African ivory, told as the whole life of a trade
tuples.time_place_scope: the interior, the coast and the markets in Asia and Europe across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a commodity whose supply moved steadily inland as the near sources were exhausted, dragging the trade routes with it
tuples.evidence_lens: customs and shipping records, carving workshop evidence at the destinations, and elephant population reconstructions

tuples.episode_object: the east African slave trade, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the interior, the coast and the Indian Ocean markets across twelve centuries
tuples.mechanism: an export trade that turned inland raiding into a business and coastal plantations into its second market
tuples.evidence_lens: customs registers, plantation records, naval patrol reports, and the freed captives' own testimonies

tuples.episode_object: Swahili as a language and a culture, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coast, the islands and eventually the interior across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a coastal language that became the trade tongue of half a continent because it was nobody's exclusive property
tuples.evidence_lens: early manuscripts in Arabic script, poetry, loanword layers, and the missionary and colonial standardisation records

tuples.episode_object: Madagascar, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island and the channel across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: an island settled from across an ocean rather than from the nearby continent, which shaped its language and its farming
tuples.evidence_lens: linguistic evidence tying it to the far east, crop transfers, settlement archaeology, and later kingdom chronicles

tuples.episode_object: the Merina kingdom, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central highlands of Madagascar and the coasts across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a highland kingdom that unified an island by adopting writing, firearms and a bureaucracy within one generation
tuples.evidence_lens: the kingdom's own written records, mission school archives, and the accounts of foreign embassies

tuples.episode_object: the Comoros and the channel islands, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the islands between Africa and Madagascar across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: small island sultanates living on the channel traffic, too valuable to ignore and too small to defend themselves
tuples.evidence_lens: town archaeology, sultanate chronicles, and the records of the shipping that stopped there

tuples.episode_object: east Africa under colonial rule, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coast, the highlands and the lakes across seventy years
tuples.mechanism: railways built to reach the interior, which decided where the cities, the farms and the frontiers would be
tuples.evidence_lens: railway construction files, land alienation records, tax and labour registers, and mission archives

tuples.episode_object: Ethiopia, told whole from Aksum to the last emperor
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the Red Sea approaches and the lowlands across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a highland empire with its own script, church and calendar, which survived by being difficult to reach and hard to hold
tuples.evidence_lens: royal chronicles in a liturgical language, church manuscripts, stele and church archaeology, and foreign embassy accounts

tuples.episode_object: the kingdom of Aksum, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern highlands and the Red Sea coast across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: a highland kingdom with a Red Sea port, which minted its own gold and vanished from the record when the sea trade moved
tuples.evidence_lens: the stelae and their inscriptions, a gold and silver coinage, and the trade notices of Mediterranean writers

tuples.episode_object: Kush and Meroe, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Nile above the cataracts across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: an iron and trade kingdom that outlived its northern neighbour by a thousand years and wrote in a script still unread
tuples.evidence_lens: the pyramid fields, an undeciphered script, iron slag heaps, and the records of Egyptian and Roman contacts

tuples.episode_object: Christian Nubia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Nile between the cataracts across nine centuries
tuples.mechanism: three Christian kingdoms on a river that survived beside an Islamic empire for six centuries under a single treaty
tuples.evidence_lens: church wall painting, the treaty document, cathedral excavation, and the correspondence of bishops

tuples.episode_object: the Ethiopian church, told as one long institutional life
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the monasteries and the Holy Land across seventeen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a national church tied to a distant patriarchate by a single appointed bishop, which made every succession a foreign policy problem
tuples.evidence_lens: monastic libraries, the correspondence over episcopal appointment, church councils, and land grant charters

tuples.episode_object: Lalibela and the rock churches, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern highlands across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: churches cut down into the rock rather than built up from it, a technique that leaves no scaffolding and no quarry
tuples.evidence_lens: the churches themselves, their tool marks and hydrology, monastic tradition, and pilgrim accounts

tuples.episode_object: the Zagwe and Solomonic dynasties, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands and their shifting capitals across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a dynasty legitimated by a descent claim written into a book, and the political work that book did for six hundred years
tuples.evidence_lens: the dynastic epic itself, royal chronicles, land charters, and church painting programmes

tuples.episode_object: the Ethiopian moving capital, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland plateau across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a court that moved every few years because a stationary capital would eat its district bare, which is why there are so few ruins
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicle itineraries, deforestation evidence, church foundation dates, and the accounts of foreign visitors

tuples.episode_object: the wars of the sixteenth century and the highland recovery, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the eastern lowlands and the Red Sea across a century
tuples.mechanism: a highland empire nearly destroyed by a lowland sultanate with firearms, and rescued by a foreign expedition it then expelled
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicles from both sides, the accounts of the foreign expedition, and the church rebuilding records

tuples.episode_object: the Oromo migrations, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern and central highlands across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a pastoral expansion into an exhausted country, which reshaped the population of an empire from the inside
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicle notices, the age-grade system's own oral record, and the settlement and land tenure evidence

tuples.episode_object: Ethiopian manuscripts and the Ge'ez tradition, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the monasteries and the highland churches across seventeen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a manuscript culture in a liturgical language, copied by monasteries continuously from late antiquity to the present
tuples.evidence_lens: the manuscripts themselves and their colophons, scriptorium practices, and translation records

tuples.episode_object: the Gondar period, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern highlands and the lake country across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a fixed stone capital at last, and the factional politics that filled the vacuum when it stopped being obeyed
tuples.evidence_lens: the castle complex, royal chronicles, church land charters, and the accounts of European visitors

tuples.episode_object: the era of the princes and the reunification, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the coast and the lowlands across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a period with an emperor and no imperial power, ended by three rulers who rebuilt the state with imported firearms
tuples.evidence_lens: regional chronicles, arms import records, missionary correspondence, and the campaign accounts

tuples.episode_object: Ethiopia and the Red Sea coast, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the escarpment, the coastal plain and the sea across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a highland power permanently cut off from its own coastline by whoever held the ports, which set its foreign policy for centuries
tuples.evidence_lens: port customs records, treaty documents, and the correspondence over access to the sea

tuples.episode_object: the Sudanese Nile after Christianity, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Nile and the surrounding deserts across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: the slow replacement of a Christian river society by Arabic-speaking pastoralists, without a single conquest to date it
tuples.evidence_lens: genealogical traditions, church abandonment sequences, language change evidence, and traveller accounts

tuples.episode_object: the Funj and Darfur sultanates, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Nile confluence country and the western deserts across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: inland sultanates controlling the pilgrimage road across Africa, which was their revenue and their vulnerability
tuples.evidence_lens: the sultanates' land charters, pilgrimage route accounts, and the records of their conquerors

tuples.episode_object: the Nile cataracts and the desert routes, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the river between Egypt and the Sudan and the deserts beside it across five millennia
tuples.mechanism: six rock barriers that made the river un-navigable in places, so that the desert road and the river were always alternatives
tuples.evidence_lens: route surveys, fortress and way station archaeology, and the transport records of successive states

tuples.episode_object: Ethiopian and Nubian gold and ivory, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the river valleys and the Red Sea across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: two commodities that made an inland region worth an empire's attention for four thousand years without interruption
tuples.evidence_lens: mine surveys, Egyptian expedition records, customs registers, and the metal analysis of finished objects

tuples.episode_object: the Horn's frontier with Europe, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the coasts and the desert borders across a century
tuples.mechanism: the one African state to defeat a European invasion in the field, and the diplomacy that turned a battle into a border
tuples.evidence_lens: treaty texts, boundary commission records, arms purchase documents, and the campaign accounts of both sides

tuples.episode_object: Ethiopian food and farming, told as one long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland terraces and the lowland pastures across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a set of crops domesticated nowhere else, farmed with an ox plough on terraces, which supported a dense highland population
tuples.evidence_lens: crop domestication evidence, terrace archaeology, land tenure charters, and famine chronicles

tuples.episode_object: the Bantu expansion, told as one very long movement
tuples.time_place_scope: the country from the Cameroon grasslands to the southern cape across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: the spread of a language family with iron and farming into a continent, at walking pace and over a hundred generations
tuples.evidence_lens: linguistic family trees, pottery style sequences, iron working dates, and the genetics of modern populations

tuples.episode_object: the kingdom of Kongo, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Congo river and the Atlantic coast across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a centralised kingdom that adopted a foreign religion and literacy on its own terms, and was undone by the trade that came with them
tuples.evidence_lens: the kingdom's own letters in a European language, mission records, and the archaeology of the capital

tuples.episode_object: the Luba and Lunda states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the savannah and lakes of the southern Congo basin across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a portable political charter that could be exported, so that a title system spread far beyond the original kingdom
tuples.evidence_lens: oral traditions of the founding charter, tribute route evidence, and the accounts of the first outside travellers

tuples.episode_object: the Kuba kingdom, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the forest and savannah between two rivers across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom that recorded its own history through a king list and an art tradition, and controlled a craft economy
tuples.evidence_lens: the royal portrait figures and king list, textile and craft production evidence, and ethnographic collection records

tuples.episode_object: the Zimbabwe plateau successor states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau and its escarpments across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the fragmentation of a stone-building tradition into smaller states as the gold trade shifted to the coast
tuples.evidence_lens: stone enclosure sequences, imported goods dating, and Portuguese and later oral records

tuples.episode_object: the Zulu kingdom, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southeastern grasslands and the coast across a century
tuples.mechanism: the consolidation of many chiefdoms into one regimental state under population and drought pressure, and its collapse in one war
tuples.evidence_lens: oral testimony collected soon afterwards, settler and missionary records, and the campaign documents of its conquerors

tuples.episode_object: the Sotho and Tswana states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highveld and the Kalahari margin across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: large stone-walled towns on the highveld, dispersed by conflict and reassembled as mountain kingdoms under pressure
tuples.evidence_lens: stone-walled town surveys from the air, missionary records, and the treaties with colonial powers

tuples.episode_object: the Khoikhoi and San, told as one very long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern African interior and the cape across twenty millennia
tuples.mechanism: a foraging and herding society that met farming and then settlement, and was documented mainly by those who dispossessed it
tuples.evidence_lens: rock art in enormous quantity, herding site archaeology, colonial records, and the recorded oral traditions

tuples.episode_object: the Cape colony's founding and its African context, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southwestern cape and its hinterland across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a supply station that became a settler colony because the ships kept coming, and expanded because the settlers kept moving
tuples.evidence_lens: company records, land grant registers, slave lodge documents, and the frontier commando reports

tuples.episode_object: the Great Trek and the interior republics, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highveld and the eastern escarpment across half a century
tuples.mechanism: a settler migration into an interior recently emptied by war, and the republics it founded on that ground
tuples.evidence_lens: trek diaries, republic constitutions, treaty texts, and the African testimonies of the same events

tuples.episode_object: southern African gold and diamonds, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highveld, the diamond fields and the ports across a century
tuples.mechanism: two mineral discoveries that turned a farming periphery into an industrial economy and rewrote its politics in twenty years
tuples.evidence_lens: mining company records, labour recruitment registers, railway construction files, and the tax and tariff debates

tuples.episode_object: the Angolan coast and its interior, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Atlantic coast and the highlands behind it across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a coastal colony that existed to export people inland-sourced, and never developed anything else until it was forced to
tuples.evidence_lens: shipping registers, trading post accounts, mission records, and the inland kingdom traditions

tuples.episode_object: Mozambique and the channel coast, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Indian Ocean coast and the Zambezi mouth across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a coast held for the river route inland, never for itself, and therefore administered as a corridor rather than a country
tuples.evidence_lens: customs records, prazo grant documents, mission archives, and river navigation reports

tuples.episode_object: the Congo basin forests, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the great forest and its rivers across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a forest where the river is the only road, so that political reach was measured in canoe days and never exceeded them
tuples.evidence_lens: riverine settlement archaeology, linguistic distributions, expedition journals, and the rubber concession records

tuples.episode_object: the Congo Free State and the rubber years, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole basin and its river stations across a quarter century
tuples.mechanism: a state run as a private concession with a quota system, and the international campaign that ended it
tuples.evidence_lens: concession company records, missionary photographs and testimony, the commission of inquiry, and the population estimates

tuples.episode_object: central African copper, told as the whole life of a metal
tuples.time_place_scope: the copperbelt and the trade routes out of it across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a metal traded as standardised crosses across half a continent, which functioned as money long before any coin arrived
tuples.evidence_lens: copper cross finds far from the mines, smelting site archaeology, and the later mining company records

tuples.episode_object: the Swahili-Arab caravans into the interior, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the routes from the coast to the great lakes and the Congo across a century
tuples.mechanism: the arrival of firearms and credit in an interior with neither, which restructured every polity along the routes
tuples.evidence_lens: caravan ledgers, station records, the journals of missionaries and explorers, and local oral testimony

tuples.episode_object: southern African languages and their spread, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole subcontinent across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: the meeting of two entirely unrelated language families, which left click sounds inside Bantu languages as a record of the contact
tuples.evidence_lens: comparative linguistics, loanword analysis, settlement archaeology, and the early recorded vocabularies

tuples.episode_object: central African art and its collecting, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the forest and savannah kingdoms and the museums abroad across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a body of objects removed as ethnography rather than as art, and reassessed a century later by the people who took it
tuples.evidence_lens: collection registers and expedition records, workshop and lineage attributions, and restitution correspondence

tuples.episode_object: southern Africa under segregation, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the mines, the cities and the reserves across a century
tuples.mechanism: a labour system requiring men to migrate and families to stay behind, legislated into a whole social order
tuples.evidence_lens: pass and labour registers, mining compound records, commission reports, and the press of the period

tuples.episode_object: the Maya, told whole from the first villages to the last independent town
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yucatan, the Peten forest and the highlands across three and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: a civilisation of competing city states with a shared script and calendar, which never unified and never entirely ended
tuples.evidence_lens: the deciphered hieroglyphic inscriptions, stucco and stelae, settlement survey, and the colonial-era accounts

tuples.episode_object: Maya writing and its decipherment, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lowlands and the libraries abroad across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a script recording dynastic history in a spoken language, which turned a silent civilisation into one that names its own kings
tuples.evidence_lens: the monuments themselves, four surviving books, and the two-century decipherment record

tuples.episode_object: the Maya calendar, told as the whole life of a system
tuples.time_place_scope: the lowlands and highlands across two and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: a count of days running continuously for millennia, which lets an entire civilisation's events be dated to the day
tuples.evidence_lens: the long count inscriptions, astronomical tables in the surviving books, and the correlation with the European calendar

tuples.episode_object: Tikal, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central Peten forest across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a forest city that rose, was defeated and interrupted for a century and a half, and rose again on the same spot
tuples.evidence_lens: the dynastic inscriptions recording the defeat, the reservoir system, and the settlement survey from the air

tuples.episode_object: Calakmul and the great rivalry, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Yucatan forest across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a two-power system in which every smaller city had to choose a patron, recorded on the monuments of both sides
tuples.evidence_lens: the paired inscription records, alliance and accession dates, and the excavation of the two capitals

tuples.episode_object: Palenque, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western foothills above the plain across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a small kingdom that wrote its dynastic legitimacy into its architecture in unusual detail because its claim was unusually weak
tuples.evidence_lens: the tomb and its inscriptions, the palace complex, and the hieroglyphic panels read as an argument

tuples.episode_object: Copan, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern highland valley across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a city at the edge of the Maya world whose valley agriculture failed under its own population, documented in its own skeletons
tuples.evidence_lens: the hieroglyphic stairway, sculptural sequence, valley settlement survey, and the palaeopathology of the burials

tuples.episode_object: Caracol and the road-building cities, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Belizean forest across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a city that built causeways to absorb its neighbours' populations, which is visible only through survey from the air
tuples.evidence_lens: the causeway network mapped by laser survey, the inscriptions of its wars, and terrace agriculture evidence

tuples.episode_object: the Preclassic Maya and El Mirador, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Peten swamps across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: monumental building on a scale never matched later, abandoned centuries before the classic cities were founded
tuples.evidence_lens: the great platform complexes, causeways across swamp, and the absence of the later inscription tradition

tuples.episode_object: the Maya collapse, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern lowlands across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a staggered abandonment city by city over a hundred and fifty years, which is a process rather than an event
tuples.evidence_lens: the last dated monument at each site, drought proxies from lake cores, and the settlement abandonment sequences

tuples.episode_object: Chichen Itza and the northern lowlands, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Yucatan plain across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a city that flourished as the south emptied, built around water access in a country with no rivers at all
tuples.evidence_lens: the sinkhole deposits, building style mixtures, and the accounts of the later Maya chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Mayapan and the postclassic north, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a walled capital ruling by holding other cities' lords as residents, an arrangement that collapsed in a single revolt
tuples.evidence_lens: the city wall and residential survey, the Maya chronicles, and the early colonial testimonies

tuples.episode_object: the Maya highlands and the Quiche kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Guatemalan highlands across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: highland kingdoms in defensible country, conquered by an alliance of their own neighbours with a foreign army
tuples.evidence_lens: the highland dynastic epic written after the conquest, fortified site archaeology, and the conquest accounts

tuples.episode_object: Maya agriculture and water, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lowland forest and the northern plain across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: reservoirs, terraces and raised fields in a limestone country with no surface water, all requiring constant maintenance
tuples.evidence_lens: reservoir and canal survey, raised field remains, soil studies, and the drought record from lake cores

tuples.episode_object: Maya trade and the coastal canoe routes, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yucatan coast, the rivers and the highlands across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: an obsidian, salt, jade and cacao exchange run by canoe around a peninsula, which the first Europeans met before they met a city
tuples.evidence_lens: obsidian sourcing, salt works excavation, canoe route evidence, and the first European encounter accounts

tuples.episode_object: Maya religion and its books, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lowlands, the highlands and the archives abroad across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a written religious tradition of which four books survive because the rest were deliberately burnt
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving codices, painted pottery texts, the burning account, and the post-conquest recorded traditions

tuples.episode_object: the Spanish conquest of the Maya, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yucatan, the highlands and the Peten forest across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a conquest that took a hundred and seventy years because there was no single capital to capture
tuples.evidence_lens: conquest campaign records, mission and encomienda documents, and the Maya-language town records of the period

tuples.episode_object: colonial Maya society, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Yucatan and the highlands across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: town governments run in the Maya language under Spanish law, which preserved communities and their land records intact
tuples.evidence_lens: town council records written in Maya, land documents, church registers, and the tribute assessments

tuples.episode_object: the Caste War and the independent Maya, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Yucatan forest across half a century and more
tuples.mechanism: a rebellion that established an independent Maya polity in the forest for fifty years, ended by a railway
tuples.evidence_lens: the rebel correspondence, military campaign records, mission accounts, and the settlement archaeology of the forest towns

tuples.episode_object: the rediscovery of the Maya, told as the whole life of an idea
tuples.time_place_scope: the forest sites and the institutions abroad across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: the shift from imagining a peaceful priesthood to reading an inscribed record of dynastic war, forced entirely by decipherment
tuples.evidence_lens: expedition publications, the decipherment correspondence, and the changing museum interpretation records

tuples.episode_object: the Aztec empire, told whole from an island town to a siege
tuples.time_place_scope: the valley of Mexico and the tributary provinces across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: an empire of tribute rather than administration, which left conquered towns intact and therefore left them available to an ally
tuples.evidence_lens: tribute rolls and pictorial codices, the accounts of both sides, and the excavation of the island city

tuples.episode_object: Tenochtitlan, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lake basin at the centre of the highlands across two centuries and after
tuples.mechanism: a city built on an island in a lake, fed by chinampa farming and destroyed by a siege that cut its causeways
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavated temple precinct, chinampa remains, the conquest accounts, and the colonial drainage records

tuples.episode_object: the Olmec, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the gulf coast lowlands across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the earliest monumental tradition in the region, which supplied later civilisations with a template and left no readable text
tuples.evidence_lens: the colossal heads and their basalt sourcing, site excavation, and the iconographic comparisons with later cultures

tuples.episode_object: Teotihuacan, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northeastern valley of Mexico across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: the largest city in the Americas of its day, apparently governed without a portrayed king, and burnt in its own centre
tuples.evidence_lens: the grid plan and apartment compounds, the burnt palace layer, murals, and the references in Maya inscriptions

tuples.episode_object: the Zapotec and Monte Alban, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Oaxaca valleys across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a capital founded on a levelled hilltop between three valleys, a neutral site that made a confederation into a state
tuples.evidence_lens: the hilltop site itself, conquest slabs, an early script, and the valley settlement survey

tuples.episode_object: the Mixtec kingdoms, told whole
