tuples.time_place_scope: the Oaxaca highlands and coast across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: small mountain kingdoms whose politics ran on marriage alliance, recorded in painted books that read like genealogies
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving painted codices, tomb goods, and the colonial land documents that continue the same claims

tuples.episode_object: the Toltec and Tula, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern highland frontier across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a city whose real history is buried under the legend that later empires told about it to claim descent
tuples.evidence_lens: the site excavation, the later pictorial and textual traditions, and the comparison with distant sites claiming the same style

tuples.episode_object: the Tarascan state, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western highlands and lake country across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: the one neighbour the Aztec empire could not conquer, thanks to metallurgy and a defended frontier
tuples.evidence_lens: the state's own recorded account, copper and bronze artefacts, and frontier fortification survey

tuples.episode_object: Tlaxcala and the independent states, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern highlands across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: an enclave surrounded and deliberately left unconquered, which made it the natural ally for anyone attacking the centre
tuples.evidence_lens: the conquest alliance records, the town's own pictorial histories, and the privileges granted afterwards

tuples.episode_object: Cholula and the great pyramid, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern highland plain across two and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: the largest pyramid by volume anywhere, built in stages over fifteen centuries and mistaken for a hill
tuples.evidence_lens: the tunnelled excavation of its stages, the massacre account, and the church built on its summit

tuples.episode_object: the Gulf coast cultures, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern lowlands and the coast across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a humid lowland region whose ceramic and sculptural traditions record a society whose politics remain largely unreadable
tuples.evidence_lens: the sculpture and ceramic sequences, site excavation, and the tribute records of later empires

tuples.episode_object: west Mexican societies, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western highlands and the Pacific coast across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: shaft tomb societies and metalworking traditions that connected north along the coast rather than east to the centre
tuples.evidence_lens: shaft tomb excavation, metallurgical analysis showing Andean links, and the settlement surveys

tuples.episode_object: Mesoamerican maize, told as the whole life of a crop
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland valleys and everywhere it spread across nine millennia
tuples.mechanism: the domestication of a grass into the crop that made every civilisation in two continents possible
tuples.evidence_lens: the archaeobotanical sequence, the genetics of teosinte and maize, and the storage and field archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Mesoamerican writing and books, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands and lowlands across two and a half millennia
tuples.mechanism: several independent writing traditions, most of them burnt, surviving mainly as painted books produced after the conquest
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving pre-conquest and early colonial codices, monument inscriptions, and the burning records

tuples.episode_object: Mesoamerican ballgames, told as one long institutional life
tuples.time_place_scope: from the gulf coast to the northern deserts across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a game with permanent stone courts and ritual stakes, played across three thousand years and every culture in the region
tuples.evidence_lens: the courts themselves, rubber ball finds, sculptural depictions, and the early colonial descriptions

tuples.episode_object: the Spanish conquest of central Mexico, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coast, the highlands and the lake basin across three years and their aftermath
tuples.mechanism: a conquest carried out mostly by indigenous allies with their own reasons, in which the European contingent was small
tuples.evidence_lens: accounts from both sides written afterwards, the allies' own pictorial records, and epidemic mortality evidence

tuples.episode_object: the epidemics and the demographic collapse, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole region across a century
tuples.mechanism: the arrival of several diseases in sequence into a population with no exposure, which is the largest single fact of the century
tuples.evidence_lens: tribute count series, parish registers, colonial censuses, and the palaeopathological evidence

tuples.episode_object: colonial New Spain and its indigenous towns, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the mining north and the coasts across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: indigenous town governments and land titles that persisted under colonial law, and the silver economy built around them
tuples.evidence_lens: town council records in indigenous languages, land title documents, mining registers, and church archives

tuples.episode_object: Mesoamerican silver and the world, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern mining districts and the ports across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: silver mined in the highlands and spent in Asia, which made a colonial periphery the hinge of the world economy
tuples.evidence_lens: mint and mining records, shipping registers, mercury supply accounts, and the price series in three continents

tuples.episode_object: the survival of indigenous Mesoamerica, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the forests and the cities across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: the persistence of languages, towns and land claims through three different states, each of which assumed they would disappear
tuples.evidence_lens: colonial land documents, census language data, community archives, and the modern legal claim records

tuples.episode_object: the Inca empire, told whole from a valley kingdom to a captured king
tuples.time_place_scope: the Andes from Ecuador to Chile and the coast across a century
tuples.mechanism: an empire that resettled populations and rebuilt landscapes wholesale, held together by roads and a knotted-cord record system
tuples.evidence_lens: the knotted cords, colonial administrative inspections, road and storehouse archaeology, and the conquest accounts

tuples.episode_object: Cusco, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highland valley and its terraces across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a capital rebuilt as a ceremonial plan radiating lines of shrines, so that the city itself was an administrative diagram
tuples.evidence_lens: the stonework and its phases, the shrine line system recorded by colonial writers, and the colonial land records

tuples.episode_object: Machu Picchu and the royal estates, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern slopes above the river across a century
tuples.mechanism: royal estates owned by a dead ruler's household in perpetuity, which is why an empire kept building new ones
tuples.evidence_lens: the site itself, the colonial land documents naming its owner, and the terrace and hydraulic engineering

tuples.episode_object: the Chavin horizon, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern highlands and the coast across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a religious centre whose style spread across a whole region without any evidence of conquest
tuples.evidence_lens: the temple complex and its galleries, the style distribution in pottery and textiles, and the exotic goods deposited

tuples.episode_object: the Moche, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern desert coast and its valleys across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: irrigated desert valleys supporting a warrior elite, whose portrait pottery and tombs record the whole hierarchy
tuples.evidence_lens: the royal tombs, portrait ceramics, murals, irrigation canal archaeology, and the flood layers

tuples.episode_object: the Nazca, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern desert coast across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: a society in one of the driest places on earth, whose water engineering and ground drawings are its entire visible record
tuples.evidence_lens: the underground aqueducts, the ground drawings mapped from the air, textiles, and settlement excavation

tuples.episode_object: Tiwanaku, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the high altiplano around the great lake across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a highland ceremonial capital sustained by raised field agriculture at extreme altitude, which failed when the lake fell
tuples.evidence_lens: raised field remains, monumental stonework, colony settlements far away, and lake level reconstructions

tuples.episode_object: the Wari empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central highlands and the coast across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the first Andean state to build administrative centres and roads across a distance, which later empires simply reused
tuples.evidence_lens: the planned administrative sites, road segments, textile and ceramic distributions, and the storage facility archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the Chimu and Chan Chan, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern coast and its valleys across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a coastal empire of walled compounds, each built new for each ruler, which turned succession into a construction programme
tuples.evidence_lens: the compound sequence at the capital, canal archaeology, and the later Inca administrative records

tuples.episode_object: the Andean coastal valleys and their irrigation, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the desert coast and its river valleys across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: canal systems that made a desert coast one of the most productive farmlands anywhere, and needed constant repair
tuples.evidence_lens: canal survey, flood damage layers, field system archaeology, and the colonial water allocation records

tuples.episode_object: Andean textiles, told as the whole life of a craft
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands and the coast across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: cloth as the highest form of wealth in a society with no coinage, so that textiles were tax, gift and record together
tuples.evidence_lens: the preserved textiles from dry coastal graves, the tribute lists, and the workshop archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the quipu, told as the whole life of a record system
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands and the coast across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: an accounting and possibly narrative system in knotted cord, which recorded an empire and remains only partly readable
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving cords, colonial descriptions and court testimony, and the statistical analyses of knot patterns

tuples.episode_object: the Andean road system, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the mountains and the coast from Ecuador to Chile across two centuries and after
tuples.mechanism: a road network with runners, way stations and storehouses, which made a mountain empire governable at walking speed
tuples.evidence_lens: road and bridge archaeology, storehouse excavation, and the colonial inspections that used the same roads

tuples.episode_object: Andean vertical archipelagos, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the mountains from the coast to the forest edge across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: communities holding land at several altitudes at once, which spread risk across climates instead of trading for it
tuples.evidence_lens: colonial land inspections, settlement distribution, crop remains at multiple altitudes, and community records

tuples.episode_object: the potato and Andean crops, told as the whole life of a farming system
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands and their terraces across eight millennia
tuples.mechanism: the domestication of dozens of varieties suited to different altitudes, and the freeze-drying that made storage possible
tuples.evidence_lens: archaeobotanical sequences, terrace and storehouse archaeology, and the genetics of the domesticated varieties

tuples.episode_object: the Spanish conquest of Peru, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the coast and the forest across four decades
tuples.mechanism: a conquest that arrived during a civil war and used one side of it, followed by forty years of a rump resistance state
tuples.evidence_lens: the conquest accounts, the indigenous chronicles written afterwards, and the negotiation records of the resistance

tuples.episode_object: Potosi and Andean silver, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the high mountain mining district and the routes to the coast across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: one mountain that supplied much of the world's silver, worked by a rotating labour draft that hollowed out the countryside
tuples.evidence_lens: mining and mint records, labour draft registers, mercury supply accounts, and parish registers

tuples.episode_object: colonial Andean society and its rebellions, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the highlands, the mining districts and the cities across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: indigenous nobility used as tax collectors, which preserved a hereditary elite and eventually produced the leaders of a revolt
tuples.evidence_lens: colonial inspection records, noble genealogical petitions, rebellion trial documents, and tribute registers

tuples.episode_object: the Amazon frontier of the Andes, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern slopes and the upper rivers across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a permanently open frontier where highland states never established control, and the exchange that continued regardless
tuples.evidence_lens: trade goods in both directions, mission records, and the archaeology of the eastern slope settlements

tuples.episode_object: the Andean world after independence, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the mountains, the coasts and the new republics across a century
tuples.mechanism: republics that abolished tribute and kept the land system, so that the countryside changed less than the flag did
tuples.evidence_lens: land title and tax records, census data, hacienda accounts, and the community petition archives

coverage_profiles.subject: the Americas beyond the great empires

tuples.episode_object: the peopling of the Americas, told as one very long arrival
tuples.time_place_scope: from the northern land bridge to the southern tip across twenty millennia
tuples.mechanism: a continental settlement by small groups moving fast along coasts and rivers, argued over by every dating method available
tuples.evidence_lens: the earliest site dates and their disputes, coastal and inland finds, and the genetics of ancient and modern populations

tuples.episode_object: the Mississippian world and Cahokia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the central river valleys of North America across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a mound city of tens of thousands that rose and emptied within three hundred years and left no successor
tuples.evidence_lens: the mound complex, the plaza and palisade sequences, the settlement hinterland survey, and the isotope evidence

tuples.episode_object: the Ancestral Puebloan southwest, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the high desert plateau of the southwest across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: great houses and roads built in a marginal environment, abandoned in a decades-long drought and reformed elsewhere
tuples.evidence_lens: tree ring dating to the year, great house and road archaeology, and the migration evidence in the later pueblos

tuples.episode_object: the Hohokam and the desert canals, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern desert river valleys across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the largest canal system in pre-industrial North America, which sustained a society and required a coordination we cannot see
tuples.evidence_lens: canal survey and dating, ballcourt distributions, and the abandonment sequence in the fourteenth century

tuples.episode_object: the Hopewell and Adena mound builders, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern woodlands and their river valleys across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: an exchange network moving obsidian, copper and shell across a continent with no cities and no agriculture at scale
tuples.evidence_lens: the earthwork geometry, exotic raw material sourcing, and the burial assemblages

tuples.episode_object: the Iroquois confederacy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern woodlands and the lakes across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a confederation with a spoken constitution, which made five nations one diplomatic actor in every European war
tuples.evidence_lens: the recorded constitutional tradition, treaty minutes, longhouse village archaeology, and the wampum record

tuples.episode_object: the Great Plains and the horse, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the grasslands of central North America across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the arrival of an escaped domestic animal, which created an entirely new way of life within two generations
tuples.evidence_lens: horse remains and their dating, winter count calendars, trade records, and the accounts of early travellers

tuples.episode_object: the Pacific northwest coast peoples, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coast from Oregon to Alaska across five millennia
tuples.mechanism: a society of extraordinary wealth built on salmon and cedar without agriculture, organised around ceremonial redistribution
tuples.evidence_lens: shell midden and village site archaeology, house post and carving traditions, and the ethnographic record

tuples.episode_object: the Arctic and the Thule expansion, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the North American Arctic and Greenland across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a maritime hunting technology that let one culture cross the entire Arctic within a few centuries and displace another
tuples.evidence_lens: site sequences across the Arctic, whaling equipment finds, and the Norse accounts of contact in Greenland

tuples.episode_object: the Norse in North America, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the north Atlantic, Greenland and the Newfoundland coast across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a colony at the far end of a long supply line, which failed when the climate and the home economy both turned
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavated settlement, Icelandic sagas read cautiously, Greenland farm archaeology, and the ice core climate record

tuples.episode_object: the Amazon before contact, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the great basin and its rivers across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: dense riverine settlement and engineered soils in a forest long assumed to be empty, revealed by soil and survey
tuples.evidence_lens: dark earth soil distribution, geometric earthwork survey, ceramic sequences, and the first European river accounts

tuples.episode_object: the Caribbean before and after contact, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island chain and the surrounding seas across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: island societies connected by canoe across a whole sea, extinguished within a lifetime of the first European landfall
tuples.evidence_lens: island site archaeology, the canoe route evidence, the earliest colonial accounts, and the population estimates

tuples.episode_object: the Guarani and the missions, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the rivers of the southern interior across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: mission towns that protected a population from slaving raids and were dissolved by an order's expulsion
tuples.evidence_lens: mission account books and censuses, the mission town ruins, and the expulsion and dispersal records

tuples.episode_object: Patagonia and the southern cone peoples, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the plains, the Andes and the far south across ten millennia
tuples.mechanism: societies at the far end of the continent, adopting the horse and then being destroyed by a state campaign within a century
tuples.evidence_lens: rock art and cave sites, early European accounts, mission records, and the campaign documents of the conquest

tuples.episode_object: the fur trade and the northern interior, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the boreal forest, the lakes and the rivers across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: an economy in which indigenous nations supplied and controlled the trade for two centuries, then lost that leverage
tuples.evidence_lens: company post journals and account books, treaty records, and the archaeology of the trading posts

tuples.episode_object: North American treaties and land, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole continent across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a legal record of dispossession conducted almost entirely through documents, which is why the documents matter so much
tuples.evidence_lens: the treaty texts and their negotiation minutes, survey and allotment records, and the court case files

tuples.episode_object: the Californian peoples, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coast, the valleys and the mountains across ten millennia
tuples.mechanism: one of the densest non-agricultural populations anywhere, sustained by acorns and fisheries and destroyed in two waves
tuples.evidence_lens: midden and village archaeology, mission registers, and the gold rush period records

tuples.episode_object: the Andean and Mesoamerican peripheries, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the deserts of the north and the forests of the south across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: the frontier societies that traded with empires without joining them, and outlasted several of them
tuples.evidence_lens: trade goods in frontier sites, imperial frontier fortification, and the colonial mission and campaign records

tuples.episode_object: the Atlantic slave trade seen from the Americas, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the plantation coasts of two continents and the islands across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a plantation economy that required constant importation because it did not reproduce its own labour force
tuples.evidence_lens: shipping and plantation registers, port arrival records, probate inventories, and the narratives of the enslaved

tuples.episode_object: the American independence century, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: both continents and the Caribbean across a hundred years
tuples.mechanism: a wave of republics founded by colonial-born elites, which changed the sovereignty and left the land system standing
tuples.evidence_lens: constitutional texts, war correspondence, land and tax records, and the periodical press of the new states

tuples.episode_object: the Celts, told whole from the first princely graves to the last free tribes
tuples.time_place_scope: the country from the Danube to the Atlantic across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a shared material culture and language family spread without any state, which is why it left no capital and no archive
tuples.evidence_lens: princely burial excavation, art style distributions, coin issues, and the ethnographies of hostile neighbours

tuples.episode_object: the Hallstatt and La Tene worlds, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Alpine north, the upper Danube and the Rhine across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: salt and iron wealth concentrating in a few hillfort courts, which imported Mediterranean luxury and left it in graves
tuples.evidence_lens: salt mine archaeology, princely grave goods including imported vessels, and hillfort excavation

tuples.episode_object: the Gauls before Rome, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the Rhine, the Alps and the ocean across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a landscape of large fortified towns with coinage and trade, which is not the barbarian picture the conquest account gives
tuples.evidence_lens: oppidum excavation, coin issues in quantity, and a conquest narrative read against what the ground shows

tuples.episode_object: the Britons before Rome, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island south of the highlands across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: an island of hillforts and tribal coinages, already deeply connected to the continent before any legion arrived
tuples.evidence_lens: hillfort sequences, coin distributions, imported goods, and the earliest classical notices

tuples.episode_object: the Irish early kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island and its coasts across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a country of many small kingdoms with a shared law and learned class, never unified and never conquered from within
tuples.evidence_lens: the vernacular law tracts, annals kept in monasteries, ringfort archaeology, and the ogham inscriptions

tuples.episode_object: early Christian Ireland and its monasteries, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island and the sea routes to Britain and the continent across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: monasteries as the country's towns, schools and banks, which exported scholars and were emptied by raiders
tuples.evidence_lens: monastic annals, manuscripts, high crosses and round towers, and the raid records

tuples.episode_object: the Picts, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the north of Britain across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a people known mainly by their carved stones and by their neighbours' annals, who merged rather than fell
tuples.evidence_lens: symbol stones and their sequence, fort excavation, place name distributions, and the annals of neighbours

tuples.episode_object: Wales and the British kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western hills and the borderlands across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: small mountain kingdoms preserving a law and a language, unified briefly and conquered by a castle-building programme
tuples.evidence_lens: the vernacular law books, annals, castle building accounts, and the conquest settlement records

tuples.episode_object: Cornwall, Brittany and the Atlantic west, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western peninsulas on both sides of the Channel across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: sea-linked communities that were closer to each other than to their own hinterlands, sharing a language across water
tuples.evidence_lens: migration period settlement archaeology, saints' cults distribution, and the tin and salt trade records

tuples.episode_object: Scotland's making, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the north of Britain, the isles and the borders across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the amalgamation of four peoples into one kingdom, driven as much by Norse pressure from outside as by conquest within
tuples.evidence_lens: chronicle traditions, church foundation records, place names, and the archaeology of the royal centres

tuples.episode_object: the Iberian peoples before Rome, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula's plateau, coast and northwest across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: coastal societies transformed by Mediterranean contact while the interior stayed on its own trajectory for centuries
tuples.evidence_lens: sculpture and grave goods, Iberian script inscriptions, hillfort excavation, and the classical accounts

tuples.episode_object: Tartessos and the Atlantic south, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Guadalquivir and the Atlantic coast across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a metal-rich society at the far end of the Mediterranean network, famous in classical writing and archaeologically elusive
tuples.evidence_lens: metal working sites, hoards, Phoenician colony finds, and the classical references read carefully

tuples.episode_object: the Celtiberian wars and the conquest of Spain, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the plateau, the northwest and the mountains across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a two-hundred-year conquest of a country with no capital to take, which was ended by siege rather than by battle
tuples.evidence_lens: siege archaeology, camp remains, the conquest narratives, and the treaty and settlement records

tuples.episode_object: Gallaecia, Asturias and the northwest, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Atlantic northwest of the peninsula across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: hillfort country whose gold made it worth conquering and whose mountains made it the base for a later reconquest
tuples.evidence_lens: hillfort excavation, Roman gold mining engineering, and the early medieval chronicles

tuples.episode_object: the Basque country, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western Pyrenees and both slopes across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a language with no relatives that survived every conquest, in a region every empire found expensive to hold
tuples.evidence_lens: the language itself, inscriptions, the records of successive administrations, and the iron and whaling trade documents

tuples.episode_object: Celtic law and learning, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Ireland, Wales and Brittany across fifteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: a professional learned class of lawyers and poets, paid by clients and independent of kings, which outlasted the kings
tuples.evidence_lens: the law tracts and their commentaries, poetic corpora, and the records of the schools

tuples.episode_object: the Celtic languages, told as one long life
tuples.time_place_scope: the country from central Europe to the Atlantic islands across three millennia
tuples.mechanism: a language family that retreated westward for two thousand years and survives only at the ocean edge
tuples.evidence_lens: inscriptions in the continental languages, place name distributions, manuscripts, and the modern survey data

tuples.episode_object: the oppida of Europe, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country from the Danube to the Atlantic across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: large fortified towns with industry and coinage across temperate Europe, which vanished as urban places within a century of conquest
tuples.evidence_lens: excavation of the enclosures, coin minting evidence, and the settlement pattern after conquest

tuples.episode_object: Celtic art, told as the whole life of a style
tuples.time_place_scope: temperate Europe and the Atlantic islands across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: an abstract curvilinear style applied to metal, stone and manuscript, which travelled and was revived twice
tuples.evidence_lens: metalwork sequences, manuscript decoration, stone sculpture, and the nineteenth-century revival record

tuples.episode_object: the Atlantic seaways, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coasts from Iberia to Norway across four millennia
tuples.mechanism: a sea road along the western edge of Europe, which connected peninsulas that had almost no land contact
tuples.evidence_lens: shared monument types, metal and stone sourcing, boat finds, and the saints' cult distributions

tuples.episode_object: the Gothic kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Danube, Italy, Gaul and Iberia across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: federate armies settled inside an empire on tax revenue, which became kingdoms without ever quite deciding to
tuples.evidence_lens: the law codes, the letters of their own officials, church councils, and the burial archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the Ostrogothic kingdom of Italy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula and the Alpine approaches across seven decades
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom that governed Romans and Goths under two legal systems at once, destroyed by a reconquest it did not provoke
tuples.evidence_lens: the royal chancery letters, church building programmes, and the reconquest campaign accounts

tuples.episode_object: the Visigothic kingdom of Spain, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula and southern Gaul across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom with an elective monarchy and a strong church council, which made succession its permanent vulnerability
tuples.evidence_lens: the church council acts, the law code, coin issues, and the archaeology of the capital

tuples.episode_object: the Vandal kingdom of Africa, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the north African coast, Sicily and the western sea across a century
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom that took the empire's granary and its fleet at once, which is why it lasted and why it was destroyed
tuples.evidence_lens: the tax and estate documents, church controversy records, and the reconquest accounts

tuples.episode_object: the Lombards in Italy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain, the Apennines and the southern duchies across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a conquest that stopped short, leaving a country divided between a kingdom and imperial enclaves for two hundred years
tuples.evidence_lens: the law edicts, the church correspondence, duchy records, and the burial and church archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the Burgundians and the Rhone kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Rhone and Saone valleys and the Alps across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a small kingdom between larger ones, which codified its law early and was absorbed by inheritance rather than conquest
tuples.evidence_lens: the law code, church councils, and the Frankish records of the absorption

tuples.episode_object: the Anglo-Saxon settlement and kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the island south of the northern kingdoms across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a migration whose scale is still argued about, followed by seven kingdoms that consolidated under external pressure
tuples.evidence_lens: the burial and settlement archaeology, the early charters and law codes, and the chronicle traditions

tuples.episode_object: Mercia and the midland kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the English midlands and the Welsh border across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: an inland kingdom that dominated by controlling tribute from its neighbours, and vanished politically within two generations
tuples.evidence_lens: charters, the great border dyke, coin issues, and the chronicles of its rivals

tuples.episode_object: Northumbria, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the north of England and the southern Scottish lowlands across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom whose scholarship outlived its politics by centuries, and whose monasteries were the first raided
tuples.evidence_lens: the monastic histories and manuscripts, church and monastery archaeology, and the raid annals

tuples.episode_object: Wessex and the making of England, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the south of England and eventually the whole country across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the one kingdom that survived the great raiding army, and therefore the one that unified the rest by default
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicle written at its own court, law codes, burh fortification records, and coin reform evidence

tuples.episode_object: the Franks before Charlemagne, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: northern Gaul and the Rhineland across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom repeatedly divided among sons and reassembled by whichever son outlived the others, for two hundred years
tuples.evidence_lens: the histories written by bishops, the law code, coin issues, and the royal burial finds

tuples.episode_object: the Alemanni, Bavarians and the southern Germans, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the upper Rhine, the Alps and the Danube across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: peoples on the old frontier who became duchies inside a larger kingdom without ever quite ceasing to be separate
tuples.evidence_lens: law codes, monastery foundation charters, and the archaeology of cemeteries and hill sites

tuples.episode_object: the Frisians and the North Sea coast, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the coastal marshes and the North Sea across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: a trading people on artificial mounds in a marsh, whose commerce made them rich and whose land made them hard to conquer
tuples.evidence_lens: the settlement mounds, coin and trade finds, the law texts, and the annals of their conquerors

tuples.episode_object: the Slavs' arrival in Europe, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country from the Elbe to the Balkans and the Dnieper across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: an expansion visible in language and settlement and almost invisible in written record until the states appear
tuples.evidence_lens: settlement and pottery sequences, place names, and the notices in Byzantine and Frankish sources

tuples.episode_object: Great Moravia and the western Slavs, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the middle Danube and the March valley across a century
tuples.mechanism: a state that chose a liturgy in its own language and lost it, and left the alphabet to its neighbours instead
tuples.evidence_lens: fortified centre excavation, the mission's own writings, papal correspondence, and Frankish annals

tuples.episode_object: the Avar and Slavic Balkans, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Balkan peninsula between the Danube and the Aegean across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the disappearance of a whole provincial urban system and its replacement by a rural society within a century
tuples.evidence_lens: the destruction and abandonment layers, the change in settlement pattern, and the Byzantine administrative silence

tuples.episode_object: the Christianisation of northern Europe, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: from Ireland to the Baltic across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: conversion of rulers first and populations afterwards, which made church building a political record rather than a religious one
tuples.evidence_lens: mission letters, church foundation dates, burial practice change, and the law codes on religion

tuples.episode_object: the migration period burials, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country from the Danube to the North Sea across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: furnished burial as a status display that appears and then stops, which is a record of a society's anxiety about rank
tuples.evidence_lens: cemetery excavation and its statistics, grave goods sequences, and the isotope evidence for mobility

tuples.episode_object: the end of the western Roman provinces, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Britain, Gaul, Spain, Africa and Italy across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: the disappearance of the tax system, which took the army, the towns and the pottery industry with it in that order
tuples.evidence_lens: coin and pottery distribution collapse, villa abandonment, and the surviving administrative documents

tuples.episode_object: the barbarian law codes, told as one long project
tuples.time_place_scope: the western kingdoms across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: kingdoms writing down customary law in Latin to look like states, which tells us more about their ambitions than their courts
tuples.evidence_lens: the codes themselves and their prefaces, manuscript transmission, and the court records that survive

tuples.episode_object: the Vikings, told whole from the first raid to the last kingdom
tuples.time_place_scope: Scandinavia, the north Atlantic, the British isles, the rivers of the east and the Mediterranean across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a shipbuilding advance combined with a surplus of young men and a coastline of undefended monasteries
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals of the raided, ship burials, silver hoards, runestones, and the sagas read very cautiously

tuples.episode_object: the Norse ships, told as the whole life of a technology
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern seas and every coast reached across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a shallow-draught keeled hull that could cross an ocean and row up a river, which is the entire strategic story
tuples.evidence_lens: excavated ships, boatbuilding experiments, timber dendrochronology, and the depictions on stones

tuples.episode_object: Norway's making, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the fjord country and the northern coast across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a country of fjord districts unified by controlling the coastal sailing route rather than the land between them
tuples.evidence_lens: the sagas of the kings written later, church foundation records, and the archaeology of the coastal centres

tuples.episode_object: Denmark's making, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the islands, Jutland and the southern approaches across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom controlling the entrance to the Baltic, which was rich, early to unify, and permanently involved in England
tuples.evidence_lens: the great earthwork and its dating, runestones, fortress ring excavation, and the coin issues

tuples.episode_object: Sweden and the Baltic, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Scandinavian country, the Baltic islands and the eastern shores across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: a Baltic orientation that took Swedes east into rivers rather than west into oceans, which is why their record is elsewhere
tuples.evidence_lens: the trading town excavations, Arabic silver hoards, runestones commemorating eastern deaths, and Slavic chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Iceland, told whole from settlement to the loss of independence
tuples.time_place_scope: the island in the north Atlantic across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a settled society with law and no executive, which worked for three centuries and then could not stop a feud
tuples.evidence_lens: the settlement book and the sagas, the law texts, farm archaeology, and the tephra layers that date them

tuples.episode_object: Greenland's Norse colony, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southwestern fjords of Greenland across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: an agricultural colony at the edge of possibility, undone by climate, ivory prices and the end of its shipping
tuples.evidence_lens: farm excavation, midden isotope evidence, ice core climate data, and the walrus ivory trade records

tuples.episode_object: the Norse in Ireland and the sea kingdoms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Irish coasts, the Isle of Man and the western isles across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: raiders who founded the island's first towns, which is why the ports and the country had different histories
tuples.evidence_lens: town excavation, the Irish annals, coin issues, and the runic and burial evidence

tuples.episode_object: the Danelaw and Norse England, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern and northern parts of England across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a settlement large enough to change the language and the land divisions and small enough to be politically absorbed
tuples.evidence_lens: place names and language borrowing, the law and charter record, coin issues, and burial evidence

tuples.episode_object: Normandy and the Norse in France, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the lower Seine and the Channel coast across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a raiding force granted a province to defend the river against other raiders, which became the most effective duchy in Europe
tuples.evidence_lens: the treaty tradition, ducal charters, place names, and the chronicles of the neighbours

tuples.episode_object: the Rus and the river route east, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the rivers from the Baltic to the Black and Caspian seas across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a river trade in furs, wax and captives that founded towns at the portages and became a state at the far end
tuples.evidence_lens: Arabic and Byzantine accounts, silver hoards, town excavation, and the earliest chronicles

tuples.episode_object: the Norse in the Mediterranean and Byzantium, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Mediterranean coasts and the imperial capital across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a supply of foreign guardsmen for an empire that preferred its bodyguards to have no local relatives
tuples.evidence_lens: runestones commemorating service abroad, Byzantine court records, and the coin and object finds at home

tuples.episode_object: the Norse gods and their conversion, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Scandinavia and the settlements abroad across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a religion recorded almost entirely by Christians two centuries after it stopped, which makes every detail contestable
tuples.evidence_lens: the Icelandic prose and verse collections, place names, sacrificial site archaeology, and the conversion narratives

tuples.episode_object: runes, told as the whole life of a script
tuples.time_place_scope: Scandinavia, the British isles and the eastern rivers across sixteen centuries
tuples.mechanism: an alphabet cut into wood and stone by ordinary people, which records everyday speech that manuscripts never would
tuples.evidence_lens: the inscription corpus, wooden message finds from town excavations, and the manuscript runic traditions

tuples.episode_object: the Norse legal assemblies, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Scandinavia, Iceland and the Norse colonies across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: open-air assemblies with law recited from memory, which is a constitution that requires no writing and no capital
tuples.evidence_lens: assembly site archaeology, the law texts written down later, and the saga accounts of assembly procedure

tuples.episode_object: the Norse slave trade, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern seas, the eastern rivers and the southern markets across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a raiding economy whose primary export was people, which explains both the routes and the silver that came back
tuples.evidence_lens: silver hoard distribution, Arabic market accounts, legal texts on status, and the isotope evidence in burials

tuples.episode_object: Norse towns, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Baltic and North Sea coasts across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: planned trading towns founded by kings to tax exchange, which appear and disappear with the routes they served
tuples.evidence_lens: the excavated town sites, coin minting evidence, plot layouts, and the trade goods distributions

tuples.episode_object: the sagas, told as the whole life of a literature
tuples.time_place_scope: Iceland and Norway across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: prose narratives written centuries after the events they describe, which are evidence of their own century first
tuples.evidence_lens: manuscript transmission, comparison with contemporary annals, and the archaeological checks on their details

tuples.episode_object: the end of the Viking age, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern seas, England and Scandinavia across a century
tuples.mechanism: the moment defended coasts, established kingdoms and church integration made raiding unprofitable and treason at once
tuples.evidence_lens: the failed invasion accounts, fortification records, church integration documents, and the coin evidence

tuples.episode_object: the Norse legacy in Europe, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the north Atlantic, the British isles, France, Sicily and the eastern rivers across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the dispersal of one small population into the ruling class of half a dozen countries within four generations
tuples.evidence_lens: genealogies, land records, language borrowings, and the genetic studies of the settled regions

tuples.episode_object: the Frankish empire, told whole from a warband to three kingdoms
tuples.time_place_scope: Gaul, Germany, Italy and the Spanish march across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: an empire assembled by one long reign and divided by inheritance custom, which turned a continent into its successor states
tuples.evidence_lens: royal annals, capitularies, monastic charters, and the treaty of partition

tuples.episode_object: Charlemagne's reign, told whole from accession to succession
tuples.time_place_scope: Gaul, Germany, Italy, the Danube and the Pyrenees across half a century
tuples.mechanism: a state run by travelling inspectors and written instructions in a country with almost no literacy outside the church
tuples.evidence_lens: the capitularies and inspection instructions, court correspondence, annals, and the palace complex archaeology

tuples.episode_object: the Carolingian renaissance, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the palace schools and the monasteries across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a script and text reform that saved most of the Latin literature we have, undertaken to standardise the liturgy
tuples.evidence_lens: the manuscripts and their script, monastery library catalogues, and the correspondence of the scholars

tuples.episode_object: the partition of the empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country from the Elbe to the Ebro across a century
tuples.mechanism: a division by inheritance that created a middle kingdom nobody could hold, and a frontier argued over for a thousand years
tuples.evidence_lens: the treaty texts, the annals of each successor kingdom, and the coin and charter records of the middle lands

tuples.episode_object: west Francia and the making of France, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the Rhine, the Pyrenees and the ocean across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom whose counts became hereditary while the king stayed elective, so the crown was the weakest lordship in it
tuples.evidence_lens: royal and comital charters, monastic cartularies, and the annals of the great churches

tuples.episode_object: east Francia and the making of Germany, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the Rhine and the Elbe across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom of stem duchies where the crown was elective in practice, which made every succession a negotiation
tuples.evidence_lens: royal diplomas, ducal records, church council acts, and the chronicles of the monasteries

tuples.episode_object: the Carolingian church, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the empire's dioceses and monasteries across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a church reformed into an administrative arm of the state, which made bishops officials and monasteries landholders
tuples.evidence_lens: the reform capitularies, monastic rules and customaries, and the estate surveys of the great abbeys

tuples.episode_object: the Carolingian economy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the estates, the rivers and the North Sea trade across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a great estate system recorded in surveys, alongside a river and sea trade that the surveys almost never mention
tuples.evidence_lens: the estate surveys, coin reform and mint evidence, trading town excavation, and the toll records

tuples.episode_object: the Spanish march and the Pyrenean counties, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern Pyrenees and the Catalan plain across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a frontier zone of counties settled under charter, which grew away from its overlord until the tie was simply forgotten
tuples.evidence_lens: settlement charters, comital documents, monastery cartularies, and the frontier fortification record

tuples.episode_object: the Saxon wars and the northern frontier, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the Rhine and the Elbe across three decades and after
tuples.mechanism: a thirty-year war of conquest and forced conversion, and the duchy that grew out of the conquered ground
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals of the campaigns, the capitulary on Saxony, mission records, and the settlement archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Brittany and the western marches, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the peninsula and the marches behind it across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a duchy that stayed outside the empire by being expensive to invade and useful to leave alone
tuples.evidence_lens: monastic charters, the frontier march records, and the chronicles of both sides

tuples.episode_object: Aquitaine and the south, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the Loire and the Pyrenees across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a southern country with Roman law and a different language, joined to a northern kingdom by marriage and war repeatedly
tuples.evidence_lens: the law and charter record, monastic cartularies, and the marriage and inheritance documents

tuples.episode_object: the Vikings in Francia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Seine, the Loire and the Atlantic coast across a century
tuples.mechanism: raiding that exposed how little a large kingdom could protect, and made local defence the basis of local power
tuples.evidence_lens: the annals of the raids, bridge and fortification orders, tribute payment records, and coin hoards

tuples.episode_object: the rise of the castle and the knight, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the Loire and the Rhine across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the privatisation of defence into local strongpoints, which is the whole institutional story of the following four centuries
tuples.evidence_lens: castle excavation and dating, charter references to fortifications, and the peace movement council records

tuples.episode_object: the peace of God movement, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the south and centre of France across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: councils of bishops trying to regulate private war by oath, which is what a society does when the state cannot
tuples.evidence_lens: the council decrees, the oath texts, monastic chronicles, and the relic procession records

tuples.episode_object: Cluny and monastic reform, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Burgundy and the whole of Latin Europe across six centuries
tuples.mechanism: an abbey exempt from every local authority and answerable only to the pope, which created the first transnational institution
tuples.evidence_lens: the abbey's charters and its enormous cartulary, daughter house records, and the building sequence

tuples.episode_object: Carolingian and post-Carolingian Italy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern plain and the centre across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom whose crown was worth having and impossible to hold from beyond the Alps, so it was always contested
tuples.evidence_lens: royal diplomas, city and bishopric records, and the chronicles of the contending parties

tuples.episode_object: the Ottonian succession, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Germany, Italy and the eastern marches across a century
tuples.mechanism: the revival of an imperial title by a Saxon dynasty, which tied Germany's kings to Italy for six hundred years
tuples.evidence_lens: royal diplomas, the chronicles of the court, church foundation records, and the imperial coronation documents

tuples.episode_object: the Frankish law and administration, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the empire and its successor kingdoms across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: the county as the unit of everything, and the moment counts stopped being appointed and started being born
tuples.evidence_lens: capitularies and diplomas, comital family genealogies, and the estate and immunity records

tuples.episode_object: Latin Christendom's formation, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country from Ireland to the Elbe and from the North Sea to Sicily across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: the emergence of one religious jurisdiction across many kingdoms, which made a continent legible to itself
tuples.evidence_lens: papal correspondence, council acts, monastic networks, and the manuscript transmission record

tuples.episode_object: the Holy Roman Empire, told whole from an imperial coronation to a dissolution
tuples.time_place_scope: central Europe, Italy and the Burgundian lands across a thousand years
tuples.mechanism: an elective empire of hundreds of members, which was not weak so much as designed for a different job than a state
tuples.evidence_lens: the imperial diet records, the golden bull, the imperial court archives, and the treaty texts of its wars

tuples.episode_object: the Salian emperors and the investiture contest, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Germany and Italy across a century
tuples.mechanism: a quarrel over who appoints bishops, which was really about who controls the largest landholder in every province
tuples.evidence_lens: the papal and imperial letters, council decrees, the concordat text, and the chronicles of both parties

tuples.episode_object: the Hohenstaufen century, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Germany, Italy and Sicily across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: an emperor with a Sicilian kingdom, which made Italy the empire's centre of gravity and Germany its problem
tuples.evidence_lens: imperial charters, the Sicilian legal constitutions, city league records, and papal correspondence

tuples.episode_object: the Italian communes and the imperial wars, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Italian plain and its cities across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: self-governing cities that could out-finance an emperor, and a league that beat him without ever taking his crown
tuples.evidence_lens: city statutes, league treaty texts, campaign accounts, and the peace treaties

tuples.episode_object: the imperial cities, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the German lands across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: cities holding directly from the emperor and therefore from nobody nearby, which is a legal status doing economic work
tuples.evidence_lens: imperial privileges, city council records, guild archives, and the diet attendance lists

tuples.episode_object: the prince-bishoprics, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Rhine, the Danube and the north across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: bishops who were also territorial rulers, elected by cathedral chapters, so that a diocese was also a small state
tuples.evidence_lens: cathedral chapter election records, territorial administration documents, and the secularisation inventories

tuples.episode_object: the Hanseatic League, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Baltic and North Sea coasts and their rivers across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a league of trading towns with no army, no capital and no charter, which nonetheless made war and won
tuples.evidence_lens: the league diet minutes, town account books, warehouse and shipwreck archaeology, and treaty texts

tuples.episode_object: the Teutonic Order's state, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Baltic coast and Prussia across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a crusading order that acquired a country, and had no purpose left once its designated enemy converted
tuples.evidence_lens: the order's own extensive archive, castle building records, and the treaties with its neighbours

tuples.episode_object: Bohemia and the Luxembourg emperors, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Bohemian basin and the empire across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom inside the empire that provided emperors, and a religious rebellion that redefined the empire's politics
tuples.evidence_lens: royal and imperial charters, university records, the reform writings, and the crusade campaign accounts

tuples.episode_object: the Hussite wars and the Bohemian reformation, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Bohemia, Moravia and the imperial frontier across two decades and their aftermath
tuples.mechanism: a religious movement with a field army and a wagon fortress tactic, which no crusade could defeat and which split itself
tuples.evidence_lens: the movement's own writings, campaign accounts from both sides, and the negotiated settlement documents

tuples.episode_object: the imperial reform and the diet, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the German lands across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: an empire trying to give itself courts, taxes and a peace, and succeeding at the courts more than at anything else
tuples.evidence_lens: diet records, the perpetual peace text, the imperial court's case files, and the tax matriculation lists

tuples.episode_object: the German Reformation, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the German lands and the empire's institutions across a century
tuples.mechanism: a religious split that became a constitutional settlement, in which each prince chose for his own territory
tuples.evidence_lens: the theological writings, diet records, the peace treaty texts, and the visitation records of the new churches

tuples.episode_object: the Thirty Years War, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: central Europe from the Baltic to the Alps across three decades and after
tuples.mechanism: a religious war that became a general European war over the empire's constitution, and depopulated the ground it crossed
tuples.evidence_lens: army contract and contribution records, diplomatic correspondence, parish registers, and the peace treaties

tuples.episode_object: the Peace of Westphalia and after, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the empire and its neighbours across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a settlement that fixed the empire as a system of guaranteed rights rather than a state, and worked for a hundred and fifty years
tuples.evidence_lens: the treaty texts, the imperial court case files, diet records, and the diplomatic correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Saxony, Bavaria and the great electorates, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the German lands across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: electoral status as the difference between a large duchy and a European power, and what the electors bought with it
tuples.evidence_lens: electoral capitulations, court and treasury records, and the diplomatic correspondence of the courts

tuples.episode_object: Brandenburg-Prussia, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern German plain, the Baltic and the Rhineland across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a scattered inheritance with no natural frontiers, which built an army first and a state around it afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: military and tax administration records, the general directory's files, and the treaties of acquisition

tuples.episode_object: Austria and the Habsburg lands in the empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Alpine and Danubian lands across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: a dynasty that held the imperial title almost continuously and governed its own lands by entirely separate machinery
tuples.evidence_lens: court chancery records, land estate documents, and the imperial and territorial legal cases

tuples.episode_object: the imperial knights and the small territories, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the southwest and the Rhineland across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: hundreds of territories of a few villages each, which survived because the empire's law protected the small against the large
tuples.evidence_lens: imperial court case files, knightly association records, and the mediatisation inventories

tuples.episode_object: the empire's Jewish communities, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Rhineland, the south and the east across eight centuries
tuples.mechanism: communities protected by imperial charter and attacked locally, whose legal position was a rent paid to an absent emperor
tuples.evidence_lens: imperial protection charters, community record books, tax registers, and the records of expulsions and returns

tuples.episode_object: the dissolution of the empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: central Europe across two decades
tuples.mechanism: a thousand-year constitution ended by a war and a reorganisation, after which its members had to invent a new idea of Germany
tuples.evidence_lens: the mediatisation and secularisation inventories, the confederation treaty, and the diet's final records

tuples.episode_object: the house of Habsburg, told whole from a Swiss castle to a republic
tuples.time_place_scope: central Europe, Spain, the Netherlands and the Americas across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a dynasty that acquired more by marriage contract than by war, and therefore inherited quarrels it had no way to settle
tuples.evidence_lens: the family archives and marriage treaties, court records, and the succession war diplomacy

tuples.episode_object: the Austrian hereditary lands, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Alps, the Danube valley and the Adriatic approaches across seven centuries
tuples.mechanism: a cluster of duchies each with its own estates and law, governed by one family through separate negotiations with each
tuples.evidence_lens: estate assembly records, land registers, court chancery documents, and tax negotiation files

tuples.episode_object: the Habsburg Netherlands, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the North Sea and the Meuse across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the richest and least governable inheritance in Europe, whose privileges no ruler could keep and no ruler could revoke
tuples.evidence_lens: provincial privilege charters, revolt records, tax and revolt correspondence, and the treaty documents

tuples.episode_object: Habsburg Hungary and the frontier, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Danube plain, the Carpathians and the military border across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom held in three parts for a century and a half, and a permanent military border settled with soldier-farmers
tuples.evidence_lens: frontier regiment records, diet documents, reconquest campaign accounts, and the resettlement registers

tuples.episode_object: the Habsburg reconquest of Hungary, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Danube plain and Transylvania across half a century and after
tuples.mechanism: a reconquest that emptied a country and repopulated it deliberately with settlers from three directions
tuples.evidence_lens: campaign records, resettlement charters, land distribution files, and the demographic surveys

tuples.episode_object: Bohemia under the Habsburgs, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Bohemian basin and Moravia across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a kingdom whose nobility was replaced wholesale after one battle, which made a defeated country a governable province
tuples.evidence_lens: the confiscation registers, the renewed land ordinance, estate records, and the church visitation documents

tuples.episode_object: the Habsburg court and its ceremony, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Vienna, Madrid, Prague and Brussels across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a court ritual designed to make an elective and a hereditary dignity look like one thing, staged daily for centuries
tuples.evidence_lens: court ceremonial books, ambassadorial reports, building programmes, and the household account books

tuples.episode_object: the Spanish Habsburg inheritance, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Spain, Italy, the Netherlands and the Americas across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: an empire funded by American silver and spent on European wars, which defaulted repeatedly while being the richest state in the world
tuples.evidence_lens: treasury and default records, silver fleet registers, war correspondence, and the council minutes

tuples.episode_object: the war of the Spanish succession, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Spain, Italy, the Netherlands and the Americas across thirteen years
tuples.mechanism: a succession fought by everyone else to prevent one family holding two crowns, settled by dividing the inheritance
tuples.evidence_lens: the will and its contested texts, campaign records, and the peace treaties and their trade clauses

tuples.episode_object: Maria Theresa's reforms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole monarchy across four decades
tuples.mechanism: a defeat that forced a scattered inheritance to become one taxable administration within a single reign
tuples.evidence_lens: the tax and land survey records, administrative reorganisation files, school regulations, and court correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Josephinism and the enlightened reforms, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole monarchy across two decades and after
tuples.mechanism: reform imposed from above at a speed the provinces could not absorb, most of which had to be withdrawn
tuples.evidence_lens: the reform patents, monastery dissolution inventories, provincial protest files, and the revocation documents

tuples.episode_object: the Habsburg army, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: central Europe, Italy and the Balkans across four centuries
tuples.mechanism: a multilingual army whose command language and regimental identities were the monarchy's most successful institution
tuples.evidence_lens: regimental records, recruitment and conscription files, campaign correspondence, and the officer career registers

tuples.episode_object: the Habsburg bureaucracy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole monarchy across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a professional civil service in a state with no common language, which held the monarchy together longer than politics did
tuples.evidence_lens: ministry files, civil service examination and career records, and the language of administration decrees

tuples.episode_object: Vienna, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Danube crossing and its basin across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a frontier fort that became an imperial capital, twice besieged from the east and rebuilt each time as a statement
tuples.evidence_lens: the fortification and siege records, building and endowment documents, and the city administration files

tuples.episode_object: Prague, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Vltava basin across twelve centuries
tuples.mechanism: a capital that was imperial, then provincial, then national, and whose architecture records each demotion and revival
tuples.evidence_lens: the castle and city building phases, university records, and the administrative correspondence with the capital

tuples.episode_object: Trieste and the Adriatic ports, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the head of the Adriatic and its hinterland across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a free port created by decree to give a landlocked monarchy a sea outlet, which grew a cosmopolitan city around it
tuples.evidence_lens: the free port decrees, customs and shipping records, and the insurance and merchant company archives

tuples.episode_object: Galicia and the Polish partition lands, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Carpathian foothills and the plains across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a province acquired by partition and governed as a subsidised periphery, poor, populous and politically loud
tuples.evidence_lens: partition treaty texts, provincial administration files, land reform records, and the local press

tuples.episode_object: Habsburg Italy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Lombardy, Venetia, Tuscany and the smaller duchies across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: the richest and best-administered Habsburg provinces, which is exactly why losing them cost so much revenue
tuples.evidence_lens: the land survey and cadastral records, provincial administration files, and the campaign and treaty documents

tuples.episode_object: the nationalities question, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole monarchy across a century
tuples.mechanism: a state of eleven language groups trying every constitutional arrangement in turn and satisfying none of them completely
tuples.evidence_lens: census language data, parliamentary records in several languages, school and language ordinance files, and the press

tuples.episode_object: the end of the monarchy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: central Europe from the Alps to the Carpathians across five years
tuples.mechanism: a state that survived defeat repeatedly and dissolved along its language lines within weeks when the army stopped holding
tuples.evidence_lens: the war administration records, the succession state declarations, and the peace treaties of the successor states

coverage_profiles.subject: the French monarchy and its empire

tuples.episode_object: France itself, told whole from a small royal domain to a republic
tuples.time_place_scope: the country between the Rhine, the Pyrenees, the Alps and the ocean across a millennium
tuples.mechanism: the slow absorption of great fiefs into a royal domain by inheritance, marriage, purchase and confiscation over eight hundred years
tuples.evidence_lens: royal charters and acts, the accounts of the treasury, provincial estate records, and the parlement registers

tuples.episode_object: the Capetian kings, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Paris basin and the expanding kingdom across three and a half centuries
tuples.mechanism: an elective crown made hereditary by crowning the heir early every time, for eleven generations without a failure
tuples.evidence_lens: royal acts and charters, monastic chronicles, seals, and the domain account rolls

tuples.episode_object: the Hundred Years War, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: France, England and the Channel across a hundred and sixteen years
tuples.mechanism: a dynastic claim that became a national war, decided in the end by artillery and taxation rather than by battles
tuples.evidence_lens: campaign records, tax grant documents, chronicles from both sides, and the treaty texts

tuples.episode_object: Paris, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Seine island and its basin across two millennia
tuples.mechanism: a capital on a river crossing whose university, court and markets were all in one place, which made every revolt national
tuples.evidence_lens: the city accounts, university records, building and wall phases, and the police archives

tuples.episode_object: the French religious wars, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole kingdom across four decades
tuples.mechanism: a civil war of confession and faction, ended by a conversion and an edict that traded toleration for order
tuples.evidence_lens: the edict texts, faction correspondence, siege and massacre accounts, and the parish registers

tuples.episode_object: Richelieu, Mazarin and the making of absolutism, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the kingdom, its provinces and its wars across half a century
tuples.mechanism: the substitution of appointed intendants for provincial elites, which is what absolutism actually meant in practice
tuples.evidence_lens: intendant correspondence, treasury records, the Fronde documents, and the ministerial memoranda

tuples.episode_object: Versailles and the court, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the palace and the kingdom it governed across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a court that made attendance compulsory for the nobility, which turned potential rebels into full-time courtiers
tuples.evidence_lens: the building accounts, court ceremonial and pension records, and the memoirs of the courtiers

tuples.episode_object: the French fiscal system and its collapse, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the whole kingdom across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: a tax system riddled with exemptions and farmed out to contractors, which could not be reformed without a constitutional crisis
tuples.evidence_lens: tax farm contracts, treasury accounts, the assembly of notables records, and the reform memoranda

tuples.episode_object: the French Revolution, told whole from the calling of the estates to an empire
tuples.time_place_scope: the kingdom, its provinces and its borders across a decade
tuples.mechanism: a fiscal crisis that became a constitutional one, radicalised by war and ended by the army it created
tuples.evidence_lens: the assembly debates, the decrees, section and club records, and the army and requisition documents

tuples.episode_object: the Napoleonic empire, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: Europe from Iberia to Moscow across sixteen years
tuples.mechanism: an empire of satellite kingdoms and a legal code, held by one army that could not be in two places
tuples.evidence_lens: the code and its adoption records, campaign correspondence, conscription registers, and the treaties

tuples.episode_object: the French colonial empire in the Americas, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Saint Lawrence, the Mississippi and the Caribbean across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a fur and sugar empire with too few settlers to hold the mainland and too much profit to give up the islands
tuples.evidence_lens: colonial administration files, fur trade records, plantation registers, and the treaty cessions

tuples.episode_object: Haiti and Saint-Domingue, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the western third of the island and the Atlantic across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: the richest colony in the world built on the harshest plantation regime, and the only slave revolt that founded a state
tuples.evidence_lens: plantation and shipping registers, the revolutionary correspondence, the constitution texts, and the indemnity records

tuples.episode_object: the French in India and the Indian Ocean, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Indian coasts, the islands and the sea routes across two centuries
tuples.mechanism: a trading company that came second everywhere and lost its bases each time a European war was settled elsewhere
tuples.evidence_lens: company records, treaty and cession documents, and the correspondence of the local governors

tuples.episode_object: French north Africa, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Maghreb coast, the mountains and the Sahara across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: settler colonisation of the best land in a country legally declared part of France, which made withdrawal a constitutional crisis
tuples.evidence_lens: land registration records, settlement statistics, military reports, and the parliamentary debates

tuples.episode_object: French west and central Africa, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Sahel, the forests and the equatorial basin across eight decades
tuples.mechanism: a federation of colonies administered from one capital, built around railways to the coast and a single currency
tuples.evidence_lens: administration files, railway and concession records, tax and labour registers, and the boundary agreements

tuples.episode_object: French Indochina, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the deltas, the highlands and the coast across nine decades
tuples.mechanism: a colony organised around rice and rubber exports and a monopoly system, which paid for itself and for very little else
tuples.evidence_lens: customs and monopoly records, plantation registers, administration files, and the colonial and local press

tuples.episode_object: the French Pacific and the smaller colonies, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the Pacific islands, the Indian Ocean and the Caribbean across three centuries
tuples.mechanism: scattered small possessions kept for coaling, prestige and strategic denial rather than for revenue
tuples.evidence_lens: naval station records, administration files, missionary archives, and the plebiscite and status documents

tuples.episode_object: the French language as policy, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: France, the empire and the world across five centuries
tuples.mechanism: the deliberate replacement of regional languages by one administrative language, at home first and abroad afterwards
tuples.evidence_lens: the language ordinances, school records, census language data, and the academy's own archives

tuples.episode_object: French republics and restorations, told whole
tuples.time_place_scope: the country and its institutions across a century and a half
tuples.mechanism: a country that wrote fifteen constitutions in a hundred and fifty years while its administration barely changed at all
