tuples.mechanism: the strategic decision to attack an enemy's homeland rather than fight him where he stood, and the politics it made at home
tuples.evidence_lens: the histories of two traditions, senate proceedings reported later, and the archaeology of the Iberian campaign sites

tuples.episode_object: Belisarius, from a guard officer to a general repeatedly recalled
tuples.time_place_scope: the Balkans, north Africa, Italy and Mesopotamia across roughly sixty years
tuples.mechanism: a general trusted with reconquest and never with resources, by an emperor who feared success more than failure
tuples.evidence_lens: a secretary who wrote both an official history and a hostile one, plus the imperial legislation and the campaign archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Trajan, from a provincial soldier's son to a death on the road home
tuples.time_place_scope: Iberia, the Danube, Mesopotamia and Rome across sixty-three years
tuples.mechanism: the last emperor to expand the empire, and the demonstration that the new provinces cost more to hold than they yielded
tuples.evidence_lens: the triumphal column read as an official account, the letters with a provincial governor, coins, and the frontier archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Mehmed the Conqueror, from a twice-crowned boy to a death on campaign
tuples.time_place_scope: Anatolia, the straits and the Balkans across forty-nine years
tuples.mechanism: the decision to take one city whatever it cost, and the deliberate repopulation programme that followed the taking
tuples.evidence_lens: the chronicles of both besiegers and besieged, the resettlement registers, and the building and endowment records

tuples.episode_object: Shivaji, from a hill fort commander to a crowned king
tuples.time_place_scope: the western Deccan, the ghats and the coast across fifty-three years
tuples.mechanism: the conversion of raiding and fort-holding into a revenue state, by taxing the country he could not permanently occupy
tuples.evidence_lens: the court records and letters, the fort archaeology, and the accounts of the empires he raided

tuples.episode_object: Nader Shah, from a tribal officer to an assassinated conqueror
tuples.time_place_scope: the Iranian plateau, India, the Caucasus and Central Asia across fifty-nine years
tuples.mechanism: a conqueror whose state was an army payroll, which required a new campaign every year and had no institution to inherit
tuples.evidence_lens: court chronicles, the plunder and treasury records, and the accounts of foreign merchants and envoys

tuples.episode_object: Mahmud of Ghazni, from a slave commander's son to a raiding empire's ruler
tuples.time_place_scope: Afghanistan, eastern Iran and northern India across fifty-nine years
tuples.mechanism: annual raiding as fiscal policy, which funded a capital and a court and built almost nothing in the country raided
tuples.evidence_lens: court poetry and history written for him, Indian temple and inscription records, and the coin issues

tuples.episode_object: Pachacuti, from a younger son at a siege to the builder of an empire
tuples.time_place_scope: the Andean highlands from the Cusco valley outward across roughly seventy years
tuples.mechanism: the conversion of a valley kingdom into an empire by resettling populations and rebuilding the capital as an idea
tuples.evidence_lens: colonial-era interviews with descendants, the knotted-cord derived accounts, and the archaeology of the estates

tuples.episode_object: Shaka of the Zulu, from an outcast youth to a killing at his own homestead
tuples.time_place_scope: the southeastern African grasslands across roughly forty years
tuples.mechanism: the reorganisation of many chiefdoms into age-regiments, which made an army and destroyed the societies that fed it
tuples.evidence_lens: oral testimony collected within living memory of it, settler and missionary accounts, and the settlement archaeology

tuples.episode_object: Toyotomi Hideyoshi, from a peasant's son to a regent whose heir lost everything
tuples.time_place_scope: the Japanese archipelago and the Korean peninsula across sixty-one years
tuples.mechanism: a career built on being indispensable to a superior, and a succession he could not secure because he began it too late
tuples.evidence_lens: the land survey he ordered, campaign correspondence, court records, and the accounts of foreign missionaries

coverage_profiles.subject: whole lives, founders, lawgivers and reformers

tuples.episode_object: Hammurabi, from a small city's king to a name on a law stele
tuples.time_place_scope: the Mesopotamian floodplain across roughly forty-three years of rule
tuples.mechanism: a king who unified a plain by canal control and diplomacy, and advertised the result as justice carved in stone
tuples.evidence_lens: the stele itself, the letters of his own administration, and the ordinary court records that show law in practice

tuples.episode_object: Ashoka, from a contested succession to a ruler preaching on rocks
tuples.time_place_scope: almost the whole Indian subcontinent across roughly forty years of rule
tuples.mechanism: the conversion of an imperial ideology from conquest to moral instruction, published on stone across a subcontinent
tuples.evidence_lens: the edicts themselves in several languages, later Buddhist traditions, and the archaeology of the pillars

tuples.episode_object: Solon, from a merchant poet to a self-imposed exile
tuples.time_place_scope: Athens and the Aegean across roughly seventy years
tuples.mechanism: a debt cancellation and a constitutional reordering imposed by one man who then left so it could not be undone for him
tuples.evidence_lens: his own surviving verse, later constitutional histories, and the legal traditions attributed to him

tuples.episode_object: Augustus, from an unknown heir to an emperor who never used the word
tuples.time_place_scope: Rome, Italy, the provinces and the frontiers across seventy-five years
tuples.mechanism: the accumulation of ordinary republican powers in one person, so that a monarchy could be built without announcing one
tuples.evidence_lens: his own record of achievements read as advertisement, hostile later histories, coins, inscriptions and the building record

tuples.episode_object: Justinian, from a peasant's nephew to an emperor who outlived his own reconquest
tuples.time_place_scope: the eastern empire, north Africa, Italy and the frontiers across eighty-two years
tuples.mechanism: the codification of a thousand years of law in six years, which outlasted every province he spent his treasury reconquering
tuples.evidence_lens: the legal codification itself, a secretary's official and hostile accounts, the building programme, and the plague records

tuples.episode_object: Umar ibn al-Khattab, from a merchant to a caliph killed in a mosque
tuples.time_place_scope: Arabia, the Levant, Egypt and Iran across roughly sixty years
tuples.mechanism: the invention of the administrative apparatus of a new empire in ten years, including its calendar and its stipend register
tuples.evidence_lens: later compilations of his decisions, the earliest papyri and coins of the administration, and the conquest narratives

tuples.episode_object: Alfred of Wessex, from a fourth son to a king with a school and a navy
tuples.time_place_scope: southern England and the Danish frontier across fifty years
tuples.mechanism: a defensive system of fortified towns and rotating levies, which turned survival into the basis for a later unification
tuples.evidence_lens: his own translation prefaces, a court biography, the burghal fortification list, the chronicle, and the coin reform

tuples.episode_object: Frederick the Second of Sicily, from a ward of the pope to an excommunicated emperor
tuples.time_place_scope: Sicily, Italy, Germany and the Levant across fifty-six years
tuples.mechanism: a bureaucratic kingdom in the south financing an elective empire in the north, which neither the popes nor the princes would allow
tuples.evidence_lens: his own legal constitutions, the chancery correspondence, papal letters, and the castle building record

tuples.episode_object: Suleiman the Lawgiver, from a provincial governor to a death in a tent on campaign
tuples.time_place_scope: the Balkans, Anatolia, the Arab provinces and the Mediterranean across seventy-one years
tuples.mechanism: the codification of secular law beside religious law, which is what let a growing empire govern provinces it had just taken
tuples.evidence_lens: the law code, the imperial council registers, the campaign diaries, and the endowment and building records

tuples.episode_object: Akbar, from a boy on a contested throne to an emperor with a measured empire
tuples.time_place_scope: northern India, the Deccan and Afghanistan across sixty-three years
tuples.mechanism: a revenue survey and a rank system for officials, which turned a conquest into an administration within one reign
tuples.evidence_lens: the court history written to his order, the revenue manuals, the religious debate records, and the architecture

tuples.episode_object: Sejong of Joseon, from a third son to a king who gave a country an alphabet
tuples.time_place_scope: the Korean peninsula and its northern frontier across fifty-three years
tuples.mechanism: state-sponsored research institutes producing a script, a calendar and farming manuals as instruments of government
tuples.evidence_lens: the daily court annals, the alphabet's promulgation document, the technical treatises, and the frontier records

tuples.episode_object: Tokugawa Ieyasu, from a child hostage to a retired shogun who arranged everything
tuples.time_place_scope: the Japanese archipelago across seventy-three years
tuples.mechanism: outliving every rival and then legislating so thoroughly that the settlement held for two and a half centuries
tuples.evidence_lens: the house laws and edicts, the land survey, the domain assignment records, and the accounts of foreign traders

tuples.episode_object: the Kangxi emperor, from a boy under regents to a ruler who outlasted his own heirs
tuples.time_place_scope: China, the steppe, Taiwan and the northern frontier across sixty-eight years
tuples.mechanism: a very long reign that consolidated a conquest dynasty by governing in the conquered culture's own idiom
tuples.evidence_lens: the palace memorial archive, the campaign records, the Jesuit correspondence, and the treaty and survey documents

tuples.episode_object: Peter the Great, from a sidelined boy tsar to an emperor who died of a chill
tuples.time_place_scope: Russia, the Baltic, the Black Sea and western Europe across fifty-two years
tuples.mechanism: the forced import of shipbuilding, taxation and administration from abroad, paid for by a tax on every male soul
tuples.evidence_lens: his own decrees and correspondence, the poll tax registers, the shipyard records, and the foreign embassy reports

tuples.episode_object: Maria Theresa, from an unprepared heiress to a widow who reformed a monarchy
tuples.time_place_scope: the Austrian, Bohemian and Hungarian lands across sixty-three years
tuples.mechanism: a war of succession that proved a scattered inheritance could not defend itself, followed by four decades of building one
tuples.evidence_lens: the tax and land surveys, the administrative reform files, her own political testaments, and the court correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Catherine the Great, from a minor German princess to an empress of a doubled empire
tuples.time_place_scope: Russia, the steppe, the Black Sea and Poland across sixty-seven years
tuples.mechanism: legitimacy purchased through expansion and noble privilege, by a ruler with no hereditary claim of her own
tuples.evidence_lens: her own correspondence and legislative instruction, the partition treaties, the provincial reform files, and the memoirs

tuples.episode_object: Muhammad Ali of Egypt, from an Albanian officer to a ruler who founded a dynasty
tuples.time_place_scope: Egypt, the Sudan, Arabia and the Levant across eighty years
tuples.mechanism: the creation of a conscript army, a cotton monopoly and state factories together, because each one required the others
tuples.evidence_lens: the government's own archives, the monopoly and conscription records, and the consular and merchant correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Toussaint Louverture, from an enslaved coachman to a prisoner in a French fort
tuples.time_place_scope: the western third of Hispaniola and the Atlantic across roughly fifty-nine years
tuples.mechanism: the conversion of a slave revolt into a governing administration, which is the part that made the revolution irreversible
tuples.evidence_lens: his own proclamations and correspondence, the colonial administration records, and the accounts of all three foreign powers

tuples.episode_object: Simon Bolivar, from an orphaned heir to a man who died on his way to exile
tuples.time_place_scope: the northern Andes, the Caribbean coast and the highlands across forty-seven years
tuples.mechanism: the attempt to found one large republic where the geography and the local elites both required several
tuples.evidence_lens: his own enormous correspondence, the constitutional drafts, campaign records, and the congress documents

tuples.episode_object: Menelik the Second, from a captive prince to an emperor with a railway
tuples.time_place_scope: the Ethiopian highlands, the lowlands and the frontier across seventy years
tuples.mechanism: the purchase of modern firearms before a confrontation rather than after it, which is the whole difference in the outcome
tuples.evidence_lens: the arms purchase records, the treaty texts in two languages, the campaign accounts, and the concession documents

coverage_profiles.subject: whole lives, navigators, merchants and explorers

tuples.episode_object: Zheng He, from a captured boy to an admiral of enormous fleets
tuples.time_place_scope: the southern Chinese ports, the Indian Ocean and the east African coast across sixty-two years
tuples.mechanism: state voyages of prestige rather than trade, which are magnificent while a court wants them and cancelled when it does not
tuples.evidence_lens: the surviving stele inscriptions, the shipyard records, and the foreign accounts of the fleets' arrivals

tuples.episode_object: Ibn Battuta, from a young judge leaving home to an old man dictating a book
tuples.time_place_scope: north Africa, Arabia, Iran, India, China, the Sahel and Iberia across roughly sixty-eight years
tuples.mechanism: a religious scholar's qualification working as a passport, employable in any Muslim court from Morocco to Bengal
tuples.evidence_lens: his dictated account with its known borrowings and gaps, checked against the records of the courts he claims to have served

tuples.episode_object: Marco Polo, from a merchant's son to a prisoner dictating a book
tuples.time_place_scope: Venice, the overland routes, China and the Indian Ocean across seventy years
tuples.mechanism: a family trading firm operating across a continent under one empire's protection, and the book that made it famous
tuples.evidence_lens: the manuscript versions that differ substantially from each other, Venetian notarial records, and the Chinese sources' silence

tuples.episode_object: Vasco da Gama, from a minor noble to a viceroy dead of illness in India
tuples.time_place_scope: Portugal, the African coast and the Indian Ocean across roughly fifty-five years
tuples.mechanism: the discovery that a monsoon crossing was possible, and the violence that followed from arriving with guns into an unarmed trade
tuples.evidence_lens: an anonymous journal of the first voyage, the crown's instructions, the customs records, and the Indian accounts

tuples.episode_object: Ferdinand Magellan, from a passed-over captain to a death in the Philippines
tuples.time_place_scope: Iberia, the Atlantic, the strait and the Pacific across roughly forty-one years
tuples.mechanism: a captain who proposed a route to a rival crown after his own refused him, and did not live to see it completed
tuples.evidence_lens: a surviving diarist's account, the expedition's own records, the surviving ship's log, and the crown's contract

tuples.episode_object: Christopher Columbus, from a Genoese weaver's son to a man stripped of his titles
tuples.time_place_scope: Genoa, Iberia, the Atlantic and the Caribbean across fifty-five years
tuples.mechanism: a miscalculation of the earth's size backed by a contract for hereditary governorship, which is why the aftermath was litigated for decades
tuples.evidence_lens: his own journals as transcribed by others, the capitulation contract, the royal inquiry, and the family lawsuits

tuples.episode_object: Bartolomeu Dias, from a royal household officer to a drowning off the cape
tuples.time_place_scope: Portugal, the African coast and the Atlantic across roughly fifty years
tuples.mechanism: a voyage that proved a continent had an end, blown round it by a storm rather than steered round it
tuples.evidence_lens: the padrao stones he left, the crown's records, the later chroniclers, and the navigational reconstructions

tuples.episode_object: Zhang Qian, from an envoy to a captive to a returning ambassador
tuples.time_place_scope: the Chinese capital, the western corridor and Central Asia across roughly forty years
tuples.mechanism: a diplomatic mission that failed at its purpose and returned with the geography that redirected an empire's foreign policy
tuples.evidence_lens: the standard history's account of his report, the frontier garrison documents, and the archaeology of the corridor

tuples.episode_object: Xuanzang, from a young monk leaving illegally to a translator with an imperial workshop
tuples.time_place_scope: China, Central Asia and India across sixty-two years
tuples.mechanism: a seventeen-year journey undertaken to settle a textual question, which produced the best description we have of its century
tuples.evidence_lens: his own travel account, his biography by a disciple, the translation colophons, and the Indian archaeology it identifies

tuples.episode_object: Ahmad ibn Fadlan, from a secretary to a man who left one extraordinary report
tuples.time_place_scope: Baghdad, the steppe and the Volga across an unknown lifespan
tuples.mechanism: an embassy sent for religious and political reasons, whose incidental ethnography became its only lasting value
tuples.evidence_lens: the report itself, partly preserved in later compilations, checked against the archaeology of the Volga sites

tuples.episode_object: Leif Erikson, from an exiled family's son to a landowner in Greenland
tuples.time_place_scope: Norway, Iceland, Greenland and the north Atlantic across an uncertain lifetime
tuples.mechanism: a voyage that reached a continent and could not be followed up, because the colony behind it was too small to supply it
tuples.evidence_lens: two sagas that disagree, the excavated Newfoundland settlement, and the Greenland farm archaeology

tuples.episode_object: James Cook, from a farm labourer's son to a death on a Hawaiian beach
tuples.time_place_scope: the north Atlantic, the Pacific and the southern ocean across fifty years
tuples.mechanism: systematic charting with an accurate longitude method, which converted a guessed ocean into a mapped one in three voyages
tuples.evidence_lens: his own journals, the ships' logs and charts, the artists' and scientists' records, and the Pacific oral traditions

tuples.episode_object: Abel Tasman, from a company navigator to a merchant in retirement
tuples.time_place_scope: the Dutch East Indies, the southern ocean and the Pacific across roughly fifty-six years
tuples.mechanism: an exploration voyage judged a commercial failure at the time, whose charts nonetheless outlined a continent
tuples.evidence_lens: his own journal, the company's instructions and its verdict on the voyage, and the resulting charts

tuples.episode_object: Mungo Park, from a surgeon's apprentice to a drowning on the Niger
tuples.time_place_scope: Scotland, the Gambia and the upper Niger across thirty-five years
tuples.mechanism: a solo journey financed by a subscription society, whose second, larger expedition failed for exactly that reason
tuples.evidence_lens: his own published account, the society's records, the second expedition's surviving letters, and the local traditions

tuples.episode_object: Alexander von Humboldt, from a mining official to an old man still writing
tuples.time_place_scope: Prussia, the Americas, Russia and Paris across eighty-nine years
tuples.mechanism: the measurement of everything simultaneously, which turned travel writing into a quantitative science of the whole earth
tuples.evidence_lens: his own instruments and notebooks, the published volumes, the enormous correspondence, and the collection records

tuples.episode_object: Jeanne Baret, from a servant to the first woman to circle the globe
tuples.time_place_scope: France, the Atlantic, the Pacific and the Indian Ocean across sixty-seven years
tuples.mechanism: a life conducted in disguise because the ships' regulations forbade her presence, and documented only when the disguise failed
tuples.evidence_lens: the expedition journals that mention her, the pension document granted afterwards, and the botanical collection records

tuples.episode_object: Mary Kingsley, from a housebound daughter to a nurse dead in South Africa
tuples.time_place_scope: England, west Africa and the Congo across thirty-seven years
tuples.mechanism: a self-financed collecting expedition by someone with no institutional backing, whose reports argued against her own government
tuples.evidence_lens: her own books and lectures, the museum specimen registers, and the colonial office correspondence she provoked

tuples.episode_object: Ahmad ibn Majid, from a pilot's son to a name in navigation manuals
tuples.time_place_scope: the Arabian coasts, the Indian Ocean and the routes east across an uncertain lifetime
tuples.mechanism: a navigator who wrote his knowledge down in verse so it could be memorised, which is why it survived at all
tuples.evidence_lens: his own navigational poems and treatises, the Portuguese accounts, and the comparison with later pilot books

tuples.episode_object: Benjamin of Tudela, from a Navarrese traveller to an author of one itinerary
tuples.time_place_scope: Iberia, the Mediterranean, the Levant, Mesopotamia and beyond across an uncertain lifetime
tuples.mechanism: a traveller who counted communities and recorded their trades, which makes his book a census where no census exists
tuples.evidence_lens: the itinerary itself and its manuscript variants, checked against the administrative records of the places he lists

tuples.episode_object: Pytheas of Massalia, from a Greek colonial to a voyage nobody believed
tuples.time_place_scope: the western Mediterranean, the Atlantic coast and the northern seas across an uncertain lifetime
tuples.mechanism: an astronomical voyage north whose observations were dismissed for centuries and turned out to be measurable and right
tuples.evidence_lens: fragments quoted by later hostile writers, the latitude calculations he reported, and the archaeology of the tin routes

coverage_profiles.subject: whole lives, builders, scholars and physicians

tuples.episode_object: Imhotep, from a royal official to a god of medicine two thousand years later
tuples.time_place_scope: the Egyptian royal cemetery and the country across an uncertain lifetime and a very long afterlife
tuples.mechanism: the first named architect, whose deification is a better record of what later ages needed than of what he did
tuples.evidence_lens: his name on a statue base, the step pyramid complex itself, and the much later cult and medical texts

tuples.episode_object: Archimedes, from a Syracusan astronomer's son to a death at a siege
tuples.time_place_scope: Syracuse, Sicily and Alexandria across seventy-five years
tuples.mechanism: mathematics pursued for its own sake by a man remembered for the machines he built when his city was attacked
tuples.evidence_lens: his surviving treatises including one recovered from a scraped manuscript, and the siege accounts of his enemies

tuples.episode_object: Hypatia, from a mathematician's daughter to a killing in a street
tuples.time_place_scope: Alexandria and the eastern Mediterranean across roughly sixty years
tuples.mechanism: a public teacher of mathematics and philosophy in a city where public life had become a religious contest
tuples.evidence_lens: her students' letters, the commentaries attributed to her circle, and the church historians' conflicting accounts

tuples.episode_object: al-Khwarizmi, from a scholar in a library to a name inside two ordinary words
tuples.time_place_scope: Baghdad and the eastern Islamic world across roughly seventy years
tuples.mechanism: the systematic presentation of two borrowed ideas, a positional number system and equation solving, which made both teachable
tuples.evidence_lens: his surviving treatises and their Latin translations, the library's records, and the astronomical tables

tuples.episode_object: Ibn Sina, from a prodigy in Bukhara to a death on campaign with a patron
tuples.time_place_scope: Central Asia and the Iranian plateau across fifty-seven years
tuples.mechanism: a physician whose employment depended on courts that kept falling, so that his books were written between flights
tuples.evidence_lens: his own autobiography continued by a student, the surviving medical and philosophical works, and their translation record

tuples.episode_object: al-Razi, from a musician to a blind old physician
tuples.time_place_scope: Rayy, Baghdad and the Iranian plateau across roughly sixty-nine years
tuples.mechanism: clinical case records kept systematically, which is the difference between a medical tradition and a set of opinions
tuples.evidence_lens: his enormous case compendium, the hospital records, and the citations of him by later physicians

tuples.episode_object: Sinan, from a conscripted boy to an architect of hundreds of buildings
tuples.time_place_scope: the Ottoman empire from the Balkans to the Arab provinces across roughly ninety-eight years
tuples.mechanism: a state architect's office with a standing workforce, which is what allows one career to produce three hundred buildings
tuples.evidence_lens: the buildings themselves and their inscriptions, the endowment deeds, the construction account books, and his dictated memoir

tuples.episode_object: Filippo Brunelleschi, from a goldsmith to the builder of an impossible dome
tuples.time_place_scope: Florence and Rome across sixty-nine years
tuples.mechanism: a construction problem solved by inventing the machinery for it, and a competition system that let an outsider win
tuples.evidence_lens: the cathedral works records and payments, the surviving machinery drawings, and the contemporary biographies

tuples.episode_object: Leonardo da Vinci, from an unschooled boy to an old man with notebooks
tuples.time_place_scope: Florence, Milan, Rome and France across sixty-seven years
tuples.mechanism: a life of unfinished commissions by a man employed for engineering as often as for painting, and paid for both
tuples.evidence_lens: the notebooks in mirror writing, the commission contracts and lawsuits, and the surviving and lost works record

tuples.episode_object: Galileo Galilei, from a musician's son to a man under house arrest
tuples.time_place_scope: Pisa, Padua, Florence and Rome across seventy-seven years
tuples.mechanism: the use of a new instrument to settle an old argument, and the institutional collision that instrument made inevitable
tuples.evidence_lens: his own published works and letters, the trial documents, the surviving telescopes, and the observation notebooks

tuples.episode_object: Zhang Heng, from a provincial student to an imperial astronomer
tuples.time_place_scope: the Han capital and its provinces across sixty-one years
tuples.mechanism: an official astronomer whose instruments were state property, so that science and calendar politics were the same job
tuples.evidence_lens: the standard history's account, the surviving treatises and poems, and the reconstruction of his instruments

tuples.episode_object: Su Song, from an official to the builder of an astronomical clock tower
tuples.time_place_scope: the Song capital and the provinces across seventy-one years
tuples.mechanism: a state clock tower built to fix a calendar dispute, described in a book precisely because it might have to be rebuilt
tuples.evidence_lens: his own illustrated treatise, the court records of the dispute, and the modern reconstructions from that book

tuples.episode_object: Aryabhata, from an unknown youth to a name on a short book
tuples.time_place_scope: the Ganges plain across an uncertain lifetime
tuples.mechanism: an entire astronomy and mathematics compressed into a few hundred verses so it could be memorised and taught
tuples.evidence_lens: the text itself, the commentaries that unpack it, and the later astronomical tables that depend on it

tuples.episode_object: Ibn al-Haytham, from an engineer in Basra to an optician in Cairo
tuples.time_place_scope: Iraq and Egypt across roughly seventy-four years
tuples.mechanism: the replacement of argument by controlled experiment in one field, worked out during years of enforced idleness
tuples.evidence_lens: his optical treatise and its Latin translation, the biographical accounts, and the citations by later opticians

tuples.episode_object: Vitruvius, from a military engineer to the author of one surviving book
tuples.time_place_scope: Italy, Gaul and the Roman provinces across an uncertain lifetime
tuples.mechanism: an obscure engineer whose single book became the only complete ancient architectural treatise, and therefore the rulebook
tuples.evidence_lens: the treatise itself, the buildings that match its prescriptions, and the manuscript rediscovery record

tuples.episode_object: Hildegard of Bingen, from a child given to a convent to an abbess with two monasteries
tuples.time_place_scope: the Rhineland across eighty-one years
tuples.mechanism: a cloistered woman whose visions gave her the standing to write medicine, music and correspondence to popes and emperors
tuples.evidence_lens: her own works and letters, the convent records, the canonisation inquiry, and the surviving musical manuscripts

tuples.episode_object: Paracelsus, from a mining town boy to a wandering physician's death
tuples.time_place_scope: the Alps, Germany and central Europe across forty-seven years
tuples.mechanism: a physician who took his chemistry from miners and metalworkers and was unemployable in every university he entered
tuples.evidence_lens: his own printed and unprinted works, the town council records that dismissed him, and the mining medicine tradition

tuples.episode_object: Andreas Vesalius, from an apothecary's family to a death on a Greek island
tuples.time_place_scope: the Low Countries, Italy, Spain and the Mediterranean across forty-nine years
tuples.mechanism: the decision to dissect personally and publish the illustrations, which made a thousand-year-old textbook checkable
tuples.evidence_lens: his own illustrated anatomy, the university records, the printing house documents, and the court correspondence

tuples.episode_object: Ulugh Beg, from a prince to a murdered astronomer king
tuples.time_place_scope: Central Asia and the Timurid lands across fifty-five years
tuples.mechanism: a ruler who built an observatory and a college and could not hold a throne, which cost him both in one year
tuples.evidence_lens: the star catalogue itself, the observatory excavation, the college records, and the court chronicles

tuples.episode_object: Nicolaus Copernicus, from a canon's ward to a dying man handed his own book
tuples.time_place_scope: Poland, Italy and the Baltic across seventy years
tuples.mechanism: a lifetime of astronomy conducted as a sideline by a cathedral administrator who delayed publication for three decades
tuples.evidence_lens: his own manuscript and the printed book, the chapter records of his day job, and the correspondence with his one advocate

evidence_expectations: Ground each era in the kind of record named by the slot, and describe record types rather than citing any specific title, author, or archive reference.
Prefer documentary and material evidence such as tax registers, charters, inscriptions, coin hoards, excavated levels, canal and road works, and surviving buildings over anecdote.
State uncertainty plainly and calmly where a date, a population, a cause of collapse, or a chain of succession is disputed, and never resolve it with invented detail.
Say who wrote a source and when, especially where the only surviving account of a civilisation was produced by the empire that ended it.
Give the thinly attested centuries of an arc their honest share of the running time rather than skipping to the well-documented ones.
compatibility_rules: Pair only with the sleep history compilation formula; this pack assumes eras of roughly even length inside one continuous arc, with no framing device and no narrative running between episodes.
Use one civilisation or one life per episode and never mix two subjects inside an episode, so that a listener waking in the middle still hears one continuous story.
Draw the twenty slots of a subject in any order, but never reuse a slot within one compilation, since each slot is deliberately a materially different whole story.
This pack is written for two-to-three-and-a-half-hour episodes; a short runtime will force the arc to be cut rather than compressed, which breaks the whole-story promise.
